```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;
using FluentAssertions;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
using Xunit;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tests;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.4: Operator comes from this install's operator list (a principal's <c>sub</c>), from an
/// <c>admin</c>-scoped automation token, or, on compose only, from membership of the dev fallback group.
/// The <c>groups</c> claim yields Operator nowhere else.
/// </summary>
public class OperatorAuthorizationPolicyTests
{
    internal const string ListedSubject = "listed-operator-sub";

    internal static readonly OperatorSubjects ListOnly =
        new(new HashSet<string> { ListedSubject }, GroupFallback: null);

    internal static readonly OperatorSubjects ListAndComposeFallback =
        new(new HashSet<string> { ListedSubject }, GroupFallback: "operators");

    /// <summary>A principal as the JwtBearer handler builds it: one claim per <c>groups</c> element.</summary>
    internal static ClaimsPrincipal Principal(string? sub, string? scope = null, params string[] groups)
    {
        var claims = new List<Claim>();
        if (sub is not null)
            claims.Add(new Claim("sub", sub));
        if (scope is not null)
            claims.Add(new Claim("scope", scope));
        claims.AddRange(groups.Select(g => new Claim("groups", g)));
        return new ClaimsPrincipal(new ClaimsIdentity(claims, "test"));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_SubjectOnTheList_ReturnsTrue()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal(ListedSubject), ListOnly).Should().BeTrue();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_SubjectNotOnTheList_ReturnsFalse()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("someone-else"), ListOnly).Should().BeFalse();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_OperatorsGroupWithoutTheComposeFallback_ReturnsFalse()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("someone-else", null, "operators"), ListOnly)
            .Should().BeFalse("a group membership the orchestrator can write must not yield Operator");
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_ComposeFallbackGroupMember_ReturnsTrue()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("someone-else", null, "operators"), ListAndComposeFallback)
            .Should().BeTrue();
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("some-other-group")]
    [InlineData("non-operators")]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_ComposeFallbackSet_ButNotAMemberOfThatGroup_ReturnsFalse(string group)
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("someone-else", null, group), ListAndComposeFallback)
            .Should().BeFalse();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_AutomationWithAdminScope_ReturnsTrue()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("ak-automation", "openid admin profile"), ListOnly)
            .Should().BeTrue();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_AutomationWithoutAdminScope_ReturnsFalse()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal("ak-automation", "openid profile"), ListOnly)
            .Should().BeFalse();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void IsSatisfiedBy_NoSubNoScopeNoGroups_ReturnsFalse()
    {
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(Principal(null), ListAndComposeFallback).Should().BeFalse();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void FromConfiguration_ReadsTheListAndTheFallback()
    {
        var configuration = new ConfigurationBuilder().AddInMemoryCollection(new Dictionary<string, string?>
        {
            ["Authorization:OperatorSubjects:0"] = "sub-a",
            ["Authorization:OperatorSubjects:1"] = "sub-b",
            ["Authorization:OperatorGroupFallback"] = "operators",
        }).Build();

        var subjects = OperatorSubjects.FromConfiguration(configuration);

        subjects.Subjects.Should().BeEquivalentTo("sub-a", "sub-b");
        subjects.GroupFallback.Should().Be("operators");
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(null)]
    [InlineData("")]
    public void FromConfiguration_NothingSet_IsAnEmptyListAndNoFallback(string? fallback)
    {
        var configuration = new ConfigurationBuilder().AddInMemoryCollection(new Dictionary<string, string?>
        {
            ["Authorization:OperatorGroupFallback"] = fallback,
        }).Build();

        var subjects = OperatorSubjects.FromConfiguration(configuration);

        subjects.Subjects.Should().BeEmpty();
        subjects.GroupFallback.Should().BeNull("an empty setting must not make members of a group named \"\" Operators");
    }
}
```

**3a.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/OperatorSubjects.cs`:
```csharp
namespace Iverson.Api;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.4: who, besides an <c>admin</c>-scoped automation token, is an Operator on this install.
/// <list type="bullet">
/// <item><see cref="Subjects"/>, from <c>Authorization:OperatorSubjects</c>: the <c>sub</c> of each human
/// operator. The chart renders it from <c>global.operatorSubjects</c> as
/// <c>Authorization__OperatorSubjects__N</c>. A <c>sub</c> is Authentik's per-install hash of the user, not
/// predictable from a username, and an Authentik group membership, which the orchestrator can write, no
/// longer yields Operator.</item>
/// <item><see cref="GroupFallback"/>, from <c>Authorization:OperatorGroupFallback</c>: compose's dev-only
/// fallback. Compose's dev operator gets its <c>sub</c> only at first database init, so no static compose
/// list can name it; with the fallback set, members of that group are Operators too. Only
/// <c>docker-compose.yml</c> sets it, the api logs a warning at startup while it is set, and the chart
/// never renders it. An empty setting counts as unset.</item>
/// </list>
/// The policies read it at each decision, as the <c>ConsoleClient</c> policy reads its audience.
/// </summary>
public sealed record OperatorSubjects(IReadOnlySet<string> Subjects, string? GroupFallback)
{
    public static OperatorSubjects FromConfiguration(IConfiguration configuration) => new(
        new HashSet<string>(
            configuration.GetSection("Authorization:OperatorSubjects").Get<string[]>() ?? Array.Empty<string>(),
            StringComparer.Ordinal),
        configuration["Authorization:OperatorGroupFallback"] is { Length: > 0 } group ? group : null);
}
```

**3b.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.cs` with:
```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;

namespace Iverson.Api;

public static class OperatorAuthorizationPolicy
{
    // CSR round 12 §2.4. Three caller shapes satisfy "operator": a human whose `sub` is on this install's
    // operator list; CI/runbook automation via a dedicated `admin` scope (a single space-separated string
    // claim, not an array — confirmed via a real decoded token); and, on compose only, a member of the
    // dev fallback group. The `groups` claim (one Claim per array element) yields Operator nowhere else:
    // the orchestrator can place users in groups, so a group must not be what makes an Operator.
    // Used by the Operator policy, the three hand-written acting-user checks in Program.cs,
    // SchemaAdminAuthorizationPolicy, ConsoleAdminAuthorizationPolicy and /admin/console/roles.
    public static bool IsSatisfiedBy(ClaimsPrincipal principal, OperatorSubjects operatorSubjects)
    {
        if (principal.FindFirst("sub")?.Value is { } sub && operatorSubjects.Subjects.Contains(sub))
            return true;

        if (principal.FindFirst("scope")?.Value is { } scope
            && scope.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).Contains("admin"))
            return true;

        return operatorSubjects.GroupFallback is { } fallbackGroup
            && principal.FindAll("groups").Any(c => c.Value == fallbackGroup);
    }
}
```

**3c.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/SchemaAdminAuthorizationPolicy.cs` with:
```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;

namespace Iverson.Api;

public static class SchemaAdminAuthorizationPolicy
{
    // Operator implies SchemaAdmin (CSR round 12 §2.4): the operator list, the `admin` scope and compose's
    // group fallback all satisfy it, through the one Operator function. Automation that should register
    // schemas without becoming an Operator gets the narrower `schema_admin` scope instead, which would not
    // also grant /admin/dlq and /admin/reconcile.
    public static bool IsSatisfiedBy(ClaimsPrincipal principal, OperatorSubjects operatorSubjects)
    {
        if (OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(principal, operatorSubjects))
            return true;

        return principal.FindFirst("scope")?.Value is { } scope
            && scope.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).Contains("schema_admin");
    }
}
```

```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;

namespace Iverson.Api;

// CSR round 12 §2.2: the console is for admins only. ConsoleAdmin is Operator or TenantAdmin, through the
// same two functions the Operator and TenantAdmin policies use, so the console's /admin/console/roles answer
// and the server's own decisions cannot disagree.
public static class ConsoleAdminAuthorizationPolicy
{
    public static bool IsSatisfiedBy(ClaimsPrincipal principal, OperatorSubjects operatorSubjects) =>
        OperatorAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(principal, operatorSubjects)
        || TenantAdminAuthorizationPolicy.IsSatisfiedBy(principal.FindAll("groups").Select(c => c.Value));
}
```

```csharp
    // ── CSR round 12 §2.4: Operator at the three acting-user sites ─────────────────────────
    // /admin/reconcile, /admin/dlq and /admin/dlq/{id}/replay decide Operator for the ACTING user by

    public static TheoryData<string, string> ActingUserSites() => new()
    {
        { "GET",  "/admin/dlq" },
        { "POST", "/admin/reconcile/SomeType" },

    // The reconcile runs in the worker (CSR round 12 §5.2), which this host does not run, so the request
    // queue answers as the worker does for a type it does not know. The DLQ is the base host's empty fake.
    private HttpClient ClientWithAQueueThatKnowsNoType()
    {
        var requests = Substitute.For<IPrivilegedRequestRepository>();
        requests.GetAsync(Arg.Any<Guid>()).Returns(new PrivilegedRequestRow(
            Guid.Empty, "ReconcileType", "{}", PrivilegedRequestStatus.Failed,
            new Iverson.Api.PrivilegedRequests.PrivilegedRequestResult(
                global::Grpc.Core.StatusCode.NotFound, "No schema registered for 'SomeType'").ToJson()));
        return _factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder => builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
        {
            services.RemoveAll<IPrivilegedRequestRepository>();
            services.AddSingleton(requests);
        })).CreateClient();
    }

    private static HttpRequestMessage ActingUserRequest(string method, string path, string actingSubject, params Claim[] actingClaims)
    {
        var request = new HttpRequestMessage(new HttpMethod(method), path);
        request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer",
            TestJwtFactory.CreateToken("test-service-audience", AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.OperatorSubject));
        request.Headers.Add("x-acting-user-authorization",
            $"Bearer {TestJwtFactory.CreateToken("test-actinguser-audience", actingSubject, extraClaims: actingClaims)}");
        return request;
    }
```

**5k.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api.Tests/AdminConsoleRolesEndpointTests.cs`:
```csharp
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Security.Claims;
using System.Text.Json;
using FluentAssertions;
using Iverson.Api.Tests.Helpers;
using Xunit;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tests;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.2: <c>GET /admin/console/roles</c>, which the console's role guard reads. It answers the
/// caller's roles with the server's own functions, for console tokens only (<c>ConsoleClient</c>), and with
/// no active-tenant filter, because an operator carries no <c>tenant_id</c>. Through the real
/// <c>Program.cs</c> pipeline, whose test host lists <see cref="AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.HumanOperatorSubject"/>.
/// </summary>
public class AdminConsoleRolesEndpointTests : IClassFixture<AuthTestWebApplicationFactory>
{
    private const string Roles = "/admin/console/roles";

    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public AdminConsoleRolesEndpointTests(AuthTestWebApplicationFactory factory)
    {
        _client = factory.CreateClient();
    }

    private static string ConsoleToken(string subject, params Claim[] claims) =>
        TestJwtFactory.CreateToken(AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.ConsoleAudience, subject, extraClaims: claims);

    private async Task<HttpResponseMessage> GetAsync(string? token)
    {
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, Roles);
        if (token is not null)
            request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
        return await _client.SendAsync(request);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task AnonymousRequest_Returns401()
    {
        var response = await GetAsync(token: null);

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task ATokenTheConsoleDidNotIssue_Returns403()
    {
        var token = TestJwtFactory.CreateToken("test-service-audience", AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.HumanOperatorSubject);

        var response = await GetAsync(token);

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.HumanOperatorSubject, null, true, false)]
    [InlineData("console-tenant-admin", "tenant-admins", false, true)]
    [InlineData(AuthTestWebApplicationFactory.HumanOperatorSubject, "tenant-admins", true, true)]
    [InlineData("console-ordinary-user", null, false, false)]
    [InlineData("console-groups-only-operator", "operators", false, false)]
    public async Task AConsoleToken_IsAnsweredWithTheCallersRoles(
        string subject, string? group, bool expectedOperator, bool expectedTenantAdmin)
    {
        var token = group is null ? ConsoleToken(subject) : ConsoleToken(subject, new Claim("groups", group));

        var response = await GetAsync(token);

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK);
        var body = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()).RootElement;
        body.GetProperty("operator").GetBoolean().Should().Be(expectedOperator);
        body.GetProperty("tenantAdmin").GetBoolean().Should().Be(expectedTenantAdmin);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task ACallerWhoseTenantIsNotActive_StillGetsItsRoles()
    {
        // This host's tenant repository knows no tenant, so ActiveTenantEndpointFilter would answer 403.
        var token = ConsoleToken("console-tenant-admin",
            new Claim("groups", "tenant-admins"), new Claim("tenant_id", "tenant_unknown"));

        var response = await GetAsync(token);

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK);
        var body = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()).RootElement;
        body.GetProperty("tenantAdmin").GetBoolean().Should().BeTrue();
    }
}
```

```bash
"""CSR round 12 §2.4 render checks: python3 check_t4.py <overlay> <expected subjects, comma-separated, or -> < render.yaml"""
import sys, yaml
name, expected = sys.argv[1], ([] if sys.argv[2] == "-" else sys.argv[2].split(","))
docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(sys.stdin) if d]
fails = []
def env_of(kind, n):
    d = next((d for d in docs if d["kind"] == kind and d["metadata"]["name"] == n), None)
    return [] if d is None else [e for c in d["spec"]["template"]["spec"]["containers"] for e in c.get("env", [])]
api = env_of("Deployment", "iverson-api")
if not api: fails.append("api Deployment missing")
listed = [e for e in api if e["name"].startswith("Authorization__OperatorSubjects__")]
if [e.get("value") for e in listed] != expected: fails.append(f"api operator subjects {[e.get('value') for e in listed]}, expected {expected}")
if [e["name"] for e in listed] != [f"Authorization__OperatorSubjects__{i}" for i in range(len(expected))]: fails.append(f"api operator subject names {[e['name'] for e in listed]}")
for d in docs:
    if "OperatorGroupFallback" in yaml.safe_dump(d):
        fails.append(f"{d['kind']}/{d['metadata']['name']} names OperatorGroupFallback")
print(f"[{name}] " + ("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL: " + "; ".join(fails)))
T4CHECK
cat > $SCR/t4_render.sh <<'T4RENDER'
```

**11a.** Create the mutation helper (Tasks 5 and 6 reuse it):
```bash
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
cat > $SCR/a2_mutate.py <<'A2MUT'
"""One mutation at a time, never committed.
  python3 a2_mutate.py <file> <n> <old> <new>   replaces the n-th occurrence (1-based) of <old> with <new>,
                                                 keeping a backup beside this script
  python3 a2_mutate.py --restore <file>          puts the backup back"""
import pathlib, shutil, sys
backup = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "a2-mutation-backup"
if sys.argv[1] == "--restore":
    shutil.copyfile(backup, sys.argv[2]); backup.unlink(); print("restored", sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(0)
path, n, old, new = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
text = path.read_text()
if backup.exists(): sys.exit("a previous mutation was not restored: run --restore first")
if text.count(old) < n: sys.exit(f"NOT APPLIED: {text.count(old)} occurrence(s) of the old text in {path}")
shutil.copyfile(path, backup)
at = -1
for _ in range(n): at = text.index(old, at + 1)
path.write_text(text[:at] + new + text[at + len(old):])
print(f"mutated {path} (occurrence {n} of {text.count(old)})")
A2MUT
```

**7b.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/Tenancy/TenantStatusCache.cs` with:
```csharp
using Iverson.Sql;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tenancy;

/// <summary>
/// Caches each tenant's status in this process for <see cref="Ttl"/>.
/// <para>
/// <c>TenantLifecycleGrpcService</c> calls <see cref="Invalidate"/> after every status write, so
/// the replica that served the write sees a suspension, reactivation or deletion immediately.
/// Every api replica, that one included, also learns of it through
/// <see cref="AuthInvalidationListener"/>, which calls <see cref="InvalidateAll"/> on the write's
/// notification, normally within seconds (CSR round 12 §2.3). <see cref="Ttl"/> stays the backstop
/// for a replica whose listener is reconnecting.
/// </para>
/// <para>
/// <see cref="InvalidateAll"/> moves every key to a new generation. A read that started before it
/// stores its result under the old generation's key, which no later read looks up, so a status read
/// before a change is never served after that change's invalidation; the orphaned entries expire with
/// <see cref="Ttl"/>. <see cref="Invalidate"/> drops one tenant's current entry, which a read in flight
/// can still repopulate, bounded by <see cref="Ttl"/>.
/// </para>
/// </summary>
public sealed class TenantStatusCache(
    ITenantRepository tenantRepository,
    IMemoryCache cache) : ITenantStatusCache
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    private long _generation;

    // Prefixed so a raw tenantId can never collide with another consumer's key in the same
    // shared IMemoryCache: /health caches its composite result under "health-composite"
    // (Program.cs), and IMemoryCache.TryGetValue<TItem> returns true with a default value for a
    // cached null, so an un-namespaced tenant key could shadow -- or be shadowed by -- that entry.
    private static string KeyFor(long generation, string tenantId) => $"tenant-status:{generation}:{tenantId}";

    public async Task<string?> GetStatusAsync(string tenantId)
    {
        var key = KeyFor(Interlocked.Read(ref _generation), tenantId);
        if (cache.TryGetValue(key, out string? cachedStatus))
            return cachedStatus;

        var tenant = await tenantRepository.GetAsync(tenantId);
        var status = tenant?.Status;
        cache.Set(key, status, Ttl);
        return status;
    }

    public void Invalidate(string tenantId) => cache.Remove(KeyFor(Interlocked.Read(ref _generation), tenantId));

    public void InvalidateAll() => Interlocked.Increment(ref _generation);
}
```

```csharp
namespace Iverson.Sql.Tests;

public class TokenRevocationRepositoryTests

    // CSR round 12 §2.3: a revocation notifies the api replicas' listeners in its own statement, so the
    // notification is sent exactly when the revocation commits.

    public async Task RevokeAsync_NotifiesTheAuthInvalidationChannel_InTheSameStatement()
```

```csharp
namespace Iverson.Sql;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.3: the channel every api replica LISTENs on (<c>AuthInvalidationListener</c>). Every
/// write to the token-revocation table and to the tenant registry appends one of the clauses below, so it
/// notifies in its own statement: the notification is sent when, and only when, the write commits, and
/// once per row written. The payload is only a hint; a listener drops both of its caches on any
/// notification. <c>pg_notify</c> takes constants only, so the clause needs no privilege beyond the write.
/// </summary>
public static class AuthInvalidation
{
    public const string Channel = "iverson_auth_invalidation";

    internal const string ReturningTokenRevocationNotification = $"RETURNING pg_notify('{Channel}', 'token-revocation')";

    internal const string ReturningTenantStatusNotification = $"RETURNING pg_notify('{Channel}', 'tenant-status')";
}
```

**13c.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api.Tests/Tenancy/AuthInvalidationListenerPostgresIntegrationTests.cs`:
```csharp
using FluentAssertions;
using Iverson.Api.Tenancy;
using Iverson.Sql;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;
using Npgsql;
using Xunit;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tests.Tenancy;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.3 against a real Postgres, with the worker's startup run as Program.cs runs it
/// (<see cref="ApiLoginGrantsPostgresContainerFixture"/>). "This instance" is a listener with its own real
/// caches over the api's login; "another instance" is a second set of repositories on their own
/// connections. The caches' 30 s TTL is the only other way a change could show, so every wait below is
/// far shorter than it.
/// </summary>
[Trait("Category", "Integration")]
[Collection(ContainerCollection.Name)]
public sealed class AuthInvalidationListenerPostgresIntegrationTests(ApiLoginGrantsPostgresContainerFixture fixture)
    : IClassFixture<ApiLoginGrantsPostgresContainerFixture>
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan Soon = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset IssuedBeforeTheTest = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddMinutes(-1);

    /// <summary>The real cache, counting the drops, so a test can wait for the listener.</summary>
    private sealed class CountingTokenRevocationCache(ITokenRevocationCache inner) : ITokenRevocationCache
    {
        private int _invalidations;

        public int Invalidations => Volatile.Read(ref _invalidations);

        public Task<bool> IsRevokedAsync(string sub, DateTimeOffset? issuedAt, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) =>
            inner.IsRevokedAsync(sub, issuedAt, cancellationToken);

        public void Invalidate()
        {
            Interlocked.Increment(ref _invalidations);
            inner.Invalidate();
        }
    }

    private sealed record ThisInstance(
        CountingTokenRevocationCache Revocations,
        TenantStatusCache TenantStatuses,
        AuthInvalidationListener Listener,
        string ApplicationName) : IAsyncDisposable
    {
        public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
        {
            await Listener.StopAsync(CancellationToken.None);
            Listener.Dispose();
        }
    }

    private async Task<ThisInstance> StartThisInstanceAsync()
    {
        var applicationName = "listener-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")[..12];
        var configuration = new ConfigurationBuilder()
            .AddInMemoryCollection(new Dictionary<string, string?>
            {
                ["ConnectionStrings:Postgres"] =
                    new NpgsqlConnectionStringBuilder(fixture.ApiConnectionString) { ApplicationName = applicationName }.ConnectionString
            })
            .Build();
        var revocations = new CountingTokenRevocationCache(
            new TokenRevocationCache(new TokenRevocationRepository(fixture.Api), TimeProvider.System));
        var tenantStatuses = new TenantStatusCache(
            new TenantRepository(TenantSchema.TableName, fixture.Api), new MemoryCache(new MemoryCacheOptions()));
        var listener = new AuthInvalidationListener(
            configuration, revocations, tenantStatuses, NullLogger<AuthInvalidationListener>.Instance);

        await listener.StartAsync(CancellationToken.None);

        (await WaitUntilAsync(() => Task.FromResult(revocations.Invalidations >= 1), Soon))
            .Should().BeTrue("the listener drops both caches once its LISTEN has taken effect");
        return new ThisInstance(revocations, tenantStatuses, listener, applicationName);
    }

    private static async Task<bool> WaitUntilAsync(Func<Task<bool>> condition, TimeSpan timeout)
    {
        var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow + timeout;
        while (DateTime.UtcNow < deadline)
        {
            if (await condition())
                return true;
            await Task.Delay(100);
        }
        return await condition();
    }

    private static string NewSub() => "sub-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");

    private static string NewTenantId() => "tenant_" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")[..12];

    [Fact]
    public async Task ARevocationByAnotherInstance_ReachesThisInstancesCache_WithinSeconds()
    {
        await using var thisInstance = await StartThisInstanceAsync();
        var sub = NewSub();
        (await thisInstance.Revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, IssuedBeforeTheTest)).Should().BeFalse();

        await new TokenRevocationRepository(fixture.Api).RevokeAsync(sub);

        (await WaitUntilAsync(() => thisInstance.Revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, IssuedBeforeTheTest), Soon))
            .Should().BeTrue("the revocation's notification drops this instance's snapshot");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task ATenantStatusWriteByAnotherInstance_ReachesThisInstancesCache_WithinSeconds()
    {
        await using var thisInstance = await StartThisInstanceAsync();
        var tenantId = NewTenantId();
        var anotherInstance = new TenantRepository(TenantSchema.TableName, fixture.Api);
        await anotherInstance.InsertAsync(tenantId, "Listener probe", "active");
        (await WaitUntilAsync(async () => await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId) == "active", Soon))
            .Should().BeTrue();

        (await anotherInstance.UpdateStatusUnlessDeletedAsync(tenantId, "suspended")).Should().BeTrue();

        (await WaitUntilAsync(async () => await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId) == "suspended", Soon))
            .Should().BeTrue("the suspension's notification drops this instance's cached status");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task TheWorkersLegacyTenantSeed_ReachesThisInstancesCachedMiss_WithinSeconds()
    {
        await using var thisInstance = await StartThisInstanceAsync();
        var tenantId = NewTenantId();
        (await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId)).Should().BeNull("an unknown tenant's miss is cached");

        // The worker seeds as the owner (Program.cs's SeedIfMissingAsync loop).
        await new TenantRepository(TenantSchema.TableName, fixture.Owner).SeedIfMissingAsync(tenantId, tenantId, "active");

        (await WaitUntilAsync(async () => await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId) == "active", Soon))
            .Should().BeTrue("the seed's notification drops the cached miss");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task AReconnect_DropsBothCaches()
    {
        await using var thisInstance = await StartThisInstanceAsync();
        var sub = NewSub();
        var tenantId = NewTenantId();
        (await thisInstance.Revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, IssuedBeforeTheTest)).Should().BeFalse();
        (await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId)).Should().BeNull();

        // Written with no notification, as no api write is: only a cache drop shows them before the TTL.
        await fixture.Owner.ExecuteAsync(
            "INSERT INTO iverson_token_revocations (sub, revoked_at) VALUES (@Sub, now())", new { Sub = sub });
        await fixture.Owner.ExecuteAsync(
            $"""INSERT INTO "{TenantSchema.TableName}" ("Id", "DisplayName", "Status", "CreatedAt") VALUES (@Id, @Id, 'active', now())""",
            new { Id = tenantId });
        (await thisInstance.Revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, IssuedBeforeTheTest)).Should().BeFalse("nothing has dropped the snapshot yet");

        await fixture.Owner.ExecuteAsync(
            "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name = @Name",
            new { Name = thisInstance.ApplicationName });

        (await WaitUntilAsync(() => Task.FromResult(thisInstance.Revocations.Invalidations >= 2), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15)))
            .Should().BeTrue("the listener reconnects after 1 s and drops both caches once it is listening again");
        (await thisInstance.Revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, IssuedBeforeTheTest)).Should().BeTrue();
        (await thisInstance.TenantStatuses.GetStatusAsync(tenantId)).Should().Be("active");
    }
}
```

**15a.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/Tenancy/AuthInvalidationListener.cs`:
```csharp
using System.Diagnostics.Metrics;
using Iverson.Sql;
using Npgsql;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tenancy;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.3: makes a revocation or a tenant-status change, written by any api replica or by the
/// worker's legacy-tenant seed, reach this replica's <see cref="ITokenRevocationCache"/> and
/// <see cref="ITenantStatusCache"/> within seconds instead of after their 30 s TTL.
/// <para>
/// One dedicated connection per replica, opened from the replica's own Postgres connection string with
/// <c>Keepalive=30</c> and without pooling, LISTENs on <see cref="AuthInvalidation.Channel"/> and waits
/// with <see cref="NpgsqlConnection.WaitAsync(CancellationToken)"/>. Every notification drops both caches;
/// its payload is only a hint. Every write to either table notifies in its own statement
/// (<see cref="AuthInvalidation"/>).
/// </para>
/// <para>
/// A notification sent while this connection is down is never replayed, so on every connect and reconnect
/// the listener issues <c>LISTEN</c> first and then drops both caches. Reconnects back off from 1 s to
/// 30 s. The TTL stays the backstop, and readiness does not depend on the listener: a lost connection is
/// logged and counted (<c>auth_invalidation.listener_connections_lost</c>), never fatal.
/// </para>
/// </summary>
public sealed class AuthInvalidationListener(
    IConfiguration configuration,
    ITokenRevocationCache tokenRevocationCache,
    ITenantStatusCache tenantStatusCache,
    ILogger<AuthInvalidationListener> logger) : BackgroundService
{
    internal const string MeterName = "Iverson.Api.Tenancy";

    private static readonly Meter Meter = new(MeterName, "1.0.0");

    // Declared after Meter: static field initializers run in source order.
    private static readonly Counter<long> ConnectionsLost = Meter.CreateCounter<long>(
        "auth_invalidation.listener_connections_lost",
        description: "Times this api replica's auth-invalidation listener lost, or could not open, its Postgres connection; its caches refresh on their 30 s TTL until it reconnects");

    private static readonly TimeSpan FirstRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);
    private static readonly TimeSpan MaxRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        var connectionString = ListenerConnectionString(configuration.GetConnectionString("Postgres")!);
        var retryDelay = FirstRetryDelay;
        while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            try
            {
                await using var connection = new NpgsqlConnection(connectionString);
                connection.Notification += (_, _) => InvalidateCaches();
                await connection.OpenAsync(stoppingToken);
                await using (var listen = new NpgsqlCommand($"LISTEN {AuthInvalidation.Channel}", connection))
                    await listen.ExecuteNonQueryAsync(stoppingToken);

                // Whatever was written while this replica was not listening was never delivered to it.
                InvalidateCaches();
                retryDelay = FirstRetryDelay;

                while (true)
                    await connection.WaitAsync(stoppingToken);
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
            {
                return;
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ConnectionsLost.Add(1);
                logger.LogWarning(ex,
                    "The auth-invalidation listener lost its Postgres connection; reconnecting in {RetryDelay}. "
                    + "Until then this replica's revocation and tenant-status caches refresh on their 30 s TTL.",
                    retryDelay);
            }

            try
            {
                await Task.Delay(retryDelay, stoppingToken);
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                return;
            }
            retryDelay = TimeSpan.FromTicks(Math.Min(retryDelay.Ticks * 2, MaxRetryDelay.Ticks));
        }
    }

    /// <summary>The replica's own connection string, with a 30 s keepalive while it waits and no pooling.</summary>
    internal static string ListenerConnectionString(string connectionString) =>
        new NpgsqlConnectionStringBuilder(connectionString) { KeepAlive = 30, Pooling = false }.ConnectionString;

    private void InvalidateCaches()
    {
        tokenRevocationCache.Invalidate();
        tenantStatusCache.InvalidateAll();
    }
}
```

```csharp
    private readonly TenantStatusCache _tenantStatuses;

    public StreamRevalidationInterceptorTests(AuthTestWebApplicationFactory factory)
    {
        _factory = factory;
        _revocationRows.ListAsync().Returns(Enumerable.Empty<(string Sub, DateTimeOffset RevokedAt)>());
        _tenants.GetAsync(TenantId).Returns(Tenant("active"));
        _revocations = new TokenRevocationCache(_revocationRows, TimeProvider.System);
        _tenantStatuses = new TenantStatusCache(_tenants, new MemoryCache(new MemoryCacheOptions()));
    }

    private static TenantRow Tenant(string status) => new(TenantId, "Tenant A", status, DateTime.UtcNow);

    private static ClaimsPrincipal Principal(string sub, string? tenantId = null)
    {
        var claims = new List<Claim>
        {
            new("sub", sub),
            new("iat", IssuedAt.ToUnixTimeSeconds().ToString(), ClaimValueTypes.Integer64)
        };
        if (tenantId is not null)
            claims.Add(new Claim("tenant_id", tenantId));
        return new ClaimsPrincipal(new ClaimsIdentity(claims, "test"));
    }

    private static readonly ClaimsPrincipal Service = Principal("ak-test-service");
    private static readonly ClaimsPrincipal ActingUser = Principal("acting-user-sub", TenantId);

    // The call as ActingUserInterceptor leaves it: the service token on HttpContext.User, the acting user
    // on the request's IActingUserAccessor.
    private static ServerCallContext CallContext(CancellationToken callCancellation)
    {
        var services = new ServiceCollection()
            .AddSingleton<IActingUserAccessor>(new ActingUserAccessor { ActingUser = ActingUser })
            .BuildServiceProvider();
        var context = new TestServerCallContext(callCancellation);
        context.UserState["__HttpContext"] = new DefaultHttpContext { User = Service, RequestServices = services };
        return context;
    }

    private void Revoke(string sub)
    {
        _revocationRows.ListAsync().Returns([(sub, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow)]);
        _revocations.Invalidate();
    }

    private void SetTenantStatus(string status)
    {
        _tenants.GetAsync(TenantId).Returns(Tenant(status));
        _tenantStatuses.Invalidate(TenantId);
    }

    private sealed class RecordingWriter : IServerStreamWriter<string>
    {
        public List<string> Written { get; } = [];
        public List<CancellationToken> TokensSeen { get; } = [];
        public WriteOptions? WriteOptions { get; set; }

        public Task WriteAsync(string message)
        {
            Written.Add(message);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        public Task WriteAsync(string message, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            Written.Add(message);
            TokensSeen.Add(cancellationToken);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }
    }

    private Task StreamAsync(ServerCallContext context, RecordingWriter writer, Func<IServerStreamWriter<string>, Task> rpc) =>
        new StreamRevalidationInterceptor(_revocations, _tenantStatuses)
            .ServerStreamingServerHandler<string, string>("request", writer, context, (_, stream, _) => rpc(stream));

    private static Task WriteAsync(IServerStreamWriter<string> stream, string message, bool twoArgumentForm, CancellationToken token) =>
        twoArgumentForm ? stream.WriteAsync(message, token) : stream.WriteAsync(message);

    [Fact]
    public async Task NothingChanged_BothWriteFormsWriteThrough_PassingTheTokenAndTheWriteOptions()
    {
        using var call = new CancellationTokenSource();
        var writer = new RecordingWriter();
        var options = new WriteOptions(WriteFlags.NoCompress);

        await StreamAsync(CallContext(call.Token), writer, async stream =>
        {
            stream.WriteOptions = options;
            await stream.WriteAsync("one");
            await stream.WriteAsync("two", call.Token);
            stream.WriteOptions.Should().BeSameAs(options);
        });

        writer.Written.Should().Equal("one", "two");
        writer.TokensSeen.Should().Equal(call.Token);
        writer.WriteOptions.Should().BeSameAs(options);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("acting-user-sub", false)]
    [InlineData("acting-user-sub", true)]
    [InlineData("ak-test-service", false)]
    [InlineData("ak-test-service", true)]
    public async Task ARevokedPrincipal_EndsTheStreamUnauthenticated_AtItsNextMessage(string revokedSub, bool twoArgumentForm)
    {
        using var call = new CancellationTokenSource();
        var writer = new RecordingWriter();

        var act = () => StreamAsync(CallContext(call.Token), writer, async stream =>
        {
            await WriteAsync(stream, "one", twoArgumentForm, call.Token);
            Revoke(revokedSub);
            await WriteAsync(stream, "two", twoArgumentForm, call.Token);
        });

        (await act.Should().ThrowAsync<RpcException>()).Which.StatusCode.Should().Be(StatusCode.Unauthenticated);
        writer.Written.Should().Equal("one");
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("suspended", false)]
    [InlineData("suspended", true)]
    [InlineData("deleted", false)]
    [InlineData("deleted", true)]
    public async Task ATenantNoLongerActive_EndsTheStreamPermissionDenied_AtItsNextMessage(string status, bool twoArgumentForm)
    {
        using var call = new CancellationTokenSource();
        var writer = new RecordingWriter();

        var act = () => StreamAsync(CallContext(call.Token), writer, async stream =>
        {
            await WriteAsync(stream, "one", twoArgumentForm, call.Token);
            SetTenantStatus(status);
            await WriteAsync(stream, "two", twoArgumentForm, call.Token);
        });

        var ex = (await act.Should().ThrowAsync<RpcException>()).Which;
        ex.StatusCode.Should().Be(StatusCode.PermissionDenied);
        ex.Status.Detail.Should().Be("Tenant 'tenant-a' is not active.");
        writer.Written.Should().Equal("one");
    }

    [Fact]
    public void TheInterceptor_IsRegisteredAfterActingUserInterceptor()
    {
        var interceptors = _factory.Services.GetRequiredService<IOptions<GrpcServiceOptions>>().Value.Interceptors
            .Select(i => i.Type)
            .ToList();

        interceptors.Should().ContainInOrder(typeof(ActingUserInterceptor), typeof(StreamRevalidationInterceptor));
    }
}
```

**19a.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/Tenancy/TokenRevocationCheck.cs`:
```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tenancy;

/// <summary>
/// The revocation check for one principal. Both JwtBearer schemes run it when a token is validated
/// (<c>Program.RejectRevokedTokenAsync</c>), and <c>StreamRevalidationInterceptor</c> runs it before every
/// streamed message (CSR round 12 §2.3). A principal with no <c>sub</c> is never revoked. <c>iat</c> is
/// read as integer seconds; a token without one is judged by <see cref="ITokenRevocationCache.IsRevokedAsync"/>.
/// </summary>
public static class TokenRevocationCheck
{
    public static Task<bool> IsRevokedAsync(
        ITokenRevocationCache revocations, ClaimsPrincipal principal, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var sub = principal.FindFirst("sub")?.Value;
        if (sub is null)
            return Task.FromResult(false);

        DateTimeOffset? issuedAt = long.TryParse(principal.FindFirst("iat")?.Value, out var iat)
            ? DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(iat)
            : null;
        return revocations.IsRevokedAsync(sub, issuedAt, cancellationToken);
    }
}
```
**19b.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api/Grpc/StreamRevalidationInterceptor.cs`:
```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;
using Grpc.Core;
using Grpc.Core.Interceptors;
using Iverson.Api.Tenancy;

namespace Iverson.Api.Grpc;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §2.3. A server-streaming RPC is authorized once, when it starts, by the JwtBearer schemes
/// and <see cref="ActingUserInterceptor"/>, and can then run for minutes. Before each message, this
/// interceptor checks again, from the in-memory caches, that neither the primary principal's <c>sub</c>
/// nor the acting user's has been revoked, and that the acting user's tenant is still active. A revoked
/// principal ends the stream with <c>Unauthenticated</c>; a suspended, deleted or unknown tenant ends it
/// with <c>PermissionDenied</c> "Tenant '…' is not active.", as the unary paths answer. The caches hear of
/// a change within seconds (<see cref="AuthInvalidationListener"/>).
/// <para>
/// The acting user's tenant is the call's effective tenant: the data plane scopes every read to it
/// (<c>EntityAccess.ForTenant</c>), and <see cref="ActingUserInterceptor"/> checks the same tenant when the
/// call starts. A call without an acting user is re-checked for revocation only, as it was checked at the
/// start. Registered after <see cref="ActingUserInterceptor"/>, which has set the acting user by the time
/// this runs.
/// </para>
/// </summary>
public sealed class StreamRevalidationInterceptor(
    ITokenRevocationCache tokenRevocationCache,
    ITenantStatusCache tenantStatusCache) : Interceptor
{
    public override Task ServerStreamingServerHandler<TRequest, TResponse>(
        TRequest request,
        IServerStreamWriter<TResponse> responseStream,
        ServerCallContext context,
        ServerStreamingServerMethod<TRequest, TResponse> continuation)
    {
        var httpContext = context.GetHttpContext();
        var primary = httpContext.User;
        var actingUser = httpContext.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<IActingUserAccessor>().ActingUser;

        return continuation(
            request,
            new RevalidatingServerStreamWriter<TResponse>(
                responseStream, ct => RecheckAsync(primary, actingUser, ct), context.CancellationToken),
            context);
    }

    private async Task RecheckAsync(ClaimsPrincipal primary, ClaimsPrincipal? actingUser, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        if (await TokenRevocationCheck.IsRevokedAsync(tokenRevocationCache, primary, cancellationToken)
            || (actingUser is not null && await TokenRevocationCheck.IsRevokedAsync(tokenRevocationCache, actingUser, cancellationToken)))
            throw new RpcException(new Status(StatusCode.Unauthenticated, "Token has been revoked."));

        var tenantId = actingUser?.FindFirst("tenant_id")?.Value;
        if (tenantId is not null
            && await tenantStatusCache.GetStatusAsync(tenantId) is null or "suspended" or "deleted")
            throw new RpcException(new Status(StatusCode.PermissionDenied, $"Tenant '{tenantId}' is not active."));
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// The writer a server-streaming RPC writes through under <see cref="StreamRevalidationInterceptor"/>: it
/// re-checks before every message and passes <see cref="WriteOptions"/> through. Both <c>WriteAsync</c>
/// forms are implemented: the interface's default two-argument form throws when the token can be cancelled
/// (Grpc.Core.Api 2.84.0), and the streaming RPCs pass <c>context.CancellationToken</c>.
/// </summary>
internal sealed class RevalidatingServerStreamWriter<T>(
    IServerStreamWriter<T> inner,
    Func<CancellationToken, Task> recheck,
    CancellationToken callCancellation) : IServerStreamWriter<T>
{
    public WriteOptions? WriteOptions
    {
        get => inner.WriteOptions;
        set => inner.WriteOptions = value;
    }

    public async Task WriteAsync(T message)
    {
        await recheck(callCancellation);
        await inner.WriteAsync(message);
    }

    public async Task WriteAsync(T message, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await recheck(cancellationToken);
        await inner.WriteAsync(message, cancellationToken);
    }
}
```

```tsx
import { render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import type { ApiResult } from "../api/client";
import type { ConsoleRolesResponse } from "../api/types";

const useAuthMock = vi.fn();
const fetchRolesMock =
  vi.fn<(token: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<ApiResult<ConsoleRolesResponse>>>();

vi.mock("react-oidc-context", () => ({
  useAuth: () => useAuthMock(),
}));

vi.mock("../api/console", () => ({
  fetchRoles: (token: string, signal: AbortSignal) => fetchRolesMock(token, signal),
}));

import { ConsoleRolesContext, RequireRole, RolesProvider, hasRole, useConsoleRoles } from "./roles";
import type { ConsoleRole, ConsoleRoleState } from "./roles";

const TOKEN = "roles-access-token";

const CHECKING: ConsoleRoleState = { status: "checking" };
const UNAVAILABLE: ConsoleRoleState = {
  status: "unavailable",
  failure: { kind: "failed", status: null, message: "network down" },
};

function ready(operator: boolean, tenantAdmin: boolean): ConsoleRoleState {
  return { status: "ready", roles: { operator, tenantAdmin } };
}

function renderGuard(state: ConsoleRoleState, role: ConsoleRole | "either") {
  return render(
    <ConsoleRolesContext.Provider value={state}>
      <RequireRole role={role}>
        <div>Privileged content</div>
      </RequireRole>
    </ConsoleRolesContext.Provider>
  );
}

/** Renders what the provider publishes, so a test can read it. */
function RoleProbe() {
  const state = useConsoleRoles();
  return (
    <div
      data-testid="role-probe"
      data-status={state.status}
      data-operator={String(hasRole(state, "operator"))}
      data-tenant-admin={String(hasRole(state, "tenantAdmin"))}
    />
  );
}

beforeEach(() => {
  useAuthMock.mockReset();
  fetchRolesMock.mockReset();
});

describe("RequireRole", () => {
  it("renders an Operator page for an operator", () => {
    renderGuard(ready(true, false), "operator");

    expect(screen.getByText("Privileged content")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("require-role-denied")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("refuses a tenant admin an Operator page", () => {
    renderGuard(ready(false, true), "operator");

    expect(screen.queryByText("Privileged content")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
      "Not authorized: this page requires the Operator role."
    );
  });

  it("refuses an operator a tenant-admin page: the two roles answer different questions", () => {
    renderGuard(ready(true, false), "tenantAdmin");

    expect(screen.queryByText("Privileged content")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
      "Not authorized: this page requires the tenant admin role."
    );
  });

  it("admits an operator and a tenant admin alike to a page for either role", () => {
    for (const state of [ready(true, false), ready(false, true)]) {
      const { unmount } = renderGuard(state, "either");
      expect(screen.getByText("Privileged content")).toBeInTheDocument();
      unmount();
    }
  });

  it("refuses a signed-in user with neither role a page for either role", () => {
    renderGuard(ready(false, false), "either");

    expect(screen.queryByText("Privileged content")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
      "Not authorized: the console is for operators and tenant admins."
    );
  });

  it("shows progress, not the page and not a refusal, while the roles are being read", () => {
    renderGuard(CHECKING, "either");

    expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-checking")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText("Privileged content")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("require-role-denied")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("says the roles could not be read when the request failed, rather than refusing", () => {
    renderGuard(UNAVAILABLE, "either");

    expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-unavailable")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText("Privileged content")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("require-role-denied")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

describe("RolesProvider", () => {
  it("reads the roles once with the session's token and publishes them", async () => {
    useAuthMock.mockReturnValue({ user: { access_token: TOKEN } });
    fetchRolesMock.mockResolvedValue({ kind: "ok", status: 200, data: { operator: true, tenantAdmin: false } });

    render(
      <RolesProvider>
        <RoleProbe />
      </RolesProvider>
    );

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-status", "ready"));
    expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-operator", "true");
    expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-tenant-admin", "false");
    expect(fetchRolesMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(fetchRolesMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(TOKEN, expect.anything());
  });

  it("publishes 'checking' and reads nothing before the session has a token", () => {
    useAuthMock.mockReturnValue({ user: undefined });

    render(
      <RolesProvider>
        <RoleProbe />
      </RolesProvider>
    );

    expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-status", "checking");
    expect(fetchRolesMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("publishes 'unavailable' when the roles request fails", async () => {
    useAuthMock.mockReturnValue({ user: { access_token: TOKEN } });
    fetchRolesMock.mockResolvedValue({ kind: "failed", status: null, message: "network down" });

    render(
      <RolesProvider>
        <RoleProbe />
      </RolesProvider>
    );

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-status", "unavailable"));
    expect(screen.getByTestId("role-probe")).toHaveAttribute("data-operator", "false");
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { BrowserRouter } from "react-router";
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { ConsoleRolesContext } from "../auth/roles";
import type { ConsoleRoleState } from "../auth/roles";
import { Sidebar } from "./Sidebar";

function renderSidebar(state: ConsoleRoleState) {
  return render(
    <ConsoleRolesContext.Provider value={state}>
      <BrowserRouter>
        <Sidebar />
      </BrowserRouter>
    </ConsoleRolesContext.Provider>
  );
}

function ready(operator: boolean, tenantAdmin: boolean): ConsoleRoleState {
  return { status: "ready", roles: { operator, tenantAdmin } };
}

const CHECKING: ConsoleRoleState = { status: "checking" };
const UNAVAILABLE: ConsoleRoleState = {
  status: "unavailable",
  failure: { kind: "failed", status: null, message: "network down" },
};

describe("Sidebar", () => {
  it("offers Tenants, and not Tenant Admin, to an operator", () => {
    renderSidebar(ready(true, false));

    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Tenants" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenant Admin" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("offers Tenant Admin, and not Tenants, to a tenant admin", () => {
    renderSidebar(ready(false, true));

    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenants" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Tenant Admin" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("offers both to a caller with both roles", () => {
    renderSidebar(ready(true, true));

    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Tenants" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Tenant Admin" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("offers neither to a signed-in user with neither role", () => {
    renderSidebar(ready(false, false));

    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenants" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenant Admin" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("offers no privileged link while the roles are being read, or when they could not be read", () => {
    for (const state of [CHECKING, UNAVAILABLE]) {
      const { unmount } = renderSidebar(state);
      expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenants" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
      expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Tenant Admin" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
      unmount();
    }
  });

  it("no longer links the removed Performance and Storage pages", () => {
    renderSidebar(ready(true, true));

    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Performance" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Storage" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

**2c.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.AdminUI/src/router.test.tsx` with (the first two `render` calls keep the `future` prop exactly as before, so the type-check count does not move; the new third one omits it):
```tsx
import { render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { RouterProvider } from "react-router/dom";
import { createMemoryRouter, RouterProvider as MemoryRouterProvider } from "react-router";
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import type { ApiResult } from "./api/client";
import type { ConsoleRolesResponse } from "./api/types";

const signinRedirect = vi.fn();
const useAuthMock = vi.fn();
const fetchRolesMock =
  vi.fn<(token: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<ApiResult<ConsoleRolesResponse>>>();

vi.mock("react-oidc-context", () => ({
  useAuth: () => useAuthMock(),
}));

// Each test decides the caller's roles. The landing page's own reads never answer, so its cards stay
// loading and no state update escapes a test.
vi.mock("./api/console", () => ({
  fetchRoles: (token: string, signal: AbortSignal) => fetchRolesMock(token, signal),
  fetchHealth: () => new Promise(() => {}),
  fetchTenants: () => new Promise(() => {}),
  fetchSchema: () => new Promise(() => {}),
  fetchDataVolume: () => new Promise(() => {}),
  fetchMetrics: () => new Promise(() => {}),
  fetchQdrant: () => new Promise(() => {}),
}));

import { router, routes } from "./router";

const TOKEN = "router-access-token";

function signedIn(): void {
  useAuthMock.mockReturnValue({
    isLoading: false,
    isAuthenticated: true,
    user: { access_token: TOKEN, profile: { email: "test@example.com" } },
    signinRedirect,
    signoutRedirect: vi.fn(),
  });
}

function rolesAre(operator: boolean, tenantAdmin: boolean): void {
  fetchRolesMock.mockResolvedValue({ kind: "ok", status: 200, data: { operator, tenantAdmin } });
}

describe("router", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    signinRedirect.mockClear();
    useAuthMock.mockReset();
    fetchRolesMock.mockReset();
    // jsdom's location persists across tests in a file; pin it so the "no redirect" assertion
    // below is about the router's behaviour and not about what an earlier test left behind.
    window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/");
  });

  it("redirects an unauthenticated visitor at the root route instead of rendering the app", () => {
    useAuthMock.mockReturnValue({
      isLoading: false,
      isAuthenticated: false,
      signinRedirect,
    });

    render(<RouterProvider router={router} future={{ v7_startTransition: true }} />);

    expect(signinRedirect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it("renders the landing page at / for an operator, without redirecting away", async () => {
    signedIn();
    rolesAre(true, false);

    render(<RouterProvider router={router} future={{ v7_startTransition: true }} />);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Overview", level: 1 })).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    expect(window.location.pathname).toBe("/");
    expect(screen.getByTestId("widget-tenants")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(fetchRolesMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(TOKEN, expect.anything());
  });

  it("refuses the landing page to a signed-in user with neither console role", async () => {
    // CSR round 12 §2.2: the console is for admins only. The landing page used to render for every
    // signed-in user and degrade card by card.
    signedIn();
    rolesAre(false, false);

    render(<RouterProvider router={router} />);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
        "Not authorized: the console is for operators and tenant admins."
      );
    });
    expect(screen.queryByRole("heading", { name: "Overview", level: 1 })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

/**
 * Reachability, not linkage. `Sidebar.test.tsx` asserts that a caller without a role sees no nav LINK
 * to its page — which says nothing about what happens when the URL is typed, pasted, or bookmarked.
 * These mount the real route table at the privileged path directly.
 *
 * `createMemoryRouter` over the exported `routes` rather than the module's `router`, because
 * `createBrowserRouter` fixes its initial location at import time and cannot be re-pointed.
 */
describe("privileged routes", () => {
  function renderAt(path: string, operator: boolean, tenantAdmin: boolean) {
    signedIn();
    rolesAre(operator, tenantAdmin);
    const memoryRouter = createMemoryRouter(routes, { initialEntries: [path] });
    return render(<MemoryRouterProvider router={memoryRouter} />);
  }

  beforeEach(() => {
    signinRedirect.mockClear();
    useAuthMock.mockReset();
    fetchRolesMock.mockReset();
  });

  it("does not mount /tenants for a tenant admin", async () => {
    renderAt("/tenants", false, true);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
        "Not authorized: this page requires the Operator role."
      );
    });
    expect(screen.queryByText("Coming soon")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("mounts /tenants for an operator", async () => {
    renderAt("/tenants", true, false);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByText("Coming soon")).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("require-role-denied")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("does not mount /tenant-admin for an operator: the two roles answer different questions", async () => {
    renderAt("/tenant-admin", true, false);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByTestId("require-role-denied")).toHaveTextContent(
        "Not authorized: this page requires the tenant admin role."
      );
    });
    expect(screen.queryByText("Coming soon")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("mounts /tenant-admin for a tenant admin", async () => {
    renderAt("/tenant-admin", false, true);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByText("Coming soon")).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
  });

  it("has no /performance or /storage page any more", async () => {
    // An unmatched path ends in React Router's default 404 boundary, which logs; keep the run quiet.
    const consoleError = vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => {});
    const consoleWarn = vi.spyOn(console, "warn").mockImplementation(() => {});
    try {
      for (const path of ["/performance", "/storage"]) {
        const { unmount } = renderAt(path, true, true);
        await waitFor(() => {
          expect(screen.getByText("404 Not Found")).toBeInTheDocument();
        });
        expect(screen.queryByText("Coming soon")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
        unmount();
      }
    } finally {
      consoleError.mockRestore();
      consoleWarn.mockRestore();
    }
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { StrictMode } from "react";
import { render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";

import { ConsoleRolesContext } from "../auth/roles";

  fetchMetrics: (t: string, s: AbortSignal) => fetchMetricsMock(t, s),

}));

  fetchDataVolumeMock,

  fetchQdrantMock,
];

const OPERATOR: ConsoleRoleState = { status: "ready", roles: { operator: true, tenantAdmin: false } };
const TENANT_ADMIN: ConsoleRoleState = { status: "ready", roles: { operator: false, tenantAdmin: true } };

/** Every card's `data-testid`, as an operator sees them. Nine cards over six fetchers — Band B's four share one poll. */
const ALL_CARD_TEST_IDS = [
  "widget-health",
  "widget-tenants",
  "widget-schema",
  "widget-data-volume",
  "widget-fan-out-backlog",
  "widget-consumer-activity",
  "widget-transport-health",
  "widget-embedding-latency",

];

/** The cards a tenant admin is shown: the health strip and the two ConsoleAdmin reads. */
const TENANT_ADMIN_CARD_TEST_IDS = ["widget-health", "widget-schema", "widget-data-volume"];

/** The cards whose endpoints are Operator-gated: tenants, the four metrics cards and Qdrant. */
const OPERATOR_ONLY_CARD_TEST_IDS = ALL_CARD_TEST_IDS.filter((id) => !TENANT_ADMIN_CARD_TEST_IDS.includes(id));

const FORBIDDEN = { kind: "forbidden", status: 403, error: null };

const HEALTHY = {

  status: 200,

function signedIn(accessToken: string | undefined): void {

describe("LandingPage", () => {
  it("renders the four Band A widgets for an operator", async () => {

    expect(screen.getByTestId("widget-schema")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("widget-data-volume")).toBeInTheDocument();

      expect(screen.getByTestId("data-volume-denied-types")).toHaveAttribute(
        "data-hidden-count",
        "1"
      );
    });
  });

  it("threads the session's access token into every widget's fetch", async () => {
    signedIn(TOKEN);
    for (const mock of ALL_MOCKS) mock.mockResolvedValue(FORBIDDEN);

    renderLanding(OPERATOR);

    await waitFor(() => expect(fetchHealthMock).toHaveBeenCalled());
    for (const mock of ALL_MOCKS) {
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(TOKEN, expect.anything());
    }
  });

  it("puts every widget in the waiting-for-session state before a token exists", () => {
    signedIn(undefined);

    renderLanding(OPERATOR);

    for (const testId of ALL_CARD_TEST_IDS) {
      expect(screen.getByTestId(testId)).toHaveAttribute("data-state", "awaitingToken");
    }
    for (const mock of ALL_MOCKS) expect(mock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("renders under StrictMode without any widget stranded on the spinner", async () => {
    signedIn(TOKEN);
    fetchHealthMock.mockResolvedValue(HEALTHY);
    fetchTenantsMock.mockResolvedValue({ kind: "forbidden", status: 403, error: null });
    fetchSchemaMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: { typeCount: 0, types: [], withheldTypeCount: 0 },
    });
    fetchDataVolumeMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: { types: [], deniedTypeCount: 0, unknownTypeCount: 0 },
    });
    fetchMetricsMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: {
        fanOutBacklog: {
          reconciliationQueueDepth: 1,
          dlqUnreplayedCount: 0,
          documentRerenderQueueDepth: 2,
        },
        consumerActivity: { consumerRetriesPerSecond: 0, consumerDlqRoutedPerSecond: 0 },
        rpcHealth: { requestsPerSecond: 1, errorPercentage: 0, p95Seconds: 0.01 },
        embeddingLatency: { p95Seconds: 0.2 },
      },
    });
    fetchQdrantMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: { collectionCount: 0, collections: [], unreadableCollectionCount: 0 },
    });

    renderLanding(OPERATOR, true);

    await waitFor(() => {
      for (const testId of ALL_CARD_TEST_IDS) {
        if (testId === "widget-tenants") continue;
        expect(screen.getByTestId(testId)).toHaveAttribute("data-state", "ready");
      }
      expect(screen.getByTestId("widget-tenants")).toHaveAttribute("data-state", "forbidden");

  it("renders all nine cards for an operator, with Band B's four sharing a single metrics poll", async () => {
    signedIn(TOKEN);
    for (const mock of ALL_MOCKS) mock.mockResolvedValue(FORBIDDEN);
    fetchHealthMock.mockResolvedValue(HEALTHY);

    renderLanding(OPERATOR);

    await waitFor(() => {
      for (const testId of ALL_CARD_TEST_IDS) {
        expect(screen.getByTestId(testId)).toBeInTheDocument();
      }
      expect(screen.getByTestId("widget-transport-health")).toHaveAttribute(
        "data-state",
        "forbidden"
      );
    });
    // Four Band B cards, ONE request. A hook per card would be four requests and thirty-six
    // Prometheus queries every thirty seconds, per open tab.
    expect(fetchMetricsMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it("shows a tenant admin the health strip, schema and data volume only, and never asks for an Operator-only endpoint", async () => {
    // CSR round 12 §2.2: cards by role. A tenant admin is not shown cards that could only answer 403.
    signedIn(TOKEN);
    fetchHealthMock.mockResolvedValue(HEALTHY);
    fetchSchemaMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: { typeCount: 0, types: [], withheldTypeCount: 0 },
    });
    fetchDataVolumeMock.mockResolvedValue({
      kind: "ok",
      status: 200,
      data: { types: [], deniedTypeCount: 0, unknownTypeCount: 0 },
    });

    renderLanding(TENANT_ADMIN);

    await waitFor(() => {
      for (const testId of TENANT_ADMIN_CARD_TEST_IDS) {
        expect(screen.getByTestId(testId)).toHaveAttribute("data-state", "ready");
      }
    });
    for (const testId of OPERATOR_ONLY_CARD_TEST_IDS) {
      expect(screen.queryByTestId(testId)).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    }
    expect(fetchTenantsMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(fetchMetricsMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(fetchQdrantMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

**4c.** Create `Iverson.AdminUI/src/auth/roles.tsx`:
```tsx
import { createContext, useContext } from "react";
import { useAuth } from "react-oidc-context";
import { Alert, Box, CircularProgress } from "@mui/material";
import type { ApiFailure } from "../api/client";
import { fetchRoles } from "../api/console";
import type { ConsoleRolesResponse } from "../api/types";
import { usePolledResource } from "../hooks/usePolledResource";

/**
 * The console's two roles (CSR round 12 §2.2). The console is for admins only: an Operator (on this
 * install's operator list, or an admin-scoped automation token) or a tenant admin.
 *
 * **The server decides, the console renders.** The roles come from `GET /admin/console/roles`, which the
 * server answers with the same functions its `Operator` and `TenantAdmin` policies use. The console no
 * longer reads the token's `groups` claim: an Authentik group no longer makes an Operator, so the claim
 * cannot answer that question. Every route guard and the sidebar read the one answer `RolesProvider`
 * holds, so a hidden nav item and a blocked route can never disagree.
 *
 * **The guards are defence in depth, not the authorization decision.** The server enforces the same
 * roles on every endpoint these pages call.
 */
export type ConsoleRole = "operator" | "tenantAdmin";

export type ConsoleRoleState =
  | { status: "checking" }
  | { status: "ready"; roles: ConsoleRolesResponse }
  | { status: "unavailable"; failure: ApiFailure };

/** "checking" outside a provider, so a component rendered on its own offers nothing privileged. */
export const ConsoleRolesContext = createContext<ConsoleRoleState>({ status: "checking" });

export function useConsoleRoles(): ConsoleRoleState {
  return useContext(ConsoleRolesContext);
}

/**
 * Reads the caller's roles once per session token and publishes them. A failed read is retried with
 * `usePolledResource`'s backoff; the last good answer is kept while a retry runs.
 */
export function RolesProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const auth = useAuth();
  const roles = usePolledResource(fetchRoles, null, auth.user?.access_token);

  const state: ConsoleRoleState =
    roles.data !== null
      ? { status: "ready", roles: roles.data }
      : roles.failure !== null
        ? { status: "unavailable", failure: roles.failure }
        : { status: "checking" };

  return <ConsoleRolesContext.Provider value={state}>{children}</ConsoleRolesContext.Provider>;
}

/** True only for an answer that grants `role` ("either": an Operator or a tenant admin). */
export function hasRole(state: ConsoleRoleState, role: ConsoleRole | "either"): boolean {
  if (state.status !== "ready") {
    return false;
  }

  return role === "either" ? state.roles.operator || state.roles.tenantAdmin : state.roles[role];
}

const DENIED: Record<ConsoleRole | "either", string> = {
  operator: "Not authorized: this page requires the Operator role.",
  tenantAdmin: "Not authorized: this page requires the tenant admin role.",
  either: "Not authorized: the console is for operators and tenant admins.",
};

/**
 * Route guard: renders its children only for a caller who holds `role`, progress while the roles are
 * being read, an error when they could not be read, and a refusal for everyone else. Placed around a
 * route's element in `router.tsx`, one layer inside `AuthGate`, which answers "is anyone signed in?".
 */
export function RequireRole({
  role,
  children,
}: {
  role: ConsoleRole | "either";
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  const state = useConsoleRoles();

  if (state.status === "checking") {
    return (
      <Box sx={{ p: 3 }} data-testid="require-role-checking">
        <CircularProgress aria-label="Checking your console roles" />
      </Box>
    );
  }

  if (state.status === "unavailable") {
    return (
      <Box sx={{ p: 3 }}>
        <Alert severity="error" data-testid="require-role-unavailable">
          Could not read your console roles. The console retries on its own; reload the page to retry now.
        </Alert>
      </Box>
    );
  }

  if (!hasRole(state, role)) {
    return (
      <Box sx={{ p: 3 }}>
        <Alert severity="warning" data-testid="require-role-denied">
          {DENIED[role]}
        </Alert>
      </Box>
    );
  }

  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

**4d.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.AdminUI/src/router.tsx` with:
```tsx
import { createBrowserRouter } from "react-router";
import { AuthGate } from "./auth/AuthProvider";
import { RequireRole, RolesProvider } from "./auth/roles";
import { CallbackPage } from "./auth/CallbackPage";
import { AppLayout } from "./layout/AppLayout";
import { LandingPage } from "./pages/LandingPage";
import { TenantsPage } from "./pages/TenantsPage";
import { TenantAdminPage } from "./pages/TenantAdminPage";

/**
 * The route table, exported separately from `router` so tests can mount it under a memory
 * router at an arbitrary starting path. `createBrowserRouter` fixes its initial location when
 * this module is first imported, which makes "navigate straight to /tenants and see what
 * renders" untestable through `router` itself.
 */
export const routes = [
  { path: "/callback", element: <CallbackPage /> },
  {
    path: "/",
    // RolesProvider reads the caller's console roles once per session token; every guard below and
    // the sidebar render from that one answer.
    element: <AuthGate><RolesProvider><AppLayout /></RolesProvider></AuthGate>,
    children: [
      // CSR round 12 §2.2: the console is for admins only. The landing page admits an Operator or a
      // tenant admin, and shows the cards their roles allow.
      { index: true, element: <RequireRole role="either"><LandingPage /></RequireRole> },
      // Guarded so these pages are UNREACHABLE, not merely unlinked: the sidebar hides the nav item
      // for a caller without the role, but the address bar would still mount the page. The server
      // enforces the same roles on the endpoints behind them.
      {
        path: "tenants",
        element: <RequireRole role="operator"><TenantsPage /></RequireRole>,
      },
      {
        path: "tenant-admin",
        element: <RequireRole role="tenantAdmin"><TenantAdminPage /></RequireRole>,
      },
    ],
  },
];

export const router = createBrowserRouter(routes, {
  basename: import.meta.env.DEV ? "" : "/admin",
});
```

```tsx
import { Link } from "react-router";
import { Drawer, List, ListItemButton, ListItemText } from "@mui/material";
import { hasRole, useConsoleRoles } from "../auth/roles";

export function Sidebar() {
  // The answer every route guard reads (RequireRole), so a hidden nav item and a blocked route can
  // never disagree about who holds which role.
  const roles = useConsoleRoles();

  return (
    <Drawer variant="permanent">
      <List>
        {hasRole(roles, "operator") && (
          <ListItemButton component={Link} to="/tenants">
            <ListItemText primary="Tenants" />
          </ListItemButton>
        )}
        {hasRole(roles, "tenantAdmin") && (
          <ListItemButton component={Link} to="/tenant-admin">
            <ListItemText primary="Tenant Admin" />
          </ListItemButton>
        )}
      </List>
    </Drawer>
  );
}
```

**4f.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.AdminUI/src/pages/LandingPage.tsx` with:
```tsx
import { useAuth } from "react-oidc-context";
import { Box, Typography } from "@mui/material";
import { hasRole, useConsoleRoles } from "../auth/roles";
import { DataVolumeWidget } from "../widgets/DataVolumeWidget";
import { HealthStrip } from "../widgets/HealthStrip";
import { MetricsBand } from "../widgets/MetricsBand";
import { QdrantCollectionsWidget } from "../widgets/QdrantCollectionsWidget";
import { SchemaCatalogWidget } from "../widgets/SchemaCatalogWidget";
import { TenantRosterWidget } from "../widgets/TenantRosterWidget";

/**
 * The console's landing page.
 *
 * The access token is read ONCE here and passed down as a prop. Widgets take it as an
 * argument rather than each calling `useAuth()` themselves: `usePolledResource` already
 * treats the token as an argument for the same reason, and a widget that is a pure function
 * of (token, fetcher) can be render-tested without standing up an OIDC context.
 *
 * `user?.access_token` is `undefined` before the session resolves, which every widget renders
 * as "waiting for session" — the state that must NOT be confused with a spinner, since both
 * `awaitingToken` and `loading` are true at that first mount.
 *
 * **Admins only, cards by role** (CSR round 12 §2.2). The route guard in `router.tsx` admits an
 * Operator or a tenant admin and nobody else. Both see the health strip and the schema and
 * data-volume cards, whose endpoints require `ConsoleAdmin`. Only an Operator sees the tenant
 * roster, the four Band B metrics cards and the Qdrant card, whose endpoints are `Operator`-gated:
 * a tenant admin is not shown cards that could only answer 403.
 *
 * Nine cards for an Operator over six sources: the four Band B metrics cards are all fed by ONE
 * poll of `/admin/console/metrics`, which `MetricsBand` owns — see the note there.
 */
export function LandingPage() {
  const auth = useAuth();
  const accessToken = auth.user?.access_token;
  const operator = hasRole(useConsoleRoles(), "operator");

  return (
    <Box sx={{ p: 3 }}>
      <Typography variant="h5" component="h1" gutterBottom>
        Overview
      </Typography>
      <Box sx={{ mb: 2 }}>
        <HealthStrip accessToken={accessToken} />
      </Box>
      <Box
        sx={{
          display: "grid",
          gap: 2,
          gridTemplateColumns: { xs: "1fr", md: "repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))" },
        }}
      >
        {operator && <TenantRosterWidget accessToken={accessToken} />}
        <SchemaCatalogWidget accessToken={accessToken} />
        <DataVolumeWidget accessToken={accessToken} />
        {operator && <MetricsBand accessToken={accessToken} />}
        {operator && <QdrantCollectionsWidget accessToken={accessToken} />}
      </Box>
    </Box>
  );
}
```
