### Task 15: StarRocks readiness without `OPERATE ON SYSTEM`

**Spec:** §3.5; §6 "StarRocks" (readiness with no grant, Healthy with a backend alive, Unhealthy within the timeout with none, the revoke leaving `iverson_app` without OPERATE). Verified assumptions 45, 71.

**Files:**
- Modify: `Iverson.Server/Iverson.StarRocks/EngagementHealthChecker.cs:50-118`: `AnyBackendReadyAsync` runs `SELECT * FROM TABLE(generate_series(1,2))` through the new `CreateBackendProbe` (5 s `CommandTimeout`), and two rows mean ready. `AnyBackendReady(rows)` and `HasReportedDiskCapacity`, which read `SHOW BACKENDS`, are removed. `CheckHealthAsync`, `ClassifyConnectionException` and the `Healthy`/`AuthPending`/`Unhealthy` mapping are unchanged, and so is `EngagementRepository.CheckBackendAliveAsync` (`:854-860`), the readiness gate's caller.
- Modify: `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/charts/starrocks/templates/job-create-user.yaml:101` (the grant goes), `:107-108` (`REVOKE OPERATE ON SYSTEM FROM USER 'iverson_app'@'%';` after the role revoke, inside the batch that starts with `CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS`), `:113-117` (comment).
- Modify: `Iverson.Server/docker-compose.yml:116` and `:122-123` (the same pair in `starrocks-init`), `:91-94` (comment).
- Test: `Iverson.Server/Iverson.StarRocks.Tests/StarRocksHealthCheckerTests.cs` (the probe's text and timeout); `StarRocksSplitLogins.cs` (the job's statements: no grant, the revoke); `StarRocksCredentialSplitIntegrationTests.cs:157-168` (`AppLogin_HoldsNoOperatePrivilege`; the readiness test's comment); `StarRocksContainerReadinessTests.cs:44-111` (the tests of the removed production members go; the fixture's own `HasReportedDiskCapacity` tests stay); `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api.Tests/StarRocks/StarRocksReadinessIntegrationTests.cs:95-97` (`CheckHealthAsync_BackendStopped_IsUnhealthyWithinTheProbeTimeout`).
- Not changed: `Iverson.Api.Tests/Grpc/RegisterSchemaAuthorizationIntegrationTests.cs:146-175` and `Iverson.StarRocks.Tests/StarRocksIntegrationTests.cs:162` run `SHOW BACKENDS` as **root** to decide when their own test containers are ready; root keeps every privilege, and those fixture gates are not the production check.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing from earlier tasks.
- Produces: the job's batch without the grant and with the revoke. **Task 19** rewrites the job's FE/BE wait (`:87-96`) and quotes this task's batch as it leaves it. `docs/runbooks/csr12-server.md:5, 87` and `integration-test-flake-signatures.md:36-42`, which describe the old grant and readiness, are **Task 24's**.
- `EngagementHealthChecker.BackendProbeSql`, `BackendProbeTimeoutSeconds` and `CreateBackendProbe` are `internal` (the test project has `InternalsVisibleTo`, as `ClassifyConnectionException`'s tests use).

```csharp
        var stopped = DateTime.UtcNow + TimeSpan.FromSeconds(90);
        EngagementHealthStatus status;
        do
        {
            var started = DateTime.UtcNow;
            status = await healthChecker.CheckHealthAsync();
            (DateTime.UtcNow - started).Should().BeLessThan(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10),
                "each check is bounded by the probe's 5 s timeout");
            if (status != EngagementHealthStatus.Unhealthy)
                await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2));
        }
        while (status != EngagementHealthStatus.Unhealthy && DateTime.UtcNow < stopped);

        status.Should().Be(EngagementHealthStatus.Unhealthy);
```

**4a.** The probe:

In `Iverson.Server/Iverson.StarRocks/EngagementHealthChecker.cs`, replace:
```csharp
    /// <summary>
    /// Whether at least one backend is both alive AND reporting real disk capacity. Backs BOTH the
    /// k8s readiness probe above and <c>EngagementRepository</c>'s production
    /// <see cref="StarRocksReadinessGate"/>, so the two can never disagree about what "ready" means.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Alive alone was not enough, and it let both of those open too early.</b> A freshly
    /// started BE registers with the FE and flips <c>Alive</c> to <c>true</c> BEFORE its first disk
    /// heartbeat lands. In that window <c>SHOW BACKENDS</c> reports
    /// <c>AvailCapacity: 1.000 B</c> — observed directly against starrocks/allin1-ubuntu — and the
    /// FE rejects every query that touches table data with "Current available backends: [],
    /// backends without enough disk space: [1000x]". So on a cold start the readiness gate opened
    /// and the first real query failed anyway, and /health reported Healthy while k8s routed
    /// traffic to a pod whose StarRocks queries could not succeed. That signature was recorded
    /// twice during the tenant plan as an undiagnosed test flake; it is a production behaviour.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><b>A genuinely full disk now reports NOT ready, and that is correct.</b> If a backend
    /// really has less than megabyte-scale space, StarRocks itself refuses data queries with that
    /// same error — so reporting Unhealthy is the honest answer, and strictly better than reporting
    /// Healthy while every query fails.</para>
    /// </summary>
    internal static async Task<bool> AnyBackendReadyAsync(MySqlConnection conn, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        await using var cmd = new MySqlCommand("SHOW BACKENDS", conn);
        await using var reader = await cmd.ExecuteReaderAsync(ct);

        var rows = new List<(string Alive, string AvailCapacity)>();
        var aliveOrdinal = -1;
        var availOrdinal = -1;
        while (await reader.ReadAsync(ct))
        {
            if (aliveOrdinal < 0)
            {
                aliveOrdinal = reader.GetOrdinal("Alive");
                availOrdinal = reader.GetOrdinal("AvailCapacity");
            }

            rows.Add((reader.GetString(aliveOrdinal), reader.GetString(availOrdinal)));
        }

        return AnyBackendReady(rows);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The judgement itself, over rows already read — so it is unit-testable without a live
    /// StarRocks. Split out deliberately: a test that only graded
    /// <see cref="HasReportedDiskCapacity"/> would still pass with the capacity check DELETED from
    /// the caller, which is the whole defect being fixed here rather than a hypothetical.
    /// </summary>
    internal static bool AnyBackendReady(IEnumerable<(string Alive, string AvailCapacity)> rows) =>
        rows.Any(r =>
            string.Equals(r.Alive, "true", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && HasReportedDiskCapacity(r.AvailCapacity));

    /// <summary>
    /// True when <paramref name="availCapacity"/> — <c>SHOW BACKENDS</c>' AvailCapacity, which the
    /// FE formats for humans as e.g. "1.000 B" or "907.304 GB" — is at least megabyte scale. The
    /// UNIT is the whole signal: a value still expressed in bytes or kilobytes is the
    /// pre-heartbeat placeholder rather than a reading. Parsed as a unit rather than a number
    /// because the number is meaningless without it.
    ///
    /// <para>Internal so it can be tested directly: the input that matters occurs only inside a
    /// startup window no test can summon on demand.</para>
    /// </summary>
    internal static bool HasReportedDiskCapacity(string availCapacity) =>
        availCapacity.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries) is [_, var unit]
        && (unit.Equals("MB", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            || unit.Equals("GB", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            || unit.Equals("TB", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            || unit.Equals("PB", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
}
```
with:
```csharp
    /// <summary>
    /// CSR round 12 §3.5: the backend probe. A two-row table function runs on a backend, so it returns
    /// both rows only while one is alive, and it needs no privilege: <c>SHOW BACKENDS</c> needed
    /// <c>OPERATE ON SYSTEM</c>, which <c>iverson_app</c> no longer holds. With no backend alive the FE
    /// refuses it at once ("Backend node not found"); the timeout bounds a backend that hangs.
    /// </summary>
    internal const string BackendProbeSql = "SELECT * FROM TABLE(generate_series(1,2))";

    internal const int BackendProbeTimeoutSeconds = 5;

    internal static MySqlCommand CreateBackendProbe(MySqlConnection conn) =>
        new(BackendProbeSql, conn) { CommandTimeout = BackendProbeTimeoutSeconds };

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether a backend answers a query: both of the probe's rows came back. Backs BOTH the k8s
    /// readiness probe above and <c>EngagementRepository</c>'s production
    /// <see cref="StarRocksReadinessGate"/>, so the two can never disagree about what "ready" means.
    /// A failure, the probe's timeout included, throws; the callers count that as not ready.
    ///
    /// <para>It no longer waits for a backend to report megabyte-scale disk capacity, which only
    /// <c>SHOW BACKENDS</c> shows (spec §7): on a cold start a data query can still meet "backends
    /// without enough disk space" in the moments after the probe first succeeds.</para>
    /// </summary>
    internal static async Task<bool> AnyBackendReadyAsync(MySqlConnection conn, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        await using var cmd = CreateBackendProbe(conn);
        await using var reader = await cmd.ExecuteReaderAsync(ct);

        var rows = 0;
        while (await reader.ReadAsync(ct))
            rows++;

        return rows == 2;
    }
}
```

**Spec:** §3.6; §7 "1.35 availability" (the plan confirms each vendor's version table before pinning add-ons). Verified assumption 46.

**Files:**
- Modify: `modules/cluster-aws/variables.tf:13`, `modules/cluster-azure/variables.tf:13`, `modules/cluster-gcp/variables.tf:15`: `kubernetes_version` default `"1.35"`.

EKS publishes no AL2 AMI for 1.33 or later ("Kubernetes version 1.32 is the last version for which Amazon EKS will release AL2 AMIs", EKS user guide, AL2 deprecation FAQ); the AL2023 template's root device is `/dev/xvda` (`amazon-eks-ami`, `templates/al2023/template.pkr.hcl:231`), the device the launch template already encrypts.

Its values keep `autoDiscovery.clusterName`, `awsRegion` and `rbac.serviceAccount.annotations`, which `modules/operators/main.tf:77-106` sets.

```bash
check('$KindMin = [version]"0.33.0"' in open(f"{root}/Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.ps1").read(), "setup.ps1 does not require kind v0.33.0")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs setup.sh in $1 (default: the worktree's) with stub kind, helm and kubectl first on PATH, so nothing reaches a
# cluster: kind v0.24.0 must be refused before any helm or kubectl call; kind v0.33.0 must get past the check (it then
# stops at the stub helm). Prints one PASS or FAIL line per case.
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
S=${1:-$WT/Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh}; B=$SCR/t16-stubs; rm -rf $B
for v in v0.24.0 v0.33.0; do
  mkdir -p $B/$v
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "kind %s go1.25.4 linux/amd64"\n' $v > $B/$v/kind
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "stub helm reached" >&2; exit 97\n' > $B/$v/helm
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "stub kubectl reached" >&2; exit 97\n' > $B/$v/kubectl
  chmod +x $B/$v/*
  out=$(PATH=$B/$v:/usr/bin:/bin bash "$S" 2>&1); rc=$?
  case "$v:$out" in
    v0.24.0:*"kind v0.24.0 is older than v0.33.0"*) [ $rc = 1 ] && ! echo "$out" | command grep -q "stub" && r=PASS || r=FAIL ;;
    v0.33.0:*"stub helm reached"*) echo "$out" | command grep -q "older than" && r=FAIL || r=PASS ;;
    *) r=FAIL ;;
  esac
  echo "[kind $v] $r exit=$rc: $(echo "$out" | head -n 1 | cut -c1-120)"
done
T16KINDSHEOF
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CSR round 12 §4.1: Istio's base, istiod, istio-cni and ztunnel charts, vendored from the release
# tarball because no Helm index or OCI registry carries 1.31.x yet. Move them back to an index once one
# does. modules/operators/main.tf (helm_release) and deploy/kind/setup.sh and setup.ps1 install from the
# four directories this script writes next to itself:
#
#   Source:  https://github.com/istio/istio/releases/download/1.31.2/istio-1.31.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz
#   SHA-256: b3d58081fcffab9456f16b18e990d4dff8fc08b075259bbc0e82b512337a3575
#
# Each directory is the tarball's manifests/charts/<chart> copied unmodified (istio-discovery is
# manifests/charts/istio-control/istio-discovery). Re-running replaces all four.
set -euo pipefail
VERSION=1.31.2
URL="https://github.com/istio/istio/releases/download/${VERSION}/istio-${VERSION}-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
SHA256=b3d58081fcffab9456f16b18e990d4dff8fc08b075259bbc0e82b512337a3575
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
curl -fsSL -o "$WORK/istio.tar.gz" "$URL"
echo "$SHA256  $WORK/istio.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -xzf "$WORK/istio.tar.gz" -C "$WORK" "istio-${VERSION}/manifests/charts"
for chart in base istio-control/istio-discovery istio-cni ztunnel; do
  rm -rf "${HERE:?}/${chart##*/}"
  cp -R "$WORK/istio-${VERSION}/manifests/charts/$chart" "$HERE/${chart##*/}"
done
```

```yaml
# CSR round 12 §4.1: istiod on kind (local and laptop share one install, deploy/kind/setup.sh and
# setup.ps1). The chart's default request (500m / 2048Mi) does not fit the laptop profile's 4-CPU /
# 9 GB host, and the chart sets no limits, so a smaller request reserves less without throttling.
# The autoscaler is off: it scales on CPU as a percentage of the request, so a lower request would add
# replicas instead of reserving less; off, the chart renders replicas: 1 and no HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
# global.proxy.resources sizes the edge gateway's pod (deploy/kind/edge-gateway.yaml), which istiod
# generates from this release's kube-gateway template. Re-measured in the kind run: change these four
# numbers and values-laptop.yaml's capacity comment together.
profile: ambient
autoscaleEnabled: false
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 256Mi
global:
  proxy:
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 64Mi
```

```bash
# CSR round 12 §4.1, §5: the four namespaces are labelled together. An enrolled pod's egress leaves on
# the HBONE port 15008, so a release whose NetworkPolicies do not list 15008 loses every hop once its
# namespace is enrolled. They are labelled when namespace iverson has no NetworkPolicy yet (a fresh
# cluster: the chart brings its 15008 rules with its first install) or when its policies already list
# 15008 (the release was upgraded first). Otherwise nothing is labelled, and the upgrade order applies:
# helm upgrade the release, then run `--only ambient-labels`. Running pods are captured without a restart.
ambient_enroll() {
  local policies ports
  policies="$(kubectl get networkpolicy -n iverson -o name)"
  ports=" $(kubectl get networkpolicy -n iverson -o jsonpath='{..port}') "
  if [ -n "$policies" ] && [ "${ports#* 15008 }" = "$ports" ]; then
    echo "Not enrolled: the NetworkPolicies in namespace iverson do not list port 15008 yet. Run the release's helm upgrade first, then run this script with --only ambient-labels."
    return 0
  fi
  kubectl label namespace iverson cnpg-system kafka starrocks istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient --overwrite
}

phase_ambient_labels() {
  echo "Enrolling iverson, cnpg-system, kafka and starrocks in the ambient mesh..."
```

```powershell
  # namespace is enrolled. They are labelled when namespace iverson has no NetworkPolicy yet (a fresh
  # cluster: the chart brings its 15008 rules with its first install) or when its policies already list
  # 15008 (the release was upgraded first). Otherwise nothing is labelled, and the upgrade order applies:
  # helm upgrade the release, then run `--only ambient-labels`. Running pods are captured without a restart.
  $Policies = kubectl get networkpolicy -n iverson -o name
  $Ports = "$(kubectl get networkpolicy -n iverson -o jsonpath='{..port}')" -split '\s+'
  if ($Policies -and -not ($Ports -contains '15008')) {
    Write-Host "Not enrolled: the NetworkPolicies in namespace iverson do not list port 15008 yet. Run the release's helm upgrade first, then run this script with --only ambient-labels."
  } else {
    kubectl label namespace iverson cnpg-system kafka starrocks istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient --overwrite
  }
}

if ($Only) {
  switch ($Only) {
    "istio" { Install-Istio }
    "operator-namespaces" { Install-OperatorNamespacePolicies }
    "ambient-labels" { Add-AmbientLabels }
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Install and enrol from Terraform (clouds)**

A cloud install is always a fresh one (§5), so Terraform creates the four namespaces labelled, before any release pod exists. The operators' `helm_release`s install into those namespaces instead of creating their own. The Istio releases use the charts' default requests; only GKE sets `global.platform=gke`, which adds the `ResourceQuota` GKE requires for node-critical pods outside `kube-system` (the charts' GKE profile). No toleration override: the ztunnel and istio-cni defaults already tolerate every `NoSchedule` taint (Verified assumption 76).

```hcl
# CSR round 12 §4.1: Istio 1.31.2 ambient (base, istiod, istio-cni, ztunnel), installed from the charts
# vendored under charts/istio (see vendor-istio-charts.sh there for the source tarball and its SHA-256),
# with the charts' default requests. deploy/kind/setup.sh and setup.ps1 install the same four. On GKE,
# global.platform=gke selects the charts' GKE profile, which adds the ResourceQuota GKE requires for
# the node-critical istio-cni and ztunnel pods outside kube-system. The ztunnel and istio-cni default
# tolerations already admit the datastore pools' NoSchedule taints. They install into istio-system,
# kubernetes_namespace.istio_system below, which the operator-namespace policy chart also governs.
locals {
  istio_platform = var.cloud == "gcp" ? ["gke"] : []
}

resource "helm_release" "istio_base" {
  name      = "istio-base"
  chart     = "${path.module}/charts/istio/base"
  namespace = kubernetes_namespace.istio_system.metadata[0].name

  dynamic "set" {
    for_each = local.istio_platform
    content {
      name  = "global.platform"
      value = set.value
    }
  }
}

resource "helm_release" "istiod" {
  name      = "istiod"
  chart     = "${path.module}/charts/istio/istio-discovery"
  namespace = kubernetes_namespace.istio_system.metadata[0].name

  set {
    name  = "profile"
    value = "ambient"
  }
  dynamic "set" {
    for_each = local.istio_platform
    content {
      name  = "global.platform"
      value = set.value
    }
  }

  depends_on = [helm_release.istio_base]
}

resource "helm_release" "istio_cni" {
  name      = "istio-cni"
  chart     = "${path.module}/charts/istio/istio-cni"
  namespace = kubernetes_namespace.istio_system.metadata[0].name

  set {
    name  = "profile"
    value = "ambient"
  }
  dynamic "set" {
    for_each = local.istio_platform
    content {
      name  = "global.platform"
      value = set.value
    }
  }

  depends_on = [helm_release.istiod]
}

resource "helm_release" "ztunnel" {
  name      = "ztunnel"
  chart     = "${path.module}/charts/istio/ztunnel"
  namespace = kubernetes_namespace.istio_system.metadata[0].name

  dynamic "set" {
    for_each = local.istio_platform
    content {
      name  = "global.platform"
      value = set.value
    }
  }

  depends_on = [helm_release.istio_cni]
}
```

`check_t18.py` maps each NetworkPolicy peer to the service-account principal(s) of the pods it selects (an unmapped peer is itself a failure), then requires the `AuthorizationPolicy` selecting each policy's pods to hold exactly one rule per ingress rule: the peers' principals and the rule's ports, with no `to` for a port-less rule. The probe rules have no mirror (kubelet probes arrive SNATed and are not subject to the policy); an `ipBlocks` rule mirrors an edge rule only off the mesh edge.

```bash
# Builds strict JSON schemas, for kubeconform, from the Gateway API v1.6.3 standard CRDs and the vendored
# Istio base chart's CRDs, into $SCR/schemas/<group>_<kind>_<version>.json. Usage: t18_schemas.sh

mkdir -p $SCR/schemas

  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.6.3/standard-install.yaml
python3 -I - $SCR/gateway-api-v1.6.3.yaml $WT/Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/modules/operators/charts/istio/base/files/crd-all.gen.yaml $SCR/schemas <<'T18SCHEMAPY'
import json, sys, yaml
out = sys.argv[-1]
def strict(s):   # an object with declared properties admits no others, as kubeconform -strict expects
    if isinstance(s, dict):
        if s.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in s and "additionalProperties" not in s and not s.get("x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields"):
            s["additionalProperties"] = False
        for k, v in list(s.items()):
            if k == "properties":
                for p in v.values(): strict(p)
            elif isinstance(v, (dict, list)): strict(v)
    elif isinstance(s, list):
        for x in s: strict(x)
n = 0
for f in sys.argv[1:-1]:
    for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(f)):
        if not d or d.get("kind") != "CustomResourceDefinition": continue
        kind, group = d["spec"]["names"]["kind"].lower(), d["spec"]["group"]
        for v in d["spec"]["versions"]:
            sch = (v.get("schema") or {}).get("openAPIV3Schema")
            if not sch: continue
            strict(sch)
            sch.setdefault("properties", {})
            for k in ("apiVersion", "kind"): sch["properties"].setdefault(k, {"type": "string"})
            sch["properties"]["metadata"] = {"type": "object"}
            json.dump(sch, open(f"{out}/{group}_{kind}_{v['name']}.json", "w")); n += 1
print(f"{n} CRD schemas in {out}")
T18SCHEMAPY

cat > $SCR/t18/add15008.py <<'T18PORTS'
"""CSR round 12 §4.2: adds { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 } to every NetworkPolicy `ports:` list in the
files named on the command line that does not list 15008 yet. Handles the two shapes the chart uses: an
inline list on the `ports:` line, and a block list of `- { ... }` items under a bare `ports:` line.
Prints one line per list it changes. Usage: python3 add15008.py <file>..."""
import re, sys
HBONE = "{ protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }"
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    lines = open(path).read().split("\n")
    out, i, changed = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        inline = re.match(r"^(\s*(?:- )?ports: \[)(.*)(\].*)$", line)
        block = re.match(r"^(\s*)ports:\s*$", line)
        if inline:
            if "port: 15008" not in inline.group(2):
                line = f"{inline.group(1)}{inline.group(2)}, {HBONE}{inline.group(3)}"
                changed += 1
            out.append(line); i += 1
        elif block:
            out.append(line); i += 1
            indent, items = None, []
            while i < len(lines):
                item = re.match(r"^(\s*)- \{.*\}\s*(#.*)?$", lines[i])
                if not item or len(item.group(1)) <= len(block.group(1)):
                    break
                indent = item.group(1); items.append(lines[i]); out.append(lines[i]); i += 1
            if items and not any("port: 15008" in x for x in items):
                out.append(f"{indent}- {HBONE}")
                changed += 1
        else:
            out.append(line); i += 1
    open(path, "w").write("\n".join(out))
    print(f"{path}: {changed} port list(s) given 15008")
T18PORTS
cat > $SCR/t18/check_t18.py <<'T18CHECK'
"""CSR round 12 §4.1, §4.2, §4.3 #1 #2 #4 render checks (Task 18): python3 check_t18.py <overlay> < render.yaml"""
import sys, yaml
name = sys.argv[1]
docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(sys.stdin) if d]
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond: fails.append(msg)
REL, NS = "iverson", "iverson"
SA = f"cluster.local/ns/{NS}/sa/{REL}-"
mesh_edge = name in ("values-local", "values-laptop")
GATEWAY = "cluster.local/ns/iverson-edge/sa/edge-istio"
PROBE = "169.254.7.127/32"
kinds = lambda k: [d for d in docs if d["kind"] == k]
nps = {d["metadata"]["name"]: d for d in kinds("NetworkPolicy")}
aps = {d["metadata"]["name"]: d for d in kinds("AuthorizationPolicy")}
pas = {d["metadata"]["name"]: d for d in kinds("PeerAuthentication")}
cidrs = None

def ports_of(rule):
    return [p["port"] for p in rule.get("ports") or []]

# 1. 15008 beside the ports of every ingress and egress rule that lists ports.
for n, np in nps.items():
    for direction in ("ingress", "egress"):
        for i, rule in enumerate(np["spec"].get(direction) or []):
            if rule.get("ports"):
                check({"protocol": "TCP", "port": 15008} in rule["ports"], f"{n} {direction}[{i}] lists ports {ports_of(rule)} without 15008")

# 2. No ingress-nginx peer anywhere; the edge namespace peer exactly where the edge is the mesh gateway.
check("ingress-nginx" not in yaml.safe_dump_all(kinds("NetworkPolicy")), "a NetworkPolicy still names ingress-nginx")
EDGE_RULES = {f"{REL}-api-ingress": [8080, 8081], f"{REL}-admin-ui-ingress": [8080], f"{REL}-authentik-ingress": [9080]}
for n, edge_ports in EDGE_RULES.items():
    if n not in nps: continue
    for port in edge_ports:
        rules = [r for r in nps[n]["spec"]["ingress"] if port in ports_of(r)
                 and not any(p.get("ipBlock", {}).get("cidr") == PROBE for p in r.get("from", []))]
        check(len(rules) == 1, f"{n}: {len(rules)} edge rules for {port}")
        if len(rules) != 1: continue
        has_edge = any(p.get("namespaceSelector", {}).get("matchLabels", {}).get("kubernetes.io/metadata.name") == "iverson-edge" for p in rules[0]["from"])
        check(has_edge == mesh_edge, f"{n} {port}: iverson-edge peer {'missing' if mesh_edge else 'present off kind'}")
        blocks = [p["ipBlock"]["cidr"] for p in rules[0]["from"] if "ipBlock" in p]
        check(bool(blocks), f"{n} {port}: edge rule has no ipBlock peers")
        cidrs = cidrs or blocks
        check(blocks == cidrs, f"{n} {port}: edge ranges {blocks} differ from {cidrs}")

# 3. Kubelet probe allows, per probed workload: 169.254.7.127/32 on its probe ports.
PROBES = {"api-ingress": [8081], "worker-ingress": [8081], "postgres-ingress": [8000], "starrocks-ingress": [8030, 8040],
          "qdrant-ingress": [6333], "tei-ingress": [8080], "ollama-ingress": [11434], "admin-ui-ingress": [8080],
          "jaeger-ingress": [14269], "prometheus-ingress": [9090], "authentik-ingress": [9000, 9080]}
for short, want in PROBES.items():
    n = f"{REL}-{short}"
    if n not in nps: continue
    got = [ports_of(r) for r in nps[n]["spec"]["ingress"] if r.get("from") == [{"ipBlock": {"cidr": PROBE}}]]
    check(got == [want + [15008]], f"{n}: probe rules {got}, want [{want + [15008]}]")

# 4. Postgres: the CNPG operator on 8000 and 5432, and the instances themselves port-less (§4.3 #1, #4).
pg = nps[f"{REL}-postgres-ingress"]["spec"]["ingress"]
check({"from": [{"namespaceSelector": {"matchLabels": {"kubernetes.io/metadata.name": "cnpg-system"}},
                 "podSelector": {"matchLabels": {"app.kubernetes.io/name": "cloudnative-pg"}}}],
       "ports": [{"protocol": "TCP", "port": 8000}, {"protocol": "TCP", "port": 5432}, {"protocol": "TCP", "port": 15008}]} in pg,
      "postgres-ingress does not admit the CNPG operator on 8000/5432")
check({"from": [{"podSelector": {"matchLabels": {"cnpg.io/cluster": f"{REL}-postgres"}}}]} in pg, "postgres-ingress does not admit its own instances")

# 5. The AuthorizationPolicy mirror: per NetworkPolicy ingress rule, the peers' principals and the rule's ports.
def principals(peer):
    ns = peer.get("namespaceSelector", {}).get("matchLabels", {}).get("kubernetes.io/metadata.name")
    pod = peer.get("podSelector", {})
    ml = pod.get("matchLabels", {})
    if ns == "iverson-edge" and not pod: return [GATEWAY]
    if ns == "cnpg-system" and ml == {"app.kubernetes.io/name": "cloudnative-pg"}: return ["cluster.local/ns/cnpg-system/sa/cnpg-cloudnative-pg"]
    if ns == "kafka" and ml == {"strimzi.io/kind": "cluster-operator"}: return ["cluster.local/ns/kafka/sa/strimzi-cluster-operator"]
    if ns is not None or "namespaceSelector" in peer: return None
    if ml.get("app", "").startswith(f"{REL}-authentik-"): return [SA + "authentik"]
    if "app" in ml: return [SA + ml["app"][len(REL) + 1:]]
    if "job-name" in ml: return [SA + ml["job-name"][len(REL) + 1:]]
    if ml == {"cnpg.io/cluster": f"{REL}-postgres"}: return [SA + "postgres"]
    if ml == {"strimzi.io/cluster": f"{REL}-kafka"}: return [SA + "kafka-kafka", SA + "kafka-entity-operator"]
    for e in pod.get("matchExpressions", []):
        if e["key"] == "app.starrocks.ownerreference/name": return [SA + v[len(REL) + 1:] for v in e["values"]]
    return None

def selectors(np):
    sel = np["spec"]["podSelector"]
    if "matchLabels" in sel: return [sel["matchLabels"]]
    return [{e["key"]: v} for e in sel["matchExpressions"] for v in e["values"]]

def ap_rules(ap):
    out = []
    for r in ap["spec"].get("rules", []):
        src = r["from"][0]["source"]
        ports = sorted(int(p) for p in r.get("to", [{}])[0].get("operation", {}).get("ports", [])) if r.get("to") else None
        out.append((tuple(sorted(src.get("principals", []))), tuple(src.get("ipBlocks", [])), tuple(ports) if ports else None))
    return sorted(out, key=str)

covered = set()
for n, np in nps.items():
    if not np["spec"].get("ingress"): continue   # egress-only, or the default-deny
    want = []
    for rule in np["spec"].get("ingress", []):
        peers = rule.get("from", [])
        if peers == [{"ipBlock": {"cidr": PROBE}}]: continue
        ports = tuple(sorted(p for p in ports_of(rule) if p != 15008)) or None
        prins = []
        for peer in peers:
            if "ipBlock" in peer: continue
            p = principals(peer)
            check(p is not None, f"{n}: no principal mapping for peer {peer}")
            prins += p or []
        if prins:
            want.append((tuple(sorted(set(prins))), (), ports))
        if any("ipBlock" in p for p in peers) and not mesh_edge:
            want.append(((), tuple(p["ipBlock"]["cidr"] for p in peers if "ipBlock" in p), ports))
    for sel in selectors(np):
        match = [a for a in aps.values() if a["spec"]["selector"]["matchLabels"] == sel]
        check(len(match) == 1, f"{n}: {len(match)} AuthorizationPolicies select {sel}")
        if len(match) != 1: continue
        ap = match[0]; covered.add(ap["metadata"]["name"])
        check(ap["spec"].get("action") == "ALLOW" and ap["apiVersion"] == "security.istio.io/v1", f"{ap['metadata']['name']}: not an ALLOW security.istio.io/v1 policy")
        check(ap_rules(ap) == sorted(want, key=str), f"{ap['metadata']['name']} mirrors {sel} wrongly:\n      got  {ap_rules(ap)}\n      want {sorted(want, key=str)}")
        check("notPrincipals" not in str(ap), f"{ap['metadata']['name']} uses notPrincipals")
check(covered == set(aps), f"AuthorizationPolicies mirroring no NetworkPolicy: {sorted(set(aps) - covered)}")

# 6. PeerAuthentication: one per workload, STRICT; PERMISSIVE only on the edge ports off the mesh edge.
EDGE_PA = {f"{REL}-api": {8080, 8081}, f"{REL}-admin-ui": {8080}, f"{REL}-authentik-server": {9080}}
for a in aps.values():
    sel = a["spec"]["selector"]["matchLabels"]
    check(any(p["spec"]["selector"]["matchLabels"] == sel for p in pas.values()), f"no PeerAuthentication selects {sel}")
check(any(p["spec"]["selector"]["matchLabels"] == {"app": f"{REL}-authentik-worker"} for p in pas.values()), "no PeerAuthentication for the Authentik worker")
for n, pa in pas.items():
    check(pa["spec"]["mtls"] == {"mode": "STRICT"}, f"{n} is not STRICT")
    got = {int(k) for k, v in (pa["spec"].get("portLevelMtls") or {}).items() if v == {"mode": "PERMISSIVE"}}
    want = set() if mesh_edge else EDGE_PA.get(n, set())
    check(got == want and len(pa["spec"].get("portLevelMtls") or {}) == len(got), f"{n} PERMISSIVE ports {sorted(got)}, want {sorted(want)}")

# 7. StarRocks FE and BE run under service accounts of their own (laptop renders no StarRocks).
src = [d for d in kinds("StarRocksCluster")]
if src:
    spec = src[0]["spec"]
    check(spec["starRocksFeSpec"].get("serviceAccount") == f"{REL}-starrocks-fe", "FE serviceAccount wrong")
    check(spec["starRocksBeSpec"].get("serviceAccount") == f"{REL}-starrocks-be", "BE serviceAccount wrong")
    sas = {d["metadata"]["name"]: d for d in kinds("ServiceAccount")}
    for s in ("fe", "be"):
        check(sas.get(f"{REL}-starrocks-{s}", {}).get("automountServiceAccountToken") is False, f"ServiceAccount {REL}-starrocks-{s} missing or mounts a token")

# 8. §4.3 #2: the Postgres Cluster renders nodeSelector and tolerations only when non-empty.
cl = kinds("Cluster")[0]["spec"]
check(("affinity" in cl) == (name not in ("values-local", "values-laptop")), f"Cluster affinity rendered: {'affinity' in cl}")
check(all(cl["affinity"].get(k) for k in cl["affinity"]) if cl.get("affinity") else True, f"Cluster affinity renders an empty field: {cl.get('affinity')}")

print(f"[{name}] {'PASS' if not fails else 'FAIL'}", *fails, sep="\n  ")
sys.exit(bool(fails))
T18CHECK
cat > $SCR/t18/t18_mutate.sh <<'T18MUT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Task 18's mutation proof, on a copy of the chart under $SCR/t18-mut (never the worktree). Each mutation
# replaces exactly one occurrence of one line in one copied file, renders values-local and values-gcp, runs
# check_t18.py on both, and restores the copy.
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
M=$SCR/t18-mut; rm -rf $M; mkdir -p $M; cp -r $WT/Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson $M/
CH=$M/iverson
mutate() {  # file, old, new: exactly one occurrence, else the mutation is reported as not applied
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "$3" > $M/tmp <<'T18PY'
import sys
s = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
if s.count(sys.argv[2]) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"mutation not applied: {s.count(sys.argv[2])} occurrences in {sys.argv[1]}")
print(s.replace(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]), end="")
T18PY
  local rc=$?; [ $rc = 0 ] && cp "$1" $M/orig && mv $M/tmp "$1"; return $rc
}
restore() { mv $M/orig "$1"; }
check() {
  bash $SCR/t18/t18_render.sh mut $CH values-local values-gcp
  for v in values-local values-gcp; do python3 -I $SCR/t18/check_t18.py $v < $SCR/r/mut-$v.yaml | head -4 | sed 's/^/    /'; done
}
run() { echo "$1"; if mutate "$2" "$3" "$4"; then check; restore "$2"; fi; }
NP=$CH/templates/networkpolicies.yaml; MP=$CH/templates/mesh-policies.yaml
run M1 $NP '      ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 8000 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 5432 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }]' '      ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 5432 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }]'
run M2 $NP '    - from: [{ podSelector: { matchLabels: { cnpg.io/cluster: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres } } }]' '    - from: [{ podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-api } } }]'
run M3 $MP '    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}kafka-kafka", "{{ $sa }}kafka-entity-operator"] } }]' '    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}kafka-kafka"] } }]'
run M4 $MP '  {{- if and .edgePorts (not $meshEdge) }}' '  {{- if .edgePorts }}'
run M5 $CH/charts/postgres/templates/cluster.yaml '  {{- if or .Values.nodeSelector .Values.tolerations }}' '  {{- if true }}'
run M6 $CH/charts/starrocks/templates/starrockscluster.yaml '    serviceAccount: {{ .Release.Name }}-starrocks-fe' '    serviceAccount: default'
run M7 $NP '      ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 6333 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }]' '      ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 6334 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }]'
run M8 $CH/templates/_helpers.tpl '  ports: [{ protocol: UDP, port: 53 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 53 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 15008 }]' '  ports: [{ protocol: UDP, port: 53 }, { protocol: TCP, port: 53 }]'
run M9 $NP '{{- $meshEdge := eq (include "iverson.meshEdge" .) "true" }}' '{{- $meshEdge := false }}'
T18MUT
ls $SCR/t18 | wc -l
```

- [ ] **Step 4: NetworkPolicy rules: the edge peer, the probes, the operator and the instances**

**4a.** In `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/templates/networkpolicies.yaml`, replace (the comment as Task 13 leaves it):

```yaml
{{- /*
CSR round-11 #18: the ingress-nginx namespace is admitted only where the Ingress fronting the
port is served by ingress-nginx (className "nginx"); every other class reaches the pod from
clusterCidrs alone. Each rule is gated on the className of the Ingress that targets its port:
API 8080 by api.ingress, API 8081 by api.adminApiIngress, admin-ui 8080 by adminUi.ingress,
Authentik 9080 by authentik.ingress (Prometheus's 8082 rule has no Ingress and no class). A
rule's `from` list never becomes empty: clusterCidrs is non-empty (refused above otherwise), so
dropping the namespace peer narrows the rule instead of turning it into an allow-all.
*/}}
{{- $nginxApi := eq (dig "ingress" "className" "" (default dict .Values.api)) "nginx" }}
{{- $nginxAdminApi := eq (dig "adminApiIngress" "className" "" (default dict .Values.api)) "nginx" }}
{{- $nginxAdminUi := eq (dig "ingress" "className" "" (default dict .Values.adminUi)) "nginx" }}
{{- $nginxAuthentik := eq (dig "ingress" "className" "" (default dict .Values.authentik)) "nginx" }}
```

with:

```yaml
{{- /*
CSR round 12 §4.2. Where the edge is the Istio gateway (global.gateway.class istio: kind and laptop),
its namespace is admitted on the edge ports (API 8080 and 8081, admin-ui 8080, Authentik 9080); every
other profile reaches those ports from clusterCidrs alone. A rule's `from` list never becomes empty:
clusterCidrs is non-empty (refused above otherwise).

Every rule that lists ports also lists 15008, to the same peers: in the ambient mesh an enrolled
pod's traffic travels as HBONE to <destination>:15008, so both the sender's egress and the receiver's
ingress see that port. Inside the mesh NetworkPolicy therefore keeps pod-pair scoping but not port
scoping; templates/mesh-policies.yaml restores port scoping with an AuthorizationPolicy per workload
that mirrors the ingress rules here, so a peer added or a port changed here is changed there too.

Every probed pod's ingress admits 169.254.7.127/32, the address istio-cni gives kubelet probes, on
its probe ports. Calico's iptables dataplane admits probes without it (they are filtered before the
SNAT), but Istio asks for it wherever NetworkPolicy is enforced, and the cloud CNIs are untested.
*/}}
{{- $meshEdge := eq (include "iverson.meshEdge" .) "true" }}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: The mesh policies**

Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/templates/mesh-policies.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- /*
CSR round 12 §4.1, §4.2: Istio ambient's policies for the release's workloads.

PeerAuthentication, one per workload (ztunnel honours port-level settings only on a policy with a
workload selector): mutual TLS is STRICT. Only the ports the edge reaches from outside the mesh are
PERMISSIVE, which is none where the edge is the Istio gateway (a mesh client) and, elsewhere, the API's
8080 and 8081, Authentik's public listener 9080 and admin-ui's 8080.

AuthorizationPolicy (ALLOW, enforced by ztunnel), one per workload with NetworkPolicy ingress rules: it
mirrors those rules (templates/networkpolicies.yaml), because inside the mesh NetworkPolicy sees only
the HBONE port 15008 and ztunnel forwards to whatever port the sender asked for. Each rule names its
peers by service account (cluster.local/ns/<namespace>/sa/<account>) and lists that rule's ports; a
port-less NetworkPolicy rule mirrors as a rule with no `to`. Once a workload has an ALLOW policy,
ztunnel refuses every connection no rule admits. Kubelet probes arrive SNATed and are not subject to
it, so the probe rules have no mirror. A PERMISSIVE edge port gets one more rule, from the address
ranges its NetworkPolicy edge rule admits (`ipBlocks`), because a principals-only rule refuses
plaintext from outside the mesh. `notPrincipals` is never used: it also matches a connection that
carries no identity, so it would admit every plaintext caller.

The AuthorizationPolicies render with the NetworkPolicies they mirror (networkPolicy.enabled, which
also validates clusterCidrs); the PeerAuthentications always render.
*/}}
{{- $sa := printf "cluster.local/ns/%s/sa/%s-" .Release.Namespace .Release.Name }}
{{- $meshEdge := eq (include "iverson.meshEdge" .) "true" }}
{{- $edge := include "iverson.edgeGatewayPrincipal" . }}
{{- $edgeRanges := concat .Values.networkPolicy.clusterCidrs (default (list) .Values.networkPolicy.nodeSubnetFallback) }}
{{- /* name, selector label, selector value, the ports the edge reaches (cloud PERMISSIVE), whether it renders */}}
{{- $workloads := list
  (dict "name" "api" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-api" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list 8080 8081) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "worker" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-worker" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "postgres" "key" "cnpg.io/cluster" "value" (printf "%s-postgres" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "kafka" "key" "strimzi.io/cluster" "value" (printf "%s-kafka" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "starrocks-fe" "key" "app.starrocks.ownerreference/name" "value" (printf "%s-starrocks-fe" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "starrocks-be" "key" "app.starrocks.ownerreference/name" "value" (printf "%s-starrocks-be" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "qdrant" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-qdrant" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "tei" "key" "iverson.io/component" "value" "tei" "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "ollama" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-ollama" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "admin-ui" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-admin-ui" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list 8080) "on" .Values.adminUi.enabled)
  (dict "name" "jaeger" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-jaeger" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" .Values.global.tracingEnabled)
  (dict "name" "prometheus" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-prometheus" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" .Values.global.prometheusEnabled)
  (dict "name" "authentik-server" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-authentik-server" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list 9080) "on" true)
  (dict "name" "authentik-worker" "key" "app" "value" (printf "%s-authentik-worker" .Release.Name) "edgePorts" (list) "on" true)
}}
{{- range $workloads }}
{{- if .on }}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: {{ $.Release.Name }}-{{ .name }}
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { {{ .key }}: {{ .value }} }
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
  {{- if and .edgePorts (not $meshEdge) }}
  portLevelMtls:
    {{- range .edgePorts }}
    {{ . }}:
      mode: PERMISSIVE
    {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- if .Values.networkPolicy.enabled }}
---
# api: the edge on 8080 (gRPC) and 8081 (/admin, /health, /v1/traces); Prometheus on 8082.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-api }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    {{- range list "8080" "8081" }}
    {{- if $meshEdge }}
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $edge }}"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["{{ . }}"] } }]
    {{- else }}
    - from: [{ source: { ipBlocks: {{ toJson $edgeRanges }} } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["{{ . }}"] } }]
    {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}prometheus"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8082"] } }]
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-worker
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-worker }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}prometheus"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8082"] } }]
---
# Postgres: the app logins on 5432, the CNPG operator on 8000 and 5432, and the instances themselves on
# every port (streaming replication, cloning and each other's status port).
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { cnpg.io/cluster: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker", "{{ $sa }}authentik", "{{ $sa }}authentik-revoke-cross-db"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["5432"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["cluster.local/ns/cnpg-system/sa/cnpg-cloudnative-pg"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8000", "5432"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}postgres"] } }]
---
# Kafka (brokers and the entity operator): the api and worker on 9093, the cluster's own pods on every
# port, and the Strimzi cluster operator on 9090, 9091 and 8443.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-kafka
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { strimzi.io/cluster: {{ .Release.Name }}-kafka }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9093"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}kafka-kafka", "{{ $sa }}kafka-entity-operator"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["cluster.local/ns/kafka/sa/strimzi-cluster-operator"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9090", "9091", "8443"] } }]
{{- range list "fe" "be" }}
---
# StarRocks {{ upper . }}: the api, worker and create-user Job on 9030, and the FE and BE on every port.
# One policy each: a selector takes matchLabels only.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ $.Release.Name }}-starrocks-{{ . }}
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app.starrocks.ownerreference/name: {{ $.Release.Name }}-starrocks-{{ . }} }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker", "{{ $sa }}starrocks-create-user"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9030"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}starrocks-fe", "{{ $sa }}starrocks-be"] } }]
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-qdrant
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-qdrant }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["6334"] } }]
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}qdrant"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["6335"] } }]
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-tei
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { iverson.io/component: tei }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8080"] } }]
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-ollama
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-ollama }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["11434"] } }]
{{- if .Values.adminUi.enabled }}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    {{- if $meshEdge }}
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $edge }}"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8080"] } }]
    {{- else }}
    - from: [{ source: { ipBlocks: {{ toJson $edgeRanges }} } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8080"] } }]
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- if .Values.global.tracingEnabled }}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-jaeger
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-jaeger }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api", "{{ $sa }}worker"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["4317", "4318"] } }]
{{- end }}
{{- if .Values.global.prometheusEnabled }}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-prometheus }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9090"] } }]
{{- end }}
---
# Authentik server: the api on the tls-proxy's 8443, and the edge on the public listener 9080.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik-server
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik-server }
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $sa }}api"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["8443"] } }]
    {{- if $meshEdge }}
    - from: [{ source: { principals: ["{{ $edge }}"] } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9080"] } }]
    {{- else }}
    - from: [{ source: { ipBlocks: {{ toJson $edgeRanges }} } }]
      to: [{ operation: { ports: ["9080"] } }]
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: The CNPG operator's PeerAuthentication (Task 14's chart)**

**8a.** Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/modules/operators/charts/operator-namespace-policies/templates/peerauthentication-cnpg.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- /*
CSR round 12 §4.1: the CNPG operator's mutual TLS, the shape the release chart gives its own workloads
(templates/mesh-policies.yaml there): STRICT, selector-scoped, because ztunnel honours a port-level
setting only on a policy with a workload selector. On the cloud profiles (cnpgWebhookPermissive, which
modules/operators sets) the webhook port 9443 is PERMISSIVE: the API server that calls it runs off-node,
outside the mesh. On kind the API server is host-network and istio-cni lets node-originated connections
bypass ztunnel, so nothing is PERMISSIVE there.
*/}}
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: cnpg-operator
  namespace: cnpg-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: cloudnative-pg }
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
  {{- if .Values.cnpgWebhookPermissive }}
  portLevelMtls:
    9443:
      mode: PERMISSIVE
  {{- end }}
```

`cnpgWebhookPermissive` has no default in the chart's `values.yaml`: unset, it renders STRICT only, which is kind's case. `setup.sh` and `setup.ps1` need no change.

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tests.Helpers;

// The two hosts behind HstsPipelineTests.cs, built the way AdminConsoleCorsTestWebApplicationFactories.cs
// builds its siblings: Program.cs reads Hsts:Enabled before builder.Build(), too early for
// ConfigureWebHost, so each factory sets the Hsts__Enabled env var in its instance constructor
// immediately before CreateClient(). Both clients address a host that is not loopback, over https://,
// because ASP.NET's HSTS middleware writes nothing on plain HTTP or for localhost.
public sealed class HstsEnabledTestWebApplicationFactory : AuthTestWebApplicationFactory
{
    public HttpClient Client { get; }

    public HstsEnabledTestWebApplicationFactory()
    {
        Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("Hsts__Enabled", "true");
        Client = CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://iverson.test") });
    }
}

// The off counterpart, set explicitly to "false" so this host never depends on what the factory above
// left in the process-global env var.
public sealed class HstsDisabledTestWebApplicationFactory : AuthTestWebApplicationFactory
{
    public HttpClient Client { get; }

    public HstsDisabledTestWebApplicationFactory()
    {
        Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("Hsts__Enabled", "false");
        Client = CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://iverson.test") });
    }
}
```

**1b.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.Api.Tests/HstsPipelineTests.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Net;
using FluentAssertions;
using Iverson.Api.Tests.Helpers;
using Xunit;

namespace Iverson.Api.Tests;

// CSR round 12 §4.4: with Hsts:Enabled, which the chart sets where global.externalScheme is https,
// Kestrel answers HTTPS requests with Strict-Transport-Security for one year, subdomains included, no
// preload. Without it there is no header. /health/live is the anonymous target, as in
// AdminConsoleCorsPipelineTests.
public class HstsPipelineTests :
    IClassFixture<HstsEnabledTestWebApplicationFactory>,
    IClassFixture<HstsDisabledTestWebApplicationFactory>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _enabled;
    private readonly HttpClient _disabled;

    public HstsPipelineTests(HstsEnabledTestWebApplicationFactory enabled, HstsDisabledTestWebApplicationFactory disabled)
    {
        _enabled = enabled.Client;
        _disabled = disabled.Client;
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Enabled_HttpsResponse_CarriesOneYearIncludeSubDomains()
    {
        var response = await _enabled.GetAsync("/health/live");

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK);
        response.Headers.TryGetValues("Strict-Transport-Security", out var values).Should().BeTrue();
        values!.Should().ContainSingle().Which.Should().Be("max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Disabled_HttpsResponse_CarriesNoStrictTransportSecurity()
    {
        var response = await _disabled.GetAsync("/health/live");

        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK);
        response.Headers.Contains("Strict-Transport-Security").Should().BeFalse();
    }
}
```

```bash
cat > $D/bin/mysql <<'T19STUB'
#!/bin/sh
# Refuses a login whose -p password differs from the state file's (empty: no -p). Logs each -e statement
# with the login it used; SET PASSWORD for root updates the state; SHOW BACKENDS/FRONTENDS print one row
# per $STUB_BE / $STUB_FE node.
pw=""; stmt=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in -e) stmt="$2"; shift 2 ;; -p*) pw="${1#-p}"; shift ;; *) shift ;; esac; done
[ "$pw" = "$(cat "$STUB_STATE")" ] || { echo "ERROR 1045 Access denied for user 'root'" >&2; exit 1; }
printf '%s\t%s\n' "${pw:+pw}" "$(printf '%s' "$stmt" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/  */ /g; s/^ //')" >> "$STUB_LOG"
case "$stmt" in
  *"SET PASSWORD FOR 'root' = PASSWORD('"*) printf '%s' "$stmt" | sed -n "s/.*SET PASSWORD FOR 'root' = PASSWORD('\([^']*\)').*/\1/p" | tr -d '\n' > "$STUB_STATE" ;;
  "SHOW BACKENDS;") i=0; while [ $i -lt "$STUB_BE" ]; do echo "be-$i"; i=$((i+1)); done ;;
  "SHOW FRONTENDS;") i=0; while [ $i -lt "$STUB_FE" ]; do echo "fe-$i"; i=$((i+1)); done ;;
esac
exit 0
T19STUB
chmod +x $D/bin/mysql
fails=0
for c in fresh upgrade; do
  : > $D/log; if [ $c = fresh ]; then : > $D/state; else printf r > $D/state; fi
  STUB_LOG=$D/log STUB_STATE=$D/state STUB_BE=1 STUB_FE=1 ROOT_PW=r APP_PW=a PROVISIONER_PW=p PATH=$D/bin:$PATH timeout 30 sh $D/job.sh > $D/out 2>&1; rc=$?
  setpw=$(command grep -n "SET PASSWORD FOR 'root'" $D/log | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  backends=$(command grep -n "SHOW BACKENDS;" $D/log | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  frontends=$(command grep -n "SHOW FRONTENDS;" $D/log | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  create=$(command grep -n "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'iverson_app'" $D/log | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  ok=FAIL
  [ $rc = 0 ] && [ -n "$setpw" ] && [ -n "$backends" ] && [ -n "$frontends" ] && [ -n "$create" ] &&
    [ "$setpw" -lt "$backends" ] && [ "$backends" -lt "$create" ] && [ "$frontends" -lt "$create" ] &&
    [ "$(cat $D/state)" = r ] && [ "$(command grep -c "^pw" $D/log)" -ge 3 ] && ok=PASS
  [ $ok = PASS ] || { fails=1; sed 's/^/    /' $D/log; tail -3 $D/out | sed 's/^/    out: /'; }
  echo "[job:$c] $ok exit=$rc set-password@$setpw show-backends@$backends show-frontends@$frontends create-user@$create"
done
exit $fails
```

```bash
"""CSR round 12 §4.5 (kind edge) render checks (Task 20):

import base64, re, sys, yaml

def snippet_headers(ingress):
    """The headers base's ingress-nginx configuration snippet set, as [{name, value}]."""
    s = ingress["metadata"]["annotations"].get("nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet", "")
    return [{"name": n, "value": v} for n, v in re.findall(r'more_set_headers "([^:]+): (.*)";', s)]

def header_filter(rule):

    if g:

        svcs = [m["method"]["service"] for m in s["rules"][0]["matches"]]
        want = [f"iverson.{x}" for x in ("ObjectMappingService", "ObjectPersistenceService", "ObjectRetrievalService", "ObjectSearchService", "TenantLifecycleGrpcService", "TenantAdminGrpcService")]
        check(svcs == want, f"GRPCRoute services {svcs}")
        check(s["rules"][0]["backendRefs"] == [{"name": f"{REL}-api", "port": 8080}], "GRPCRoute backend wrong")
        check(header_filter(s["rules"][0]) == snippet_headers(base[("Ingress", f"{REL}-api")]),
              f"GRPCRoute headers differ from the nginx snippet's:\n      {header_filter(s['rules'][0])}\n      {snippet_headers(base[('Ingress', f'{REL}-api')])}")
    a = by.get(("HTTPRoute", f"{REL}-authentik"))
    check(a is not None and a["spec"] == {"parentRefs": [dict(GW, sectionName="authentik-http")], "hostnames": [f"authentik.{HOST}"],

    aa = by.get(("HTTPRoute", f"{REL}-admin-api"))

        check(aa is not None and aa["spec"]["parentRefs"] == [dict(GW, sectionName="admin-api-http")] and aa["spec"]["hostnames"] == [f"admin-api.{HOST}"]
              and paths == [{"type": "PathPrefix", "value": p} for p in ("/admin", "/health", "/v1/traces")]
              and aa["spec"]["rules"][0]["backendRefs"] == [{"name": f"{REL}-api", "port": 8081}], f"admin-api HTTPRoute wrong: {aa}")
    else:
        check(aa is None, "admin-api HTTPRoute rendered where the admin-api Ingress was not")
    ui = by.get(("HTTPRoute", f"{REL}-admin-ui"))
    if ("Ingress", f"{REL}-admin-ui") in base:
        check(ui is not None, "admin-ui HTTPRoute missing")

            r = ui["spec"]["rules"][0]

            check(r["matches"] == [{"path": {"type": "PathPrefix", "value": "/admin"}}], "admin-ui match wrong")

            check(r["backendRefs"] == [{"name": f"{REL}-admin-ui", "port": 8080}], "admin-ui backend wrong")
    else:

"""CSR round 12 §4.5 kind-script checks (Task 20): python3 check_t20_kind.py <worktree>"""
import sys, yaml

        ("setup.ps1", 'Write-Host "', "\nfunction New-EdgeGateway {", ("\nAdd-AmbientLabels\n", "\nNew-EdgeGateway\n"),
         '$Phases = @("istio", "operator-namespaces", "ambient-labels", "gateway")')):
    s = open(f"{K}/{f}").read()
    check("ingress-nginx ingress-nginx" not in s and "kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx" not in s, f"{f} still installs ingress-nginx")
    check(phases in s, f"{f}: the --only phases do not end with gateway")

    body = s[g:s.find("\n}\n", g)] if g >= 0 else ""
    gorder = ["edge-gateway.yaml", "rollout status deployment/edge-istio -n iverson-edge"]
    gpos = [body.find(x) for x in gorder]
    check(g >= 0 and all(p >= 0 for p in gpos) and gpos == sorted(gpos), f"{f}: the gateway phase wrong: {list(zip(gorder, gpos))}")
    order = [*calls, f"{marker}All operators installed."]
    pos = [s.find(x) for x in order]
    check(all(p >= 0 for p in pos) and pos == sorted(pos), f"{f}: fresh-install order wrong: {list(zip(order, pos))}")
ps1 = open(f"{K}/setup.ps1").read()
g = ps1.find("\nfunction New-EdgeGateway {")
gbody = ps1[g:ps1.find("\n}\n", g)] if g >= 0 else ""
tls, apply = gbody.find("kubectl create secret tls iverson-api-tls"), gbody.find("kubectl apply -f (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot \"edge-gateway.yaml\")")
check(0 <= tls < apply, "setup.ps1's gateway phase does not create the edge certificate iverson-api-tls before applying the Gateway")
try:
    docs = {d["kind"]: d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(f"{K}/edge-gateway.yaml")) if d}
except FileNotFoundError:
    docs = {}; fails.append("deploy/kind/edge-gateway.yaml missing")
cm, gw = docs.get("ConfigMap"), docs.get("Gateway")
check(cm is not None and cm["metadata"] == {"name": "edge-options", "namespace": "iverson-edge"}, "options ConfigMap wrong")
if cm:

    check(dep["strategy"] == {"type": "RollingUpdate", "rollingUpdate": {"maxSurge": 0, "maxUnavailable": 1}}, f"gateway strategy {dep['strategy']}")
    ports = dep["template"]["spec"]["containers"][0]["ports"]

check(gw is not None and gw["metadata"]["name"] == "edge" and gw["metadata"]["namespace"] == "iverson-edge", "Gateway name or namespace wrong")
if gw:
    s = gw["spec"]
    check(s["gatewayClassName"] == "istio" and s["infrastructure"]["parametersRef"] == {"group": "", "kind": "ConfigMap", "name": "edge-options"}, "Gateway class or parametersRef wrong")
    check(gw["metadata"].get("annotations", {}).get("networking.istio.io/service-type") == "ClusterIP", "gateway Service is not ClusterIP")
    ls = {l["name"]: (l["hostname"], l["port"], l["protocol"]) for l in s["listeners"]}
    check(ls == {"api-https": ("iverson.local", 443, "HTTPS"), "admin-api-http": ("admin-api.iverson.local", 80, "HTTP"),
                 "authentik-http": ("authentik.iverson.local", 80, "HTTP"), "ui-http": ("iverson.local", 80, "HTTP")}, f"listeners {ls}")
    api = [l for l in s["listeners"] if l["name"] == "api-https"][0]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Renders the chart in $1 (default: the worktree's) with values that the Task 20 guards must refuse, and prints
# PASS when the render fails with the expected message. Usage: t20_guards.sh [chart]
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
CH=${1:-$WT/Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson}
cd "$CH" && helm dependency build . >/dev/null
guard() {  # label, expected message fragment, helm args...
  local label=$1 want=$2; shift 2
  out="$(helm template iverson . -n iverson "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  if [ $rc != 0 ] && printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -qF "$want"; then echo "[guard:$label] PASS"
  else echo "[guard:$label] FAIL rc=$rc"; fi
}

s = open(sys.argv[1]).read()

T20PY
  local rc=$?; [ $rc = 0 ] && cp "$1" $M/orig && mv $M/tmp "$1"; return $rc
```

**3a.** Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/edge-gateway.yaml`:

```yaml
# CSR round 12 §4.5: kind's edge, an Istio Gateway in namespace iverson-edge (not enrolled in the mesh,
# but its pod is a mesh client: it reaches the release over mutual TLS as
# cluster.local/ns/iverson-edge/sa/edge-istio). deploy/kind/setup.sh and setup.ps1 apply this file after
# creating the namespace; the chart attaches its routes to the listeners by name (templates/gateway-istio.yaml)
# and lets the HTTPS listener read the edge certificate (its ReferenceGrant). Hosts are the kind profile's
# global.ingressHost, iverson.local.
#
# The options ConfigMap gives the gateway's pod host ports 80 and 443, which kind-config.yaml maps to
# 127.0.0.1:8080 and 8443, and replaces the old pod before starting a new one: with host ports, a surge
# pod can never schedule on a single-node cluster, so the default rollout would deadlock. The Service
# Istio generates stays ClusterIP (kind has no load balancer).
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: edge-options
  namespace: iverson-edge
data:
  deployment: |
    spec:
      strategy:
        type: RollingUpdate
        rollingUpdate: { maxSurge: 0, maxUnavailable: 1 }
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: istio-proxy
              ports:
                - { containerPort: 443, hostPort: 443, protocol: TCP }
                - { containerPort: 80, hostPort: 80, protocol: TCP }
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: edge
  namespace: iverson-edge
  annotations:
    networking.istio.io/service-type: ClusterIP
spec:
  gatewayClassName: istio
  infrastructure:
    parametersRef: { group: "", kind: ConfigMap, name: edge-options }
  listeners:
    # gRPC to the API, over TLS: external gRPC clients need HTTP/2 from the first byte.
    - name: api-https
      hostname: iverson.local
      port: 443
      protocol: HTTPS
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs: [{ kind: Secret, name: iverson-api-tls, namespace: iverson }]
      allowedRoutes: { namespaces: { from: Selector, selector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: iverson } } } }
    - name: admin-api-http
      hostname: admin-api.iverson.local
      port: 80
      protocol: HTTP
      allowedRoutes: { namespaces: { from: Selector, selector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: iverson } } } }
    - name: authentik-http
      hostname: authentik.iverson.local
      port: 80
      protocol: HTTP
      allowedRoutes: { namespaces: { from: Selector, selector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: iverson } } } }
    - name: ui-http
      hostname: iverson.local
      port: 80
      protocol: HTTP
      allowedRoutes: { namespaces: { from: Selector, selector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: iverson } } } }
```

The listeners name `iverson.local`, kind's `global.ingressHost`, and `iverson-api-tls`, the certificate `setup.sh` generates, as the scripts already did for ingress-nginx. The Service type is set by the annotation the prototype ran (Verified assumption 52); the ConfigMap carries the host ports and the rollout strategy (Verified assumption 70).

**3b.** In `Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh`, delete (replace with nothing) lines `:84-135`:

```bash
echo "Installing ingress-nginx..."
# allow-snippet-annotations is disabled by default since ingress-nginx v1.9; the
# api and admin-ui charts' Ingress templates emit
# nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet on this className, which the
# validating admission webhook rejects (or the controller silently drops) without
# this setting. This install is this repo's only source of the controller for the
# only ingress class the kind profile actually runs, so this is the one place that
# setting can be turned on.
#
# SECURITY TRADE-OFF (CSR round-2 finding #13): upstream disables snippet annotations
# by default because they let anyone who can create/edit an Ingress inject arbitrary
# nginx.conf directives (Lua, arbitrary proxying, config-level RCE surface) into the
# shared controller — a real risk on a multi-tenant cluster where Ingress creation isn't
# trusted. Here it is acceptable: this is a single-tenant kind/local cluster, every
# Ingress in the namespace is rendered from this repo's own chart templates (not
# arbitrary user input), and the only annotation actually emitted is the fixed
# security-header snippet those templates hardcode — there is no untrusted path that can
# reach configuration-snippet. This setting is scoped to the `nginx` ingress class used
# only by kind/local; production/cloud profiles use alb/gce/azure-application-gateway
# (see values-aws/azure/gcp.yaml) and never enable this flag — azure wires the same
# security headers through AGIC's own rewrite-rule-set mechanism instead (see
# charts/api/templates/ingress.yaml's `securityHeadersRuleSet`), and none of the cloud
# ingress classes support or need nginx's snippet-annotation feature at all.
# CSR round-3 finding #7: chart 4.11.3 shipped controller v1.11.3, which predates the
# March-2025 "IngressNightmare" CVE fixes (CVE-2025-1097, CVE-2025-1098, CVE-2025-1974,
# CVE-2025-24513, CVE-2025-24514), landed in controller v1.11.5 / v1.12.1. Bumped to
# chart 4.12.8 (controller v1.12.8, confirmed via the ingress-nginx Helm repo's
# index.yaml chart-version-to-appVersion mapping as of this fix), well past the fixed
# versions. Re-verified `helm template` output with this repo's exact --set flags
# renders cleanly at this chart version.
#
# `allowSnippetAnnotations=true` alone is no longer sufficient on this chart version:
# confirmed live 2026-09-24 that installing with only that flag still gets the api and
# admin-ui Ingresses rejected at apply time with "annotation group ConfigurationSnippet
# contains risky annotation" from the admission webhook. Controller 1.12 added a second,
# independent gate — annotations are now classified by risk, and the ConfigMap's default
# `annotations-risk-level` dropped from Critical to High, which sits below
# configuration-snippet's Critical classification. `allow-snippet-annotations` only
# controls whether the controller RENDERS the annotation into nginx.conf; this is what
# controls whether the admission webhook lets the Ingress through in the first place.
# Raising it back to Critical carries the same trade-off as the setting above (this is a
# single-tenant cluster; only this repo's own chart templates create Ingresses here).
helm upgrade --install ingress-nginx ingress-nginx \
  --repo https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx \
  --version 4.12.8 \
  --namespace ingress-nginx --create-namespace \
  --set controller.hostPort.enabled=true \
  --set controller.service.type=ClusterIP \
  --set controller.allowSnippetAnnotations=true \
  --set-string controller.config.annotations-risk-level=Critical \
  --wait

```

**3i.** The edge certificate, in the gateway phase, so that both the fresh install and an upgrade's `setup.ps1 --only gateway` create it (`setup.sh` has always created it; `main`'s `setup.ps1` never did). In `Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.ps1`, replace:

```powershell
  kubectl apply -f (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "edge-gateway.yaml")
```

with:

```powershell
  # The HTTPS listener api-https serves Secret iverson/iverson-api-tls (edge-gateway.yaml); setup.sh's fresh
  # install generates the same one. This phase creates it where it is missing, so a cluster set up by an
  # earlier setup.ps1, which never created it, gets it at the upgrade's --only gateway too. openssl ships
  # with Git for Windows.
  kubectl get secret iverson-api-tls -n iverson *> $null
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    if (-not (Get-Command openssl -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
      throw "openssl is not on PATH: it generates the edge gateway's self-signed certificate (iverson-api-tls). Add Git for Windows' usr\bin to PATH, or create the Secret yourself, then re-run."
    }
    Write-Host "Generating a self-signed dev cert for the edge gateway's HTTPS listener (iverson.local)..."
    $Key = Join-Path $env:TEMP "iverson-api-tls.key"; $Crt = Join-Path $env:TEMP "iverson-api-tls.crt"
    openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 365 -keyout $Key -out $Crt -subj "/CN=iverson.local" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:iverson.local"
    kubectl create secret tls iverson-api-tls -n iverson --cert=$Crt --key=$Key
    Remove-Item -Force $Key, $Crt
  }
  kubectl apply -f (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "edge-gateway.yaml")
```

**5b.** Replace the whole of `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/charts/admin-ui/templates/ingress.yaml` with:

```yaml
{{- if not (dig "gateway" "class" "" .Values.global) }}
{{/*
CSR round 12 §4.5: rendered only where the profile's own Ingress class is the edge (AWS's alb, Azure's
Application Gateway); where global.gateway.class is set, the parent's gateway templates route this path
instead, with the same security headers.

The security headers nginx.conf serves from the admin-ui pod itself are mirrored at the Ingress layer
where the class supports it. There is no portable response-header annotation across ingress
controllers:
  - azure-application-gateway: AGIC's rewrite-rule-set annotation references a
    named rule set; the header text itself cannot live in the annotation, and
    this repo's Terraform does not provision one (the AGIC add-on is enabled in
    `deploy/terraform/modules/cluster-azure/main.tf`, but no
    `azurerm_application_gateway_rewrite_rule_set` exists anywhere in
    `deploy/terraform`). Rather than have this chart provision Azure
    infrastructure, the annotation is opt-in: it is only emitted when
    `ingress.securityHeadersRuleSet` is set to the name of a rule set you have
    provisioned separately. Left at its default (empty), no such annotation is
    rendered and AGIC gets nothing to fail to resolve.
  - alb: the controller exposes no response-header annotation, so the headers come from the origin
    (this pod's own nginx) only.
*/}}
{{- include "iverson.refuseRetiredIngressClass" (dict "label" "adminUi.ingress" "className" .Values.ingress.className) }}
{{- /* CSR round-11 #6: the class's port-80 setting only (iverson.edgeAnnotations); the edge → admin-ui
   hop serves static files and stays plaintext. The call passes only className and backendTls false
   because with backendTls off the helper reads no other key (missing keys read as nil). */}}
{{- $edge := include "iverson.edgeAnnotations" (dict "className" .Values.ingress.className "backendTls" false) | fromYaml }}
{{- $annotations := mergeOverwrite (deepCopy (default dict .Values.ingress.annotations)) $edge }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui
  annotations:
    {{- toYaml $annotations | nindent 4 }}
    {{- if and (eq .Values.ingress.className "azure-application-gateway") .Values.ingress.securityHeadersRuleSet }}
    appgw.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-rule-set: {{ .Values.ingress.securityHeadersRuleSet | quote }}
    {{- end }}
spec:
  ingressClassName: {{ .Values.ingress.className | quote }}
{{- if .Values.ingress.tlsSecretName }}
  tls:
    - hosts: [{{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
      secretName: {{ .Values.ingress.tlsSecretName | quote }}
{{- end }}
  rules:
    - host: {{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /admin(/|$)(.*)
            pathType: ImplementationSpecific
            backend:
              service:
                name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui
                port:
                  number: 8080
{{- end }}
```
