**6e.** Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/templates/gateway-istio.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- if eq (dig "gateway" "class" "" .Values.global) "istio" }}
{{- /*
CSR round 12 §4.5: kind's edge. deploy/kind/setup.sh creates the Istio Gateway (deploy/kind/edge-gateway.yaml):
an HTTPS listener api-https for global.ingressHost serving api.ingress.tlsSecretName, and HTTP listeners
admin-api-http, authentik-http and ui-http. These routes attach to it with the hosts and paths the
Ingresses had. The gateway is a mesh client, so each hop to a pod is mutual TLS through ztunnel, and the
API's and Authentik's own TLS runs inside it: a BackendTLSPolicy per TLS Service names the CA
(<release>-api-ca, <release>-authentik-ca, rendered beside each internal TLS Secret) and the host name
the pod certificate carries. ResponseHeaderModifier sets the security headers the ingress-nginx
configuration snippets set.
*/}}
{{- $gw := dict "name" (include "iverson.edgeGatewayName" .) "namespace" (include "iverson.edgeGatewayNamespace" .) }}
{{- $oidcOrigin := printf "%s://authentik.%s" .Values.global.externalScheme .Values.global.ingressHost }}
{{- $https := eq .Values.global.externalScheme "https" }}
# The gateway's HTTPS listener reads the edge certificate from this namespace.
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ReferenceGrant
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge-certificate
spec:
  from:
    - { group: gateway.networking.k8s.io, kind: Gateway, namespace: {{ $gw.namespace }} }
  to:
    - { group: "", kind: Secret, name: {{ .Values.api.ingress.tlsSecretName }} }
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GRPCRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ $gw.name }}, namespace: {{ $gw.namespace }}, sectionName: api-https }
  hostnames: [{{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        {{- range list "ObjectMappingService" "ObjectPersistenceService" "ObjectRetrievalService" "ObjectSearchService" "TenantLifecycleGrpcService" "TenantAdminGrpcService" }}
        - method: { service: iverson.{{ . }} }
        {{- end }}
      filters:
        - type: ResponseHeaderModifier
          responseHeaderModifier:
            set:
              - { name: X-Frame-Options, value: DENY }
              - { name: X-Content-Type-Options, value: nosniff }
              - { name: Referrer-Policy, value: no-referrer }
              - name: Content-Security-Policy
                value: "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' {{ $oidcOrigin }}; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'"
              - { name: Permissions-Policy, value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" }
              {{- if $https }}
              - { name: Strict-Transport-Security, value: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" }
              {{- end }}
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api, port: 8080 }
{{- if .Values.api.adminConsoleEnabled }}
---
# admin-api.<host>: only /admin, /health and /v1/traces, on the API's 8081.
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-api
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ $gw.name }}, namespace: {{ $gw.namespace }}, sectionName: admin-api-http }
  hostnames: [{{ printf "admin-api.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /admin }
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /health }
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /v1/traces }
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api, port: 8081 }
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ $gw.name }}, namespace: {{ $gw.namespace }}, sectionName: authentik-http }
  hostnames: [{{ printf "authentik.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik, port: 9080 }
{{- if .Values.adminUi.enabled }}
---
# The console under /admin on the main host; the prefix is stripped before the request reaches admin-ui.
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ $gw.name }}, namespace: {{ $gw.namespace }}, sectionName: ui-http }
  hostnames: [{{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /admin }
      filters:
        - type: URLRewrite
          urlRewrite:
            path: { type: ReplacePrefixMatch, replacePrefixMatch: / }
        - type: ResponseHeaderModifier
          responseHeaderModifier:
            set:
              - { name: X-Frame-Options, value: DENY }
              - { name: X-Content-Type-Options, value: nosniff }
              - { name: Referrer-Policy, value: no-referrer }
              - name: Content-Security-Policy
                value: "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' {{ printf "%s://admin-api.%s" .Values.global.externalScheme .Values.global.ingressHost }} {{ $oidcOrigin }}; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'"
              - { name: Permissions-Policy, value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" }
              {{- if $https }}
              - { name: Strict-Transport-Security, value: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" }
              {{- end }}
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui, port: 8080 }
{{- end }}
---
# The gateway re-encrypts to the API (8080 and 8081, one Kestrel) and verifies its certificate.
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: BackendTLSPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api }
  validation:
    hostname: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
    caCertificateRefs:
      - { group: "", kind: ConfigMap, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api-ca }
---
# ... and to Authentik's public listener (9080, the tls-proxy).
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: BackendTLSPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik, sectionName: http-public }
  validation:
    hostname: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
    caCertificateRefs:
      - { group: "", kind: ConfigMap, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik-ca }
{{- end }}
```

| M3 | Authentik is re-encrypted on 9080 only | its `BackendTLSPolicy` loses `sectionName: http-public` | values-local: `BackendTLSPolicy authentik wrong` |
| M4 | admin-ui's `/admin` prefix is stripped | `replacePrefixMatch: /` → `/admin` | values-local: `admin-ui URLRewrite wrong` |
| M5 | the ConfigMap holds the CA, not the leaf | `{{- $caCrt = $ca.Cert }}` → `$cert.Cert` | values-local: `ConfigMap iverson-api-ca does not hold the Secret's ca.crt` |
| M6 | nginx is refused without a gateway | `{{- if eq .className "nginx" -}}` → `"nginx-retired"` | `[guard:nginx-without-gateway] FAIL rc=0` |
| M7 | no surge pod on a single node | `maxSurge: 0, maxUnavailable: 1` → `maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0` | `[t20-kind] FAIL`: `gateway strategy …` |

values-aws stays `PASS` under M1–M5: its Ingresses and pods do not depend on the gateway branch.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Renders the chart in $1 (default: the worktree's) with values that the Task 21 guards must refuse, and prints
# PASS when the render fails with the expected message. Usage: t21_guards.sh [chart]
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
CH=${1:-$WT/Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson}
cd "$CH" && helm dependency build . >/dev/null
guard() {  # label, expected message fragment, helm args...
  local label=$1 want=$2; shift 2
  out="$(helm template iverson . -n iverson "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  if [ $rc != 0 ] && printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -qF "$want"; then echo "[guard:$label] PASS"
  else echo "[guard:$label] FAIL rc=$rc"; fi
}
G="-f values-gcp.yaml -f values-gcp.ci-override.yaml"
guard gke-without-address 'global.gateway.addressName must be set' $G --set global.gateway.addressName=
guard gke-without-cloud-armor 'authentik.ingress.securityPolicy must be set' $G --set authentik.ingress.securityPolicy=
guard gke-without-authentik-certificate 'authentik.ingress.tlsSecretName must be set' $G --set authentik.ingress.tlsSecretName=
guard gke-without-admin-api-certificate 'api.adminApiIngress.tlsSecretName must be set' $G --set api.adminApiIngress.tlsSecretName=
guard gce-ingress 'className "gce" is no longer served' -f values-aws.yaml -f values-aws.ci-override.yaml --set api.ingress.className=gce
T21GUARDS

# Task 21's mutation proof, on a copy of the chart under $SCR/t21-mut (never the worktree). Each mutation replaces
# exactly one occurrence of one line in one copied file, runs the check named for it, and restores the copy.
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh

  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "$3" > $M/tmp <<'T21PY'
import sys
s = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
if s.count(sys.argv[2]) != 1:

print(s.replace(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]), end="")
T21PY
  local rc=$?; [ $rc = 0 ] && cp "$1" $M/orig && mv $M/tmp "$1"; return $rc
}
restore() { mv $M/orig "$1"; }
render() {

}
guards() { bash $SCR/t21/t21_guards.sh $CH | sed 's/^/    /'; }

GK=$CH/templates/gateway-gke.yaml
run M1 $T/api/templates/service.yaml '      appProtocol: HTTP2' '      appProtocol: HTTPS' render

run M4 $GK '    - { type: NamedAddress, value: {{ .Values.global.gateway.addressName | quote }} }' '    - { type: IPAddress, value: {{ .Values.global.gateway.addressName | quote }} }' render
run M5 $CH/templates/_validate.tpl '{{- if not (dig "gateway" "addressName" "" .Values.global) }}' '{{- if false }}' guards
run M6 $CH/templates/_helpers.tpl '{{- else if eq .className "gce" -}}' '{{- else if eq .className "gce-retired" -}}' guards
```

Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson/templates/gateway-gke.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- if eq (dig "gateway" "class" "" .Values.global) "gke-l7-global-external-managed" }}
{{- /*
CSR round 12 §4.5: GCP's edge, a GKE Gateway (global external Application Load Balancer) in the release
namespace, replacing the four GCE Ingresses with the same hosts and paths:
- one HTTPS listener per host, serving the TLS Secrets the Ingress blocks name, on the static address
  Terraform reserves (global.gateway.addressName); no port-80 listener, so HTTP is off;
- HTTPRoutes only (this class supports no GRPCRoute): gRPC reaches the API's 8080 because that Service
  port's appProtocol is HTTP2, and the HTTPS ports carry appProtocol HTTPS;
- a BackendTLSPolicy for the API and Authentik Services, so the load balancer verifies each pod's
  certificate against the chart's CA (<release>-api-ca, <release>-authentik-ca) and host name. admin-ui
  stays plaintext from the edge, as on every profile: it serves static files;
- the Cloud Armor policy on Authentik's backend (GCPBackendPolicy), and the health checks the GCE
  Ingresses took from the readiness probes (HealthCheckPolicy). admin-ui's default check (HTTP / on its
  serving port) is the one its Ingress had.
*/}}
{{- $mainSecrets := list .Values.api.ingress.tlsSecretName }}
{{- if and .Values.adminUi.enabled .Values.adminUi.ingress.tlsSecretName }}
{{- $mainSecrets = append $mainSecrets .Values.adminUi.ingress.tlsSecretName | uniq }}
{{- end }}
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge
spec:
  gatewayClassName: gke-l7-global-external-managed
  addresses:
    - { type: NamedAddress, value: {{ .Values.global.gateway.addressName | quote }} }
  listeners:
    - name: main
      hostname: {{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}
      port: 443
      protocol: HTTPS
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          {{- range $mainSecrets }}
          - { kind: Secret, name: {{ . }} }
          {{- end }}
    {{- if .Values.api.adminConsoleEnabled }}
    - name: admin-api
      hostname: {{ printf "admin-api.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}
      port: 443
      protocol: HTTPS
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - { kind: Secret, name: {{ .Values.api.adminApiIngress.tlsSecretName }} }
    {{- end }}
    - name: authentik
      hostname: {{ printf "authentik.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}
      port: 443
      protocol: HTTPS
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - { kind: Secret, name: {{ .Values.authentik.ingress.tlsSecretName }} }
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge, sectionName: main }
  hostnames: [{{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        {{- range list "ObjectMappingService" "ObjectPersistenceService" "ObjectRetrievalService" "ObjectSearchService" "TenantLifecycleGrpcService" "TenantAdminGrpcService" }}
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /iverson.{{ . }} }
        {{- end }}
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api, port: 8080 }
{{- if .Values.api.adminConsoleEnabled }}
---
# admin-api.<host>: only /admin, /health and /v1/traces, on the API's 8081.
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-api
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge, sectionName: admin-api }
  hostnames: [{{ printf "admin-api.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /admin }
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /health }
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /v1/traces }
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api, port: 8081 }
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge, sectionName: authentik }
  hostnames: [{{ printf "authentik.%s" .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik, port: 9080 }
{{- if .Values.adminUi.enabled }}
---
# The console under /admin on the main host; the prefix is stripped before the request reaches admin-ui
# (the GCE Ingress could not strip it).
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-edge, sectionName: main }
  hostnames: [{{ .Values.global.ingressHost | quote }}]
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /admin }
      filters:
        - type: URLRewrite
          urlRewrite:
            path: { type: ReplacePrefixMatch, replacePrefixMatch: / }
      backendRefs:
        - { name: {{ .Release.Name }}-admin-ui, port: 8080 }
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: BackendTLSPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api }
  validation:
    hostname: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
    caCertificateRefs:
      - { group: "", kind: ConfigMap, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api-ca }
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: BackendTLSPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik }
  validation:
    hostname: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
    caCertificateRefs:
      - { group: "", kind: ConfigMap, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik-ca }
---
# CSR round-11 #5: Cloud Armor's rate limit on the login path (Terraform's authentik_security_policy_name),
# on Authentik's backend only. timeoutSec is the load balancer's default backend timeout, stated.
apiVersion: networking.gke.io/v1
kind: GCPBackendPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  default:
    securityPolicy: {{ .Values.authentik.ingress.securityPolicy | quote }}
    timeoutSec: 30
  targetRef: { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik }
---
# The public listener's liveness path, over HTTPS (Authentik's / redirects).
apiVersion: networking.gke.io/v1
kind: HealthCheckPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik
spec:
  default:
    config:
      type: HTTPS
      httpsHealthCheck: { port: 9080, requestPath: /-/health/live/ }
  targetRef: { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-authentik }
---
# The API's readiness check on its HTTP/1.1 port, for both of its backends (8080 speaks only HTTP/2).
apiVersion: networking.gke.io/v1
kind: HealthCheckPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  default:
    config:
      type: HTTPS
      httpsHealthCheck: { port: 8081, requestPath: /health }
  targetRef: { group: "", kind: Service, name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api }
{{- end }}
```

The main host's listener serves both certificates the GCE Ingresses named for it (api and admin-ui), deduplicated. Each `HealthCheckPolicy` is the check the GCE Ingress took from the readiness probe of the port it served: Authentik's public listener's `/-/health/live/` over HTTPS on 9080, and the API's `/health` over HTTPS on 8081, which also covers its HTTP/2-only 8080 backend. admin-ui's default (HTTP `/` on 8080) is the check its Ingress had. `timeoutSec: 30` is the load balancer's default backend timeout, the one the GCE backend had.

Without both, Authentik ignores the proxy's `X-Forwarded-Proto` and stamps `http://localhost:9443/` instead of the `https://localhost:9443/` this task configures as the external issuer (Verified assumption 67). This task does not edit either line.

```bash
"""CSR round 12 §4.6 compose TLS checks, server side: python3 check_t22_compose.py <repo root>"""
import sys, yaml
root = sys.argv[1]
S = f"{root}/Iverson.Server"
comp = yaml.safe_load(open(f"{S}/docker-compose.yml"))["services"]
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond: fails.append(msg)

def env(svc):
    e = comp[svc].get("environment") or {}
    if isinstance(e, dict):
        return {k: (None if v is None else str(v)) for k, v in e.items()}
    return dict(x.split("=", 1) if "=" in x else (x, None) for x in e)

def binds(svc):
    return {v["target"]: (v["source"], v.get("read_only")) for v in comp[svc].get("volumes") or [] if isinstance(v, dict)}

CA = ("./deploy/compose-tls/ca.crt", True)
CA_IN_APP = "/etc/iverson/authentik-ca/ca.crt"
HC = (r'printf "GET /health HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" | openssl s_client -quiet '
      r'-verify_return_error -CAfile /etc/iverson/authentik-ca/ca.crt -verify_hostname localhost '
      r'-connect 127.0.0.1:8081 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | grep -q " 200 "')

# Postgres: ssl=on through the wrapper, which copies the read-only key into a postgres-owned 0600 file.
pg = comp["postgres"]
check(pg.get("entrypoint") == ["sh", "/usr/local/bin/iverson-pg-tls-entrypoint.sh"], f"postgres entrypoint: {pg.get('entrypoint')}")
check(pg.get("command") == ["postgres"], f"postgres command: {pg.get('command')}")
b = binds("postgres")
check(b.get("/usr/local/bin/iverson-pg-tls-entrypoint.sh") == ("./deploy/postgres/tls-entrypoint.sh", True), "postgres: wrapper mount")
check(b.get("/etc/pgtls-src/tls.crt") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/postgres.crt", True), "postgres: certificate mount")
check(b.get("/etc/pgtls-src/tls.key") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/postgres.key", True), "postgres: key mount")
try:
    w = open(f"{S}/deploy/postgres/tls-entrypoint.sh").read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    w = ""
check("install -o postgres -g postgres -m 600 /etc/pgtls-src/tls.key /etc/pgtls/tls.key" in w, "postgres wrapper: no 0600 key copy")
check('exec docker-entrypoint.sh "$@" -c ssl=on -c ssl_cert_file=/etc/pgtls/tls.crt -c ssl_key_file=/etc/pgtls/tls.key' in w,
      "postgres wrapper: does not hand over to docker-entrypoint.sh with ssl=on")

# StarRocks FE: keystore built at start by the wrapper, through the image's own tini.
sr = comp["starrocks"]
check(sr.get("entrypoint") == ["/usr/bin/tini-static", "--", "bash", "/usr/local/bin/iverson-fe-tls-entrypoint.sh"],
      f"starrocks entrypoint: {sr.get('entrypoint')}")
check("/run/iverson-fe-tls:mode=0700" in (sr.get("tmpfs") or []), f"starrocks tmpfs: {sr.get('tmpfs')}")
b = binds("starrocks")
check(b.get("/usr/local/bin/iverson-fe-tls-entrypoint.sh") == ("./deploy/starrocks/fe-tls-entrypoint.sh", True), "starrocks: wrapper mount")
check(b.get("/etc/iverson/starrocks-tls/tls.crt") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/starrocks.crt", True), "starrocks: certificate mount")
check(b.get("/etc/iverson/starrocks-tls/tls.key") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/starrocks.key", True), "starrocks: key mount")
check(b.get("/etc/iverson/starrocks-tls/ca.crt") == CA, "starrocks: CA mount")

# Qdrant serves TLS as on Helm.
q = env("qdrant")
check(q.get("QDRANT__SERVICE__ENABLE_TLS") == "true", "qdrant: TLS not enabled")
check(q.get("QDRANT__TLS__CERT") == "/qdrant-tls/cert.pem" and q.get("QDRANT__TLS__KEY") == "/qdrant-tls/key.pem", "qdrant: TLS paths")
b = binds("qdrant")
check(b.get("/qdrant-tls/cert.pem") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/qdrant.crt", True), "qdrant: certificate mount")
check(b.get("/qdrant-tls/key.pem") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/qdrant.key", True), "qdrant: key mount")

# Authentik verifies Postgres, and the host reaches Authentik only through the tls-proxy on 9443.
for svc in ("authentik-migrate", "authentik-server", "authentik-worker"):
    e = env(svc)
    check(e.get("AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__SSLMODE") == "verify-full", f"{svc}: SSLMODE {e.get('AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__SSLMODE')}")
    check(e.get("AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__SSLROOTCERT") == "/etc/postgres-tls/ca.crt", f"{svc}: SSLROOTCERT")
    check(binds(svc).get("/etc/postgres-tls/ca.crt") == CA, f"{svc}: CA mount")
check(comp["authentik-server"].get("ports") == ["127.0.0.1:9443:8443"], f"authentik-server ports: {comp['authentik-server'].get('ports')}")

# The api and the worker: verify Postgres, the FE and Qdrant; serve HTTPS on every listener.
api, wk = env("iverson-api"), env("iverson-worker")
check(api.get("ConnectionStrings__Postgres") == "Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=iverson;Username=iverson_api;"
      f"Password=dev-only-not-for-production-postgres-api-pw-0123456789;SSL Mode=VerifyFull;Root Certificate={CA_IN_APP}",
      f"api Postgres: {api.get('ConnectionStrings__Postgres')}")
check(wk.get("ConnectionStrings__Postgres") == "Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=iverson;Username=iverson;Password=iverson;"
      f"SSL Mode=VerifyFull;Root Certificate={CA_IN_APP}", f"worker Postgres: {wk.get('ConnectionStrings__Postgres')}")
check((wk.get("ConnectionStrings__StarRocksProvisioner") or "").endswith(f";SslMode=VerifyFull;SslCa={CA_IN_APP};"),
      f"worker provisioner: {wk.get('ConnectionStrings__StarRocksProvisioner')}")
for name, e, svc in (("api", api, "iverson-api"), ("worker", wk, "iverson-worker")):
    check((e.get("ConnectionStrings__StarRocks") or "").endswith(f";SslMode=VerifyFull;SslCa={CA_IN_APP};"),
          f"{name} StarRocks: {e.get('ConnectionStrings__StarRocks')}")
    for ep, port in (("Grpc", 8080), ("Http", 8081), ("Metrics", 8082)):
        check(e.get(f"Kestrel__Endpoints__{ep}__Url") == f"https://*:{port}", f"{name} {ep} URL: {e.get(f'Kestrel__Endpoints__{ep}__Url')}")
        check(e.get(f"Kestrel__Endpoints__{ep}__Certificate__Path") == "/etc/iverson/api-tls/tls.crt", f"{name} {ep} certificate")
        check(e.get(f"Kestrel__Endpoints__{ep}__Certificate__KeyPath") == "/etc/iverson/api-tls/tls.key", f"{name} {ep} key")
    check(e.get("Qdrant__CertPath") == "/etc/qdrant-tls/cert.pem", f"{name} Qdrant__CertPath")
    check(e.get("Authentication__ExternalIssuer") == "https://localhost:9443/", f"{name} ExternalIssuer: {e.get('Authentication__ExternalIssuer')}")
    check(e.get("Authentik__PublicBaseUrl") == "https://localhost:9443", f"{name} PublicBaseUrl: {e.get('Authentik__PublicBaseUrl')}")
    b = binds(svc)
    check(b.get(CA_IN_APP) == CA, f"{name}: CA mount")
    check(b.get("/etc/iverson/api-tls/tls.crt") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/kestrel.crt", True), f"{name}: Kestrel certificate mount")
    check(b.get("/etc/iverson/api-tls/tls.key") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/kestrel.key", True), f"{name}: Kestrel key mount")
    check(b.get("/etc/qdrant-tls/cert.pem") == ("./deploy/compose-tls/qdrant.crt", True), f"{name}: Qdrant certificate mount")
check(comp["iverson-worker"].get("healthcheck", {}).get("test") == ["CMD-SHELL", f"bash -c '{HC}'"],
      f"worker healthcheck: {comp['iverson-worker'].get('healthcheck', {}).get('test')}")

print(f"[compose] {'PASS' if not fails else 'FAIL'}", *fails, sep="\n  ")
sys.exit(bool(fails))
T22COMPOSE
cat > $SCR/t22_gen.sh <<'T22GEN'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Task 22: runs a copy of generate-compose-secrets.sh ($1, default the worktree's) in a scratch checkout
# shape under $SCR/t22-gen and checks the certificates it writes. One PASS/FAIL line per check; exits
# with the number of failures. Usage: t22_gen.sh [script]
source /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ben-repositories-Iverson/a8dc481d-50d9-445a-974d-18c6594e3306/scratchpad/csr12p-sdd/env.sh
GEN=${1:-$WT/scripts/generate-compose-secrets.sh}
D=$SCR/t22-gen; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D/scripts $D/Iverson.Server/deploy
cp "$GEN" $D/scripts/generate-compose-secrets.sh
T=$D/Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls
fails=0
ok()  { echo "  PASS $1"; }
bad() { echo "  FAIL $1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
gen() { bash $D/scripts/generate-compose-secrets.sh >/dev/null 2>$D/gen.err || bad "the script exited non-zero: $(cat $D/gen.err)"; }
gen
want="ca.crt kestrel.crt kestrel.key postgres.crt postgres.key qdrant.crt qdrant.key starrocks.crt starrocks.key tls.crt tls.key"
[ "$(ls $T 2>/dev/null | sort | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')" = "$want" ] && ok "exactly the CA certificate and five leaves, no CA key" || bad "files: $(ls $T 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
[ "$(stat -c %a $T)" = 700 ] && ok "directory is 0700" || bad "directory mode $(stat -c %a $T)"
[ "$(openssl x509 -in $T/ca.crt -noout -ext keyUsage 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n')" = "X509v3KeyUsage:criticalCertificateSign,CRLSign" ] \
  && ok "CA keyUsage critical, keyCertSign, cRLSign" || bad "CA keyUsage: $(openssl x509 -in $T/ca.crt -noout -ext keyUsage 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' ')"
for row in "tls DNS:authentik-server,DNS:localhost" "postgres DNS:postgres,DNS:localhost" \
           "starrocks DNS:starrocks,DNS:localhost" "kestrel DNS:iverson-api,DNS:iverson-worker,DNS:localhost,IPAddress:127.0.0.1" \
           "qdrant DNS:qdrant,DNS:localhost"; do
  read -r stem san <<< "$row"
  got="$(openssl x509 -in $T/$stem.crt -noout -ext subjectAltName 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')"
  [ "$got" = "$san" ] && ok "$stem SAN $san" || bad "$stem SAN: $got"
  openssl verify -CAfile $T/ca.crt -purpose sslserver $T/$stem.crt >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "$stem chains to the CA" || bad "$stem does not chain to the CA"
  [ -f $T/$stem.key ] && [ "$(openssl x509 -in $T/$stem.crt -noout -pubkey | sha256sum)" = "$(openssl pkey -in $T/$stem.key -pubout | sha256sum)" ] \
    && ok "$stem key matches" || bad "$stem key does not match its certificate"
done
# Python 3.14's default context (stdlib urllib and the mint script use it) must accept the CA.
port=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])')
openssl s_server -quiet -accept 127.0.0.1:$port -cert $T/kestrel.crt -key $T/kestrel.key -www >/dev/null 2>&1 &
pid=$!; sleep 1
py="$(python3 -c "
import socket, ssl
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='$T/ca.crt')
try:
    with ctx.wrap_socket(socket.create_connection(('localhost', $port), timeout=5), server_hostname='localhost'):
        print('accepted')
except ssl.SSLError as e:
    print('refused:', e.verify_message or e)
" 2>&1)"
kill $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
[ "$py" = accepted ] && ok "Python's default context accepts the CA" || bad "Python's default context: $py"
# A re-run keeps every file.
before="$(sha256sum $T/* | sha256sum)"; gen
[ "$(sha256sum $T/* | sha256sum)" = "$before" ] && ok "a re-run keeps the files" || bad "a re-run rewrote the files"
# A missing leaf key rewrites everything under a new CA.
ca="$(sha256sum < $T/ca.crt)"; pg="$(sha256sum < $T/postgres.crt)"; rm $T/qdrant.key; gen
[ -f $T/qdrant.key ] && [ "$(sha256sum < $T/ca.crt)" != "$ca" ] && [ "$(sha256sum < $T/postgres.crt)" != "$pg" ] \
  && ok "a missing leaf key rewrites every file" || bad "a missing leaf key did not rewrite every file"
# A leaf ending within 30 days rewrites everything.
ca="$(sha256sum < $T/ca.crt)"

run M6 $C '      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__SSLMODE: verify-full
```

In `scripts/generate-compose-secrets.sh`, replace:
```bash
# CSR round-10 #5: the certificate the compose authentik-tls-proxy serves on 8443 and the CA the API
# trusts for it. Written when any file is missing or the certificate ends within 30 days, so a re-run
# otherwise keeps them; all three are rewritten together. The CA key is deleted once the certificate
# is signed. The files are world-readable inside an owner-only directory: under rootless podman a
# container uid cannot read a host file that is 0600, and the directory keeps other host users out.
TLS_DIR="$(dirname "$0")/../Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls"
if [ ! -f "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt" ] || [ ! -f "$TLS_DIR/tls.crt" ] || [ ! -f "$TLS_DIR/tls.key" ] \
    || ! openssl x509 -checkend $((30 * 24 * 3600)) -noout -in "$TLS_DIR/tls.crt" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    mkdir -p "$TLS_DIR"
    chmod 700 "$TLS_DIR"
    work="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    # openssl's progress output is noise on success; on failure show it and stop.
    quiet() { "$@" 2>"$work/openssl.err" || { cat "$work/openssl.err" >&2; exit 1; }; }
    quiet openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 825 -subj "/CN=iverson-compose-authentik-ca" \
        -keyout "$work/ca.key" -out "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt"
    quiet openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj "/CN=authentik-server" \
        -keyout "$TLS_DIR/tls.key" -out "$work/tls.csr"
    printf 'subjectAltName=DNS:authentik-server\n' > "$work/ext.cnf"
    quiet openssl x509 -req -in "$work/tls.csr" -CA "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt" -CAkey "$work/ca.key" \
        -set_serial "0x$(openssl rand -hex 8)" -days 825 -extfile "$work/ext.cnf" -out "$TLS_DIR/tls.crt"
    chmod 644 "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt" "$TLS_DIR/tls.crt" "$TLS_DIR/tls.key"
    echo "Wrote $TLS_DIR"
fi
```
with:
```bash
# CSR round-10 #5 and round 12 §4.6: the compose CA and the certificates it signs, one per TLS
# server: authentik-tls-proxy (tls.crt, the name the proxy has always mounted), Postgres, the
# StarRocks FE, Kestrel (iverson-api and iverson-worker share one) and Qdrant. Every leaf names its
# compose service and `localhost`, which host clients dial; only Kestrel's also names 127.0.0.1.
# All of them are rewritten together, under a new CA, when any file is missing or any certificate
# ends within 30 days, so a re-run otherwise keeps them. The CA key is deleted once every leaf is
# signed. The CA carries keyUsage: Python 3.14's default context refuses a CA without it. The
# files are world-readable inside an owner-only directory: under rootless podman a container uid
# cannot read a host file that is 0600, and the directory keeps other host users out.
TLS_DIR="$(dirname "$0")/../Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls"
# <file stem> <common name> <subjectAltName>
LEAVES=(
    "tls authentik-server DNS:authentik-server,DNS:localhost"
    "postgres postgres DNS:postgres,DNS:localhost"
    "starrocks starrocks DNS:starrocks,DNS:localhost"
    "kestrel iverson-api DNS:iverson-api,DNS:iverson-worker,DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
    "qdrant qdrant DNS:qdrant,DNS:localhost"
)
renew=no
[ -f "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt" ] || renew=yes
for leaf in "${LEAVES[@]}"; do
    read -r stem _ <<< "$leaf"
    if [ ! -f "$TLS_DIR/$stem.crt" ] || [ ! -f "$TLS_DIR/$stem.key" ] \
        || ! openssl x509 -checkend $((30 * 24 * 3600)) -noout -in "$TLS_DIR/$stem.crt" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        renew=yes
    fi
done
if [ "$renew" = yes ]; then
    mkdir -p "$TLS_DIR"
    chmod 700 "$TLS_DIR"
    work="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    # openssl's progress output is noise on success; on failure show it and stop.
    quiet() { "$@" 2>"$work/openssl.err" || { cat "$work/openssl.err" >&2; exit 1; }; }
    quiet openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 825 -subj "/CN=iverson-compose-ca" \
        -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" -keyout "$work/ca.key" -out "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt"
    for leaf in "${LEAVES[@]}"; do
        read -r stem cn san <<< "$leaf"
        quiet openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj "/CN=$cn" \
            -keyout "$TLS_DIR/$stem.key" -out "$work/$stem.csr"
        printf 'subjectAltName=%s\n' "$san" > "$work/$stem.cnf"
        quiet openssl x509 -req -in "$work/$stem.csr" -CA "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt" -CAkey "$work/ca.key" \
            -set_serial "0x$(openssl rand -hex 8)" -days 825 -extfile "$work/$stem.cnf" -out "$TLS_DIR/$stem.crt"
        chmod 644 "$TLS_DIR/$stem.crt" "$TLS_DIR/$stem.key"
    done
    chmod 644 "$TLS_DIR/ca.crt"
    echo "Wrote $TLS_DIR"
fi
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The two entrypoint wrappers**

Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/postgres/tls-entrypoint.sh` (Verified assumption 74's wrapper, verbatim apart from the comment):
```sh
#!/bin/sh
# CSR round 12 §4.6: compose's Postgres serves TLS from the compose certificate, which is
# bind-mounted read-only at /etc/pgtls-src. Postgres refuses a key file with group or world access
# and cannot read one owned by another user, so both files are copied into a postgres-owned
# directory, the key at 0600, before the image's own entrypoint runs. This runs as root, as the
# image's entrypoint does until it drops to postgres; the server flags reach the temporary
# init-time server too.
set -eu
install -d -o postgres -g postgres -m 700 /etc/pgtls
install -o postgres -g postgres -m 600 /etc/pgtls-src/tls.key /etc/pgtls/tls.key
install -o postgres -g postgres -m 644 /etc/pgtls-src/tls.crt /etc/pgtls/tls.crt
exec docker-entrypoint.sh "$@" -c ssl=on -c ssl_cert_file=/etc/pgtls/tls.crt -c ssl_key_file=/etc/pgtls/tls.key
```

Create `Iverson.Server/deploy/starrocks/fe-tls-entrypoint.sh`:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# CSR round 12 §4.6: compose's StarRocks FE serves TLS on its MySQL port, 9030, as the chart's FE
# does (charts/starrocks/templates/starrockscluster.yaml builds the same keystore in an init
# container). At every start this builds a PKCS12 keystore from the compose certificate into a
# tmpfs, makes sure fe.conf names it, and hands over to the image's own entrypoint. fe.conf lives in
# the starrocks_data volume, so each setting is appended once, the way the image's entrypoint
# appends priority_networks. ssl_force_secure_transport stays unset: compose does not force TLS,
# so the image's own BE registration and healthcheck, which call plain mysql, keep working.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
src=/etc/iverson/starrocks-tls
keystore=/run/iverson-fe-tls/fe.p12
# Not a secret: the keystore holds the same key as the mounted file it is built from.
password=iverson-fe-keystore
openssl pkcs12 -export -name fe -in "$src/tls.crt" -inkey "$src/tls.key" -certfile "$src/ca.crt" \
    -passout "pass:$password" -out "$keystore"
conf="$SR_HOME/fe/conf/fe.conf"
for setting in "ssl_keystore_location = $keystore" "ssl_keystore_password = $password" "ssl_key_password = $password"; do
    key="${setting%% =*}"
    if ! grep -aEq "^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*=" "$conf"; then
        if [ -s "$conf" ] && [ "$(tail -c 1 "$conf" | wc -l)" -eq 0 ]; then echo >> "$conf"; fi
        echo "$setting" >> "$conf"
    fi
done
exec ./entrypoint.sh
```

Both run through `sh`/`bash` from compose, so neither needs an executable bit.

```yaml
    # stores answer. bash /dev/tcp again: the runtime image has no curl or wget. CMD-SHELL wrapping
    # `bash -c '...'`, as qdrant's does, rather than ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "..."]: podman's Docker
    # API splits every CMD argument on whitespace, which turns that form into `bash -c exec`, a
    # check that always passes. The script holds no single quote (it sits inside one) and no `$`
    # (compose would interpolate it).
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8081 && printf \"GET /health HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\" >&3 && head -n 1 <&3 | grep -q \" 200 \"'"]
```

```yaml
    # stores answer. 8081 serves TLS (CSR round 12 §4.6), so the request goes through the runtime
    # image's openssl (it has no curl, wget or nc), which verifies the Kestrel certificate against the
    # mounted compose CA and the name localhost; -verify_return_error ends the check on a failed
    # verification. CMD-SHELL wrapping `bash -c '...'`, as qdrant's does, rather than
    # ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "..."]: podman's Docker API splits every CMD argument on whitespace,
    # which turns that form into `bash -c exec`, a check that always passes. The script holds no
    # single quote (it sits inside one) and no `$` (compose would interpolate it).
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c 'printf \"GET /health HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\" | openssl s_client -quiet -verify_return_error -CAfile /etc/iverson/authentik-ca/ca.crt -verify_hostname localhost -connect 127.0.0.1:8081 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | grep -q \" 200 \"'"]
```

```csharp
using FluentAssertions;
using Grpc.Core;
using Xunit;

namespace Iverson.ClientConformance.Tests;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §4.6: the harness's channel takes its transport from IVERSON_GRPC_URL's scheme, so it
/// reaches the compose API's TLS listener on https:// and a plaintext listener on http://.
/// Grpc.Net.Client refuses, while it builds the channel, insecure credentials on an https:// address
/// and secure credentials on an http:// one, so a wrong choice throws here.
/// </summary>
public class HarnessChannelTests
{

    [InlineData("HTTPS://localhost:8080")]
    [InlineData("http://localhost:8080")]

    {
        var act = () => HarnessChannel.Create(grpcUrl, NoOp).Dispose();

        act.Should().NotThrow();
    }
}
```

```python
# ── CSR round 12 §4.6: the --grpc scheme picks the transport ──────────────────────────────────

@pytest.mark.parametrize("grpc_addr,expected", [
    ("https://localhost:8080", ("localhost", 8080, True)),
    ("http://localhost:8080", ("localhost", 8080, False)),
    ("localhost:8080", ("localhost", 8080, False)),
])
def test_parse_grpc_address_takes_tls_from_the_scheme(grpc_addr, expected):
    assert parse_grpc_address(grpc_addr) == expected


def _record_channel_credentials(monkeypatch):
    """Records which base ChannelCredentials build_driver_channel asks grpc for."""
    made = []
    real_ssl, real_local = grpc.ssl_channel_credentials, grpc.local_channel_credentials

    def ssl(*args, **kwargs):
        made.append("ssl")
        return real_ssl(*args, **kwargs)

    def local(*args, **kwargs):
        made.append("local")
        return real_local(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(grpc, "ssl_channel_credentials", ssl)
    monkeypatch.setattr(grpc, "local_channel_credentials", local)
    return made


@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_tls,acting_token,expected", [
    (True, "acting", ["ssl"]),
    (False, "acting", ["local"]),
    (True, None, ["ssl"]),
    (False, None, []),
])
def test_build_driver_channel_takes_its_transport_from_use_tls(monkeypatch, use_tls, acting_token, expected):
    made = _record_channel_credentials(monkeypatch)
    channel = build_driver_channel("localhost", 1, None, None, None, acting_token, None, use_tls=use_tls)
    channel.close()
    assert made == expected
```

**3a.** Create `Iverson.Server/Iverson.ClientConformance/HarnessChannel.cs`:
```csharp
using Grpc.Core;
using Grpc.Net.Client;
using Iverson.LoadTest.Auth;

namespace Iverson.ClientConformance;

/// <summary>
/// CSR round 12 §4.6: the harness's own gRPC channel, which carries the service and acting-user
/// tokens, takes its transport from the URL's scheme, as the five drivers do. An https:// URL dials
/// TLS against the system roots (SSL_CERT_FILE names the compose CA); an http:// URL dials plaintext
/// h2c, which <see cref="CheckEndpoints"/> admits only on loopback.
/// </summary>
public static class HarnessChannel
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Why these endpoints may not carry the harness's credentials, or null when they may: LoadTest's
    /// rule (CSR round-11 #15), with an https:// gRPC URL allowed because <see cref="Create"/> dials
    /// TLS for one.
    /// </summary>
    public static string? CheckEndpoints(string grpcUrl, string? tokenEndpoint) =>
        CredentialEndpoints.Check(grpcUrl, tokenEndpoint, grpcMayUseTls: true);

    /// <summary>
    /// A channel that sends <paramref name="callCredentials"/> on every call: TLS for an https:// URL,
    /// plaintext h2c otherwise. Grpc.Net.Client drops call credentials on a plaintext channel unless
    /// UnsafeUseInsecureChannelCallCredentials is set, so it is set exactly then.
    /// </summary>
    public static GrpcChannel Create(string grpcUrl, CallCredentials callCredentials)
    {
        var tls = grpcUrl.StartsWith("https://", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        return GrpcChannel.ForAddress(grpcUrl, new GrpcChannelOptions
        {
            UnsafeUseInsecureChannelCallCredentials = !tls,
            Credentials = ChannelCredentials.Create(
                tls ? ChannelCredentials.SecureSsl : ChannelCredentials.Insecure, callCredentials),
        });
    }
}
```

```go
// transportOption picks the channel's transport security from --grpc's scheme (CSR round 12 §4.6):
// https:// dials TLS, verifying the server against the system roots, which SSL_CERT_FILE points at
// the compose CA; anything else dials plaintext h2c, the accepted local dev/test model.
func transportOption(addr string) grpc.DialOption {
	if grpcUsesTLS(addr) {
		return grpc.WithTransportCredentials(credentials.NewTLS(&tls.Config{}))
	}
	return grpc.WithInsecure() //nolint:staticcheck
}

// grpcUsesTLS reports whether --grpc names an https:// endpoint.
func grpcUsesTLS(addr string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(addr), "https://")
}
```

Create `docs/runbooks/csr12-platform.md`:
````markdown
# CSR Round-12 Platform — Operator Runbook

**Why:** CSR round 12's Platform sub-project (`docs/specs/2026-10-19-csr-round12-platform-design.md`)
puts every in-cluster hop under Istio ambient mTLS, moves kind's edge from ingress-nginx to an Istio
gateway and GCP's to GKE Gateway, gates the api's and admin-automation's workload identities behind an
admission policy that only the operators group passes, adds default-deny policies to the operator
namespaces, grants Operator from a per-install list of subjects instead of an Authentik group, throttles
logins per address and account, and serves TLS on compose's authentication-carrying hops. This runbook
covers the upgrade order, the operators group, compose, and the checks a first cloud deploy must make.
Operator onboarding, the operator list, login throttling and `AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY` rotation are in
`operator-access-onboarding.md` and `csr11-identity-plane.md`.

## 1. Before the upgrade

- **kind needs a new cluster.** The node image is pinned to Kubernetes 1.35.8
  (`Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/kind-config.yaml`), and kind changes a node image only by recreating the
  cluster. `setup.sh` and `setup.ps1` refuse a kind older than v0.33.0. A fresh install needs none of
  §3; §3 is the order for a cluster that already runs `main`'s chart.
- **Run `helm dependency build`** in `Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson`. A stale `charts/*.tgz`
  renders the old subcharts.
- **The cloud profiles have no upgrade path.** No cloud cluster is deployed, so each is a fresh install
  at Kubernetes 1.35: one Terraform apply (Istio, the operator-namespace policy chart and the namespace
  labels), then the chart install, then the checks in §5.

## 2. The operators group

The admission policy `<release>-<namespace>-sensitive-identities` refuses everyone outside
`admission.operatorGroups`, cluster-admin included, when they:
- create a token for `<release>-api` or `<release>-admin-automation`;
- exec, attach or port-forward into a `<release>-api-*`, `<release>-worker-*`, `<release>-authentik-*` or
  `<release>-postgres-*` pod, add an ephemeral container to one, or change one of its container images;
- create a pod, or create or update a workload, whose pod template uses either account.

So a `kubectl rollout restart` of the api, the blueprint applies and shells in the Authentik worker,
`psql` in a Postgres instance, and every `helm upgrade` that changes a protected workload (a chart-version
or api template change does) need the group.

- **kind and laptop** (group `iverson-operators`): add the group to your own identity by impersonation.

  ```bash
  OPS="--as=kubernetes-admin --as-group=kubeadm:cluster-admins --as-group=iverson-operators"
  kubectl $OPS -n iverson rollout restart deployment/iverson-api
  kubectl $OPS -n iverson port-forward svc/iverson-authentik 9000:9000
  ```

  Helm takes `--kube-as-user` together with `--kube-as-group` (§3 step 2); `--kube-as-group` alone is
  refused. `kubectl cnpg psql` does not pass impersonation flags to the `kubectl exec` it starts: give it a
  kubeconfig context whose user sets `as` and `as-groups` (with `--context`), or run a plain
  `kubectl $OPS exec` into the primary instance's `postgres` container.
- **Under PSA baseline** `kubectl debug` also needs `--profile=baseline`.
- **Clouds.** Operators hold the group through the platform: on AKS, the Entra group(s) in
  `cluster_admin_group_object_ids`; on EKS, the operator access entries' `kubernetes_groups`; on GKE, a
  Google Group under Google Groups for RBAC. §5 checks that it reaches the API server.

## 3. Upgrading an existing kind cluster

Run the steps in order. Steps 2 and 7 need the operators group.

Steps 1, 4, 5 and 6 run one phase of the kind setup script each: `Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh
--only <phase>` (`setup.ps1 --only <phase>` on Windows) runs exactly what a fresh install runs for that
phase, and nothing else.

1. **Istio and the Gateway API CRDs.** Install Istio 1.31.2 (`base`, `istiod` with the `ambient`
   profile, `istio-cni` and `ztunnel`, from the vendored charts) and the Gateway API v1.6.3 standard CRDs.
   Nothing is enrolled yet, so traffic does not change:

   ```bash
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh --only istio
   ```
2. **Load the branch's images, then upgrade the release as the operators group.** The chart runs the
   api, the worker and the console at tag `0.1.0` with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`, so the node
   keeps serving `main`'s build under that tag until the branch's is loaded. `main`'s api checks
   StarRocks readiness with `SHOW BACKENDS`, which needs the `OPERATE ON SYSTEM` this upgrade revokes,
   so its pods would go unready for good once the revoke runs. On Windows, run
   `Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/build-and-load-image.ps1` for the api and worker image (add
   `-ClusterName <name>` if the cluster is not named `iverson`); it builds only that image, so build and
   load the console by hand: `docker build -f Iverson.AdminUI/Dockerfile -t
   docker.io/library/iverson-admin-ui:0.1.0 .`, then `kind load docker-image
   docker.io/library/iverson-admin-ui:0.1.0 --name iverson`. Elsewhere, from the repository root (pass
   `0.1.0 <cluster>` to each script if the cluster is not named `iverson`):

   ```bash
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/build-and-load-image.sh
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/build-and-load-image.sh 0.1.0 iverson --dockerfile Iverson.AdminUI/Dockerfile --image-name iverson-admin-ui
   cd Iverson.Server/deploy/helm/iverson && helm dependency build .
   helm upgrade --install --wait --timeout 10m iverson . -f values-local.yaml -n iverson \
     --kube-as-user kubernetes-admin --kube-as-group kubeadm:cluster-admins --kube-as-group iverson-operators
   ```

   Use `values-laptop.yaml` on the laptop profile. This renders the 15008 rules, the operator → operand
   rules, the mesh policies, the admission policy, the gateway routes and the Authentik changes; the
   15008 rules and the mesh policies do nothing until step 5. The upgrade moves Authentik from 2026.5.3
   to 2026.8.4: the new worker migrates the database while the old server pods keep serving, and the new
   server pods wait for the migration, which can outlast Helm's default 5-minute timeout, hence
   `--timeout 10m`. The post-upgrade revoke of `OPERATE ON SYSTEM` runs once the new pods are Ready; a
   terminating previous-release pod may still fail readiness briefly, as with the role revoke
   (`csr12-server.md` §1).

   **The kind edge is down from this step until step 6.** The chart stops rendering its Ingresses here
   (kind's routes are now `GRPCRoute` and `HTTPRoute` objects on the gateway step 6 creates), so
   ingress-nginx serves nothing for the release in between. Reach the services in-cluster meanwhile
   (`kubectl $OPS port-forward`, §2).

   The console's pod template does not change in this upgrade, so restart it to run the new build
   (local; laptop has no console): `kubectl -n iverson rollout restart deployment/iverson-admin-ui`.

   **2a. Restart Prometheus** where it runs (local; laptop has none). It reads its scrape config only at
   start, so until then it scrapes the old 8081 targets instead of 8082:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n iverson rollout restart deployment/iverson-prometheus
   ```
3. **Restart the StarRocks FE.** `ssl_force_secure_transport` is read only at start, and the StarRocks
   operator does not roll the FE when only its `fe.conf` ConfigMap changes:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n iverson delete pod -l app.starrocks.ownerreference/name=iverson-starrocks-fe
   ```
4. **The edge namespace, then the operator-namespace policies.** The phase creates `istio-system` and
   `iverson-edge` (never enrolled) where they are missing, then installs the operator-namespace policy
   chart (`Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/modules/operators/charts/operator-namespace-policies`):

   ```bash
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh --only operator-namespaces
   ```
5. **Enrol the four namespaces together.** The phase labels `iverson`, `cnpg-system`, `kafka` and
   `starrocks` once the release's NetworkPolicies list 15008 (step 2); otherwise it labels nothing and
   says so. Running pods are captured without a restart:

   ```bash
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh --only ambient-labels
   ```
6. **Replace ingress-nginx with the gateway.** Both want the node's host ports 80 and 443, so remove
   ingress-nginx first, then create the gateway in `iverson-edge`. The edge, down since step 2, returns
   once the gateway pod is Ready:

   ```bash
   helm uninstall ingress-nginx -n ingress-nginx
   kubectl delete namespace ingress-nginx
   Iverson.Server/deploy/kind/setup.sh --only gateway
   ```
7. **Apply the changed Authentik blueprints** as `csr11-identity-plane.md` §2 describes, adding the
   operators-group flags of §2 to every `kubectl exec`.

Then run the three probe scripts in `Iverson.Server/deploy/scripts/` (`authentik-probes.sh`,
`mesh-check.sh`, `admission-check.sh`); each one's header gives its arguments.

## 4. Compose

Compose's authentication-carrying hops now serve TLS from a per-checkout CA: the api and the worker
(Kestrel on 8080, 8081 and 8082), Authentik (through `authentik-tls-proxy`, published on 9443; 9000 is no
longer published), Postgres, the StarRocks FE and Qdrant. TEI, Ollama and Jaeger stay plaintext; they
carry no credentials.

1. **Re-run `scripts/generate-compose-secrets.sh`.** It writes a new CA, now carrying `keyUsage`, and
   five certificates into `Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls/`. It rewrites all of them together whenever
   one is missing or ends within 30 days; after any rewrite, recreate the stack, because each server
   reads its certificate at start.
2. **Rebuild the api image and recreate the stack:**
   `cd Iverson.Server && docker compose build iverson-api && docker compose up -d --force-recreate`.
   `iverson-api` and `iverson-worker` run the one `iverson-api` image, which `up` does not rebuild
   once it exists. With `main`'s build, the worker's `/health` fails once `starrocks-init` revokes
   `OPERATE ON SYSTEM`, and the api waits for a healthy worker.
3. **Unset `IVERSON_ACTING_USER_HOST_HEADER`** if you exported `authentik-server:9000` for compose.
   Through the tls-proxy that Host yields the issuer `https://authentik-server:9000/`, which the API
   rejects with a bare 401. Compose clients need no Host override: the API accepts
   `https://localhost:9443/`.
4. **Trust the CA on the host.** Each runtime reads its own setting:

   | Client | Setting |
   |---|---|
   | .NET and Go (LoadTest, the conformance harness, the .NET and Go drivers) | `SSL_CERT_FILE` |
   | Python's urllib (the mint script, `stack.py`, `ingest.py`, token requests) | `SSL_CERT_FILE` |
   | Python's grpcio (`pattern_leg.py`, the Python driver, the agent) | `GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH` |
   | Node (the TypeScript driver) | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` |
   | Java (the Java driver) | a PKCS12 truststore in `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore` (a PEM file is not accepted) |
   | The console in a browser | the browser's or the operating system's certificate store |
   | Prometheus (inside compose) | `tls_config.ca_file`; compose mounts the CA |

   `SSL_CERT_FILE` replaces the default roots, so a process that also reaches public endpoints
   (`dotnet run` restoring packages, `go build` fetching modules, the agent's Anthropic client) needs a
   bundle of the system roots plus the compose CA. From the repository root:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.cache/iverson
   cat /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls/ca.crt > ~/.cache/iverson/compose-ca-bundle.pem
   export SSL_CERT_FILE=~/.cache/iverson/compose-ca-bundle.pem
   export GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH="$PWD/Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls/ca.crt"
   export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="$PWD/Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls/ca.crt"
   cp "$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v java)")")")/lib/security/cacerts" ~/.cache/iverson/compose-truststore.p12
   keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias iverson-compose-ca -file Iverson.Server/deploy/compose-tls/ca.crt \
     -keystore ~/.cache/iverson/compose-truststore.p12 -storepass changeit
   export JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=$HOME/.cache/iverson/compose-truststore.p12 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit"
   ```

   `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` is the Debian and Ubuntu bundle; other distributions name theirs
   differently. Repeat the bundle, the truststore and the browser import after the script rewrites the CA.
5. **Host addresses.** Dial `localhost`, not `127.0.0.1`: only Kestrel's certificate names an IP.

   | Service | From the host |
   |---|---|
   | API, gRPC | `https://localhost:8080` |
   | API, admin, health and traces | `https://localhost:8081` |
   | API, `/metrics` and `/build` | `https://localhost:8082` |
   | Authentik (login, admin interface, token endpoint) | `https://localhost:9443`; issuer `https://localhost:9443/`, token endpoint `https://localhost:9443/application/o/token/` |
   | Postgres | `localhost:5432`; TLS offered and plaintext still accepted; `sslmode=verify-full` needs the host `localhost` |
   | StarRocks FE | `localhost:9030`; TLS offered, not forced |
   | Qdrant | `https://localhost:6333` (REST), `localhost:6334` (gRPC over TLS) |

## 5. The first deploy on a cloud

Cloud profiles were verified by render and static checks only. Run these at the first deploy; each
mismatch fails closed (a refused command, a FailedCreate event, or an edge 503), not open.

- **The operators group reaches the API server.** As an operator principal:

  ```bash
  kubectl auth whoami          # Groups lists a group named in admission.operatorGroups
  kubectl auth can-i create pods --subresource=exec -n <ns>
  kubectl auth can-i create pods --subresource=portforward -n <ns>
  kubectl auth can-i create serviceaccounts --subresource=token -n <ns>
  kubectl auth can-i create validatingadmissionpolicies.admissionregistration.k8s.io
  kubectl auth can-i create validatingadmissionpolicybindings.admissionregistration.k8s.io
  kubectl auth can-i create clusterroles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kubectl auth can-i create clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  ```

  Every `can-i` answers `yes`. The last four are what the protected `helm upgrade` writes. On GKE these
  rights come from project IAM, outside Terraform; on AKS the admin group is bound to cluster-admin
  through `azure_rbac_enabled`.
- **The controllers reach the API server under their usual names.** After the install,
  `kubectl -n <ns> get events -o custom-columns=REASON:.reason,OBJECT:.involvedObject.name,MESSAGE:.message | command grep sensitive-identities`
  prints nothing. A line there means a controller's username differs from kind's: the replicaset, job,
  statefulset and cronjob controllers record the refusal as `FailedCreate`, the deployment controller as
  `ReplicaSetCreateError`, and every refusal message names the policy `<release>-<namespace>-sensitive-identities`.
- **AWS: the EBS CSI driver add-on version, before the first `terraform apply`.** AWS publishes no
  version table for this add-on, so the pin in `Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/modules/cluster-aws/main.tf`
  (`aws_eks_addon.ebs_csi`, `v1.66.1-eksbuild.1`) follows the upstream release. Check it against the
  versions AWS offers for Kubernetes 1.35:

  ```bash
  aws eks describe-addon-versions --addon-name aws-ebs-csi-driver --kubernetes-version 1.35 \
    --query 'addons[0].addonVersions[].addonVersion' --output text
  ```

  If the pin is not listed, set `addon_version` to the newest listed version before applying; a wrong
  string fails the apply at the add-on.
- **AWS: the cluster is not replaced.** A second `terraform plan` in `Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/aws`
  after the first apply shows no change to `aws_eks_cluster.this`. Its bootstrap flag forces
  replacement, so any diff there plans a new cluster; do not apply it.
- **GKE: the service-account issuer.** Terraform computes it from the project, location and cluster
  name, a format Google does not document: run the comparison in `csr11-identity-plane.md` §7. Until
  `authentik.serviceAccountIssuer` matches what the cluster publishes, both workload-token pins refuse
  every exchange.
- **GKE: the main host's two certificates.** The Gateway's `main` listener names both
  `api.ingress.tlsSecretName` and `adminUi.ingress.tlsSecretName` for the one host; that GKE accepts two
  certificates there is unverified. If `kubectl -n <ns> describe gateway <release>-edge` shows the
  `main` listener without both `Programmed=True` and `ResolvedRefs=True`, or the host serves no certificate, set `adminUi.ingress.tlsSecretName:
  ""` in `values-gcp.yaml` (the listener then carries the api's certificate alone, for the same host)
  and upgrade.
- **GKE: gRPC-Web through the Gateway.** The class's documentation does not mention it, and the console
  reaches the api over REST, so call a gRPC-Web method directly. Sign in to the console as an operator,
  copy the access token from the browser (the `Authorization: Bearer …` header of any `/admin/console/`
  request in the developer tools' network panel), and send an empty `ListTenants` call through the
  Gateway:

  ```bash
  TOKEN='<the copied access token>'
  printf '\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00' > /tmp/empty.grpcweb
  curl -s -D - -o /tmp/listtenants.out -X POST "https://<ingressHost>/iverson.TenantLifecycleGrpcService/ListTenants" \
    -H 'content-type: application/grpc-web+proto' -H 'x-grpc-web: 1' -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data-binary @/tmp/empty.grpcweb
  command grep -a -o 'grpc-status: *[0-9]*' /tmp/listtenants.out
  ```

  The headers show status 200 and `content-type: application/grpc-web`, and the last line prints
  `grpc-status: 0`. A 4xx or 5xx from the load balancer, or no `grpc-status`, means the Gateway does not
  carry gRPC-Web.
- **Every edge answers.** The api, Authentik and the console must not answer 503 at the edge. A 503 means
  the load balancer's source address falls outside the PERMISSIVE ports' `ipBlocks` rule
  (`clusterCidrs`, plus `nodeSubnetFallback` where set).
- **AKS: the node-subnet fallback.** If the api, admin-ui or Authentik pods stay unready on probe
  timeouts, or the edge answers 503, because Azure NPM does not exempt node traffic, set the node subnet
  as a fallback peer in `values-azure.yaml` and upgrade:

  ```yaml
  networkPolicy:
    nodeSubnetFallback: ["10.1.0.0/20"]
    keepFallbacks: true
  ```

  The value renders only with `keepFallbacks: true`, which records that the profile keeps a fallback
  (`csr10-infrastructure-cutover.md` §4).
- **EKS: security groups for pods.** None are enabled today. If they ever are, run the VPC CNI with
  `POD_SECURITY_GROUP_ENFORCING_MODE=standard`, set through the `vpc-cni` add-on's
  `configuration_values` in `Iverson.Server/deploy/terraform/modules/cluster-aws/main.tf` (its `env`
  map): in strict mode the CNI drops the link-local kubelet probes the mesh relies on.
- **Istio ambient on AKS and GKE** has no vendor support statement. Check that every pod in
  `istio-system` is Ready and run `mesh-check.sh` against the cluster.
````

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

# CSR round 12 (docs/specs/2026-10-19-csr-round12-platform-design.md §2.5, §2.7 and §6): live probes
# of Authentik's public listener (:9080, reached through the edge) and its in-cluster route (:9000,
# reached through kubectl port-forward) on a running release.
#
#   A1  the public listener refuses a superuser at login, before any password is asked;
#   A2  the in-cluster route takes the same login on to the password stage;
#   A3  the public listener refuses a superuser's recovery link;
#   A4  the in-cluster route opens the same kind of link at its first prompt;
#   A5  the public listener forwards the allowed flow slugs and answers 404 for the refused ones,
#       initial-setup and /if/user/ among them;
#   A6  the public listener redirects / to the console;
#   A7  on the in-cluster route, /setup and the initial-setup executor show no prompt;
#   A8  a failed login through the public listener is recorded under the client address the edge
#       reported (the X-Forwarded-For entry the tls-proxy selects), not a loopback address;
#   A9  a failed login through a port-forward is recorded under ::ffff:127.0.0.1.
#
# Run it as the operators group: it execs into the Authentik worker and port-forwards to Authentik
# (docs/runbooks/csr11-identity-plane.md). It creates and removes its own short-lived material: a
# recovery link for iverson-breakglass (minting one replaces any link outstanding for that account),
# an API token of that account that expires after 10 minutes, and the reputation rows its two failed
# logins create, which that token reads and deletes. The two failed logins use fresh identifiers that
# name no account. It prints outcomes only, never a token, a link or a password.
#
# Usage: authentik-probes.sh [--release NAME] [--namespace NS]   (both default to iverson)
# Environment (the defaults fit the kind profile):
#   OPERATOR_AS  kubectl impersonation flags that add the operators group (default:
#                --as=kubernetes-admin --as-group=kubeadm:cluster-admins --as-group=iverson-operators)
#   EDGE_BASE    the edge as this host reaches it (default http://127.0.0.1:8080)
#   EDGE_HOST    Authentik's public host name on the edge (default authentik.iverson.local)
#   CONSOLE_URL  where the public listener's / must redirect (default http://iverson.local/admin/)
#   EDGE_HOPS    the release's global.trustedProxies.hops (default 1)
# Exit status: 0 when every check passes, 1 when any fails, 2 on a usage error.

OPERATOR_AS=${OPERATOR_AS:---as=kubernetes-admin --as-group=kubeadm:cluster-admins --as-group=iverson-operators}
EDGE_BASE=${EDGE_BASE:-http://127.0.0.1:8080}
EDGE_HOST=${EDGE_HOST:-authentik.iverson.local}
CONSOLE_URL=${CONSOLE_URL:-http://iverson.local/admin/}
EDGE_HOPS=${EDGE_HOPS:-1}
RELEASE=iverson
NS=iverson
PASSED=0
FAILED=0

usage() { echo "usage: ${0##*/} [--release NAME] [--namespace NS]" >&2; }

report() {  # <PASS|FAIL> <id> <text>
  if [ "$1" = PASS ]; then PASSED=$((PASSED + 1)); else FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); fi
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3"
}

result() {  # <id> <exit status of the check> <text>
  if [ "$2" -eq 0 ]; then report PASS "$1" "$3"; else report FAIL "$1" "$3"; fi
}

# The client address the edge reported: the X-Forwarded-For entry <hops> positions from the right,
# which the tls-proxy forwards to Authentik when the edge is one of global.trustedProxies.
edge_client_from_xff() {  # <X-Forwarded-For value> <hops>
  local IFS=, entries=() i
  read -r -a entries <<< "$1"
  i=$(( ${#entries[@]} - $2 ))
  [ "${#entries[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$i" -ge 0 ] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "${entries[$i]// /}"
}

# The X-Forwarded-For field (the last quoted field of nginx's "main" log format) of the last
# access-log line on stdin that carries <marker>, which the probe sends as its User-Agent.
xff_for_marker() {  # <marker>
  command grep -F -- "$1" | tail -n 1 | sed -n 's/.*"\([^"]*\)"$/\1/p'
}

# Authentik stores an address taken from a trusted X-Forwarded-For as sent, and an untrusted IPv4
# peer of its [::]:9000 listener in IPv4-mapped form.
ip_is() { [ "$1" = "$2" ] || [ "$1" = "::ffff:$2" ]; }

is_loopback() {
  case "$1" in
    127.*|::1|::ffff:127.*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

# A6: the redirect target names the console, with or without a trailing slash.
is_console() { [ -n "$1" ] && [ "${1%/}" = "${CONSOLE_URL%/}" ]; }

# A7: /setup shows no prompt when it fails (500, the denied initial-setup flow on a fresh install) or
# redirects anywhere but the initial-setup flow (an install whose setup is already done).
setup_shows_no_prompt() {  # <status> <location>
  [ "$1" = 500 ] || { [ "$1" = 302 ] && [[ "$2" != *initial-setup* ]]; }
}

# Drives /api/v3/flows/executor/<slug>/ the way the browser does, with one cookie jar, and prints the
# final challenge's component and error message. Each step is ident:<uid> or password:<value> and is
# submitted only while the flow shows that stage.
FLOW_PY='
import http.cookiejar, json, sys, urllib.error, urllib.parse, urllib.request
base, host, slug, query, agent = sys.argv[1:6]
class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return None
opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect(), urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(http.cookiejar.CookieJar()))
url = f"{base}/api/v3/flows/executor/{slug}/?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": query})
def call(method, body=None):
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": agent}
    if host != "-":
        headers["Host"] = host
    data = None
    if body is not None:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        response = opener.open(urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method), timeout=30)
        return response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read()
def challenge():
    status, raw = call("GET")
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return {"component": f"http-{status}"}
stage = {"ident": ("ak-stage-identification", "uid_field"), "password": ("ak-stage-password", "password")}
current = challenge()
for step in sys.argv[6:]:
    kind, _, value = step.partition(":")
    component, field = stage[kind]
    if current.get("component") != component:
        break
    call("POST", {"component": component, field: value})
    current = challenge()
print(current.get("component", ""), (current.get("error_message") or "").replace("\n", " "), sep="\t")
'
flow() { python3 -c "$FLOW_PY" "$@"; }

# Lists or deletes the reputation rows of one identifier through the API, with the token in
# PROBE_API_TOKEN. Prints the rows' addresses, or how many rows it deleted.
REPUTATION_PY='
import json, os, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
base, action, identifier = sys.argv[1:4]
def call(method, path):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, method=method, headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["PROBE_API_TOKEN"], "Accept": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
        body = response.read()
        return json.loads(body) if body else None
rows = call("GET", "/api/v3/policies/reputation/scores/?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"identifier": identifier}))["results"]
if action == "ips":
    print(" ".join(sorted(row["ip"] for row in rows)))
else:
    for row in rows:
        call("DELETE", "/api/v3/policies/reputation/scores/" + str(row["pk"]) + "/")
    print(len(rows))
'

http_status() {  # <base> <Host header or -> <path>: prints "<status> <Location>"
  local host=()
  [ "$2" != - ] && host=(-H "Host: $2")
  curl -s -o /dev/null -m 30 "${host[@]}" -w '%{http_code} %header{location}' "$1$3"
}

ak_shell() {  # <python>: runs it in the Authentik worker as the operators group
  kubectl "${OPS[@]}" -n "$NS" exec "deploy/$RELEASE-authentik-worker" -c worker -- ak shell -c "$1" 2>/dev/null
}

RECOVERY_LINK_PY='
from django.test import RequestFactory
from rest_framework.request import Request
from authentik.brands.utils import get_brand_for_request
from authentik.core.api.users import UserViewSet
from authentik.core.models import User
req = RequestFactory().get("/", HTTP_HOST="localhost:9000")
req.brand = get_brand_for_request(req)
view = UserViewSet()
view.request = Request(req)
view.get_object = lambda: User.objects.get(username="iverson-breakglass")
link, _ = view._create_recovery_link("minutes=5")
print("PROBE-LINK " + link)
'

recovery_link_query() {  # prints flow_token=<key> of a fresh link for iverson-breakglass
  ak_shell "$RECOVERY_LINK_PY" | sed -n 's/^PROBE-LINK .*[?&]\(flow_token=[^&]*\).*/\1/p' | tail -n 1
}

start_port_forward() {  # forwards a free local port to svc/<release>-authentik:9000; sets PF_PID, PF_PORT
  kubectl "${OPS[@]}" -n "$NS" port-forward "svc/$RELEASE-authentik" :9000 > "$WORK/port-forward.log" 2>&1 &
  PF_PID=$!
  local _
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
    PF_PORT=$(sed -nE 's/^Forwarding from 127\.0\.0\.1:([0-9]+) .*/\1/p' "$WORK/port-forward.log" | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$PF_PORT" ] && return 0
    kill -0 "$PF_PID" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    sleep 1
  done
  return 1
}

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "${PROBE_API_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -n "${PF_PORT:-}" ]; then
    local id
    for id in "${IDENTIFIERS[@]}"; do
      python3 -c "$REPUTATION_PY" "http://127.0.0.1:$PF_PORT" delete "$id" > /dev/null 2>&1
    done
  fi
  ak_shell "
from authentik.core.models import Token, User
from authentik.flows.models import FlowToken
Token.objects.filter(identifier='$TOKEN_ID').delete()
FlowToken.objects.filter(identifier=User.objects.get(username='iverson-breakglass').uid + '-password-reset').delete()
" > /dev/null
  [ -n "${PF_PID:-}" ] && kill "$PF_PID" 2>/dev/null
  rm -rf "$WORK"
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" != "$0" ]]; then
  return 0
fi

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --release) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { usage; exit 2; }; RELEASE=$2; shift 2 ;;
    --namespace) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { usage; exit 2; }; NS=$2; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) usage; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

read -r -a OPS <<< "$OPERATOR_AS"
NONCE=$(od -An -N4 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')
WORK=$(mktemp -d)
TOKEN_ID="authentik-probes-$NONCE"
AGENT="authentik-probes/$NONCE"
IDENTIFIERS=("probe-edge-$NONCE" "probe-forward-$NONCE")
PF_PID=""
PF_PORT=""
PROBE_API_TOKEN=""
trap cleanup EXIT

if ! start_port_forward; then
  echo "cannot port-forward to svc/$RELEASE-authentik as the operators group:" >&2
  head -n 3 "$WORK/port-forward.log" >&2
  exit 1
fi
IN="http://127.0.0.1:$PF_PORT"
PROBE_API_TOKEN=$(ak_shell "
from datetime import timedelta
from django.utils.timezone import now
from authentik.core.models import Token, TokenIntents, User
token = Token.objects.create(identifier='$TOKEN_ID', user=User.objects.get(username='iverson-breakglass'),
    intent=TokenIntents.INTENT_API, expiring=True, expires=now() + timedelta(minutes=10),
    description='authentik-probes.sh; deleted when the probe exits')
print('PROBE-TOKEN ' + token.key)
" | sed -n 's/^PROBE-TOKEN //p' | tail -n 1)
export PROBE_API_TOKEN
if [ -z "$PROBE_API_TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "cannot create the probe's API token through ak shell in deploy/$RELEASE-authentik-worker" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A1, A2: a superuser at login.
out=$(flow "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" default-authentication-flow "" "$AGENT" ident:iverson-breakglass)
[ "${out%%$'\t'*}" = ak-stage-access-denied ]; result A1 $? "public listener, superuser login: ${out//$'\t'/ - }"
out=$(flow "$IN" - default-authentication-flow "" "$AGENT" ident:iverson-breakglass)
[ "${out%%$'\t'*}" = ak-stage-password ]; result A2 $? "in-cluster route, superuser login: ${out%%$'\t'*}"

# A3, A4: a superuser's recovery link. A link is spent when it is opened, so each route gets its own.
query=$(recovery_link_query)
out=$(flow "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" iverson-recovery "$query" "$AGENT")
[ -n "$query" ] && [ "${out%%$'\t'*}" = ak-stage-access-denied ]
result A3 $? "public listener, superuser recovery link: ${out//$'\t'/ - }"
query=$(recovery_link_query)
out=$(flow "$IN" - iverson-recovery "$query" "$AGENT")
[ -n "$query" ] && [ "${out%%$'\t'*}" = ak-stage-prompt ]
result A4 $? "in-cluster route, superuser recovery link: ${out%%$'\t'*}"

# A5: the public listener's flow allow-list.
allowed=(default-authentication-flow iverson-recovery default-provider-authorization-implicit-consent
         default-invalidation-flow default-provider-invalidation-flow)
refused=(initial-setup default-provider-authorization-explicit-consent default-user-settings-flow
         default-password-change default-authenticator-totp-setup default-source-authentication
         default-source-enrollment)
bad=""
for slug in "${allowed[@]}"; do
  for path in "/if/flow/$slug/" "/api/v3/flows/executor/$slug/"; do
    s=$(http_status "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" "$path"); s=${s%% *}
    case "$s" in 404|000|5*) bad="$bad $path=$s" ;; esac
  done
done
for slug in "${refused[@]}"; do
  for path in "/if/flow/$slug/" "/api/v3/flows/executor/$slug/"; do
    s=$(http_status "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" "$path"); s=${s%% *}
    [ "$s" = 404 ] || bad="$bad $path=$s"
  done
done
for path in /if/user/ /if/admin/ /api/v3/core/users/me/ /setup; do
  s=$(http_status "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" "$path"); s=${s%% *}
  [ "$s" = 404 ] || bad="$bad $path=$s"
done
[ -z "$bad" ]
result A5 $? "public listener allow-list (allowed slugs forwarded; initial-setup, /if/user/ and the rest 404)${bad:+, unexpected:$bad}"

# A6: / redirects to the console.
s=$(http_status "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" /)
[ "${s%% *}" = 302 ] && is_console "${s#* }"; result A6 $? "public listener /: $s"

# A7: no setup prompt on the in-cluster route.
s=$(http_status "$IN" - /setup)
out=$(flow "$IN" - initial-setup "" "$AGENT")
setup_shows_no_prompt "${s%% *}" "${s#* }" && [ "${out%%$'\t'*}" != ak-stage-prompt ]
result A7 $? "in-cluster route, /setup: $s; initial-setup executor: ${out%%$'\t'*}"

# A8: a failed login through the public listener.
flow "$EDGE_BASE" "$EDGE_HOST" default-authentication-flow "" "$AGENT" \
  "ident:${IDENTIFIERS[0]}" "password:wrong-$NONCE" > /dev/null
xff=$(kubectl -n "$NS" logs -l "app=$RELEASE-authentik-server" -c tls-proxy --tail=-1 --since=10m 2>/dev/null \
  | xff_for_marker "$AGENT")
edge=$(edge_client_from_xff "$xff" "$EDGE_HOPS")
ip=$(python3 -c "$REPUTATION_PY" "$IN" ips "${IDENTIFIERS[0]}")
[ -n "$edge" ] && ip_is "$ip" "$edge" && ! is_loopback "$ip"
result A8 $? "failed login on the public listener recorded as '$ip'; the edge reported '${edge:-none}' (X-Forwarded-For '$xff')"

# A9: a failed login through the port-forward.
flow "$IN" - default-authentication-flow "" "$AGENT" "ident:${IDENTIFIERS[1]}" "password:wrong-$NONCE" > /dev/null
ip=$(python3 -c "$REPUTATION_PY" "$IN" ips "${IDENTIFIERS[1]}")
[ "$ip" = ::ffff:127.0.0.1 ]; result A9 $? "failed login through a port-forward recorded as '$ip'"

echo "${0##*/}: $PASSED passed, $FAILED failed"
[ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]
```
